title: applyThemeBootstrap(plan, options?): ThemeBootstrapApplied | null
text: applyThemeBootstrap(plan, options?): ThemeBootstrapApplied | null Apply a ThemeBootstrapPlan to the document before first paint. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `plan` | `ThemeBootstrapPlan` | The plan built by `buildBootstrapPlan`. | | `options` | `ApplyThemeBootstrapOptions` (optional) | Storage/document/window overrides, for tests and SSR shells. | **Returns** `ThemeBootstrapApplied | null` — The state written, or `null` when there is no document to patch. This is the browser-side half of the static `boot.js` asset. It performs the same writes as the generated inline script: the `.dark` class, `color-scheme`, the canonical `data-theme*` attributes, the resolved CSS variables, and the `window.__THEMVORA_BOOTSTRAP__` handoff payload. It is idempotent. Running it twice, or running it after the Vite plugin's inline script has already painted, leaves the first result untouched — the same rule that makes an accidental plugin-plus-manual setup harmless rather than a second, conflicting initialization. ---

title: auditActionProminence(theme): ActionProminence
text: auditActionProminence(theme): ActionProminence Measure whether a theme's action fill reads as a control.

title: Why this is a third contract, not a fourth context
text: Why this is a third contract, not a fourth context 1. **semantic pair** — `primary` against `primaryForeground` must be readable. 2. **context** — where each role may be used, and with whose judgement. 3. **prominence** — a *generated* fill must separate from the canvas, because a fill that does not has stopped reading as a control. It cannot be expressed as "`primary` must clear X:1 against `background`" globally, because that would condemn every dark brand anchor. Hence the `anchored` flag: the invariant binds generated fills and merely reports anchored ones — Slack's aubergine is 1.42:1 against the dark canvas, and that is the brand being the brand. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `theme` | `ThemeDefinition` | The theme to measure. | **Returns** `ActionProminence` — The measurement, with `anchored` telling the caller which rule applies. ---

title: auditSemanticContexts(theme): ContextResult[]
text: auditSemanticContexts(theme): ContextResult[] Evaluate every declared context against a theme. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `theme` | `ThemeDefinition` | The theme to check. | **Returns** `ContextResult[]` — One result per context, in declaration order. ---

title: auto(tokenName, lookup): string
text: auto(tokenName, lookup): string Resolve an `auto()` foreground token by deriving its value from a base color token. Given a token name ending in `Foreground`/`foreground` (or `Fg`), the base token is looked up via the provided resolver and its contrast foreground is returned. When the base color cannot be resolved, `#000000` is returned. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `tokenName` | `string` | The foreground token name to derive (e.g. `"primaryForeground"`). | | `lookup` | `__type(path: string): string \| undefined` | A resolver that maps a dot-path token key to its value. | **Returns** `string` — A black or white foreground color string. ---

title: buildThemeCssMap<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(themes, options?): Record<string, Record<string, string>>
text: buildThemeCssMap<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(themes, options?): Record<string, Record<string, string>> Build a lookup map of theme keys to flat CSS variables. Each theme is registered twice: - under its own `name` (e.g. `"sunrise-light"`) - under a `family:mode` key (e.g. `"sunrise:light"`) so that a persisted family + effective mode can be resolved without knowing theme names. **See also:** `createThemeBootstrapScript` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `themes` | `readonly T[]` | — | | `options` | `BuildThemeCssMapOptions` (optional) | — | **Returns** `Record<string, Record<string, string>>` ---

title: calculateSunTimes(date, args...): SunTimes
text: calculateSunTimes(date, args...): SunTimes Compute today's sunrise and sunset using the standard NOAA solar algorithm (zenith-based, corrected for the equation of time and for longitude). `latitude` and `longitude` are optional: when omitted (or when an options object is passed instead), the location is resolved from `timeZone` or the visitor's browser timezone via `resolveSolarLocation`. Passing neither coordinates nor a timezone means every visitor gets sunrise/sunset for their own location automatically. ```ts // Explicit coordinates (unchanged behavior). calculateSunTimes(date, 48.8566, 2.3522); // Resolve from the visitor's timezone. calculateSunTimes(date); // Resolve from an explicit timezone. calculateSunTimes(date, { timeZone: "Asia/Kathmandu" }); ``` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `date` | `Date` | The day to compute for. Its **local** calendar date is used. | | ...args | `[latitude: number, longitude: number, options: SolarLocationInput] \| [options: SolarLocationInput]` | `latitude, longitude[, options]`, or an options bag. | **Returns** `SunTimes` — The sunrise/sunset pair as absolute instants (see SunTimes). **The local-clock contract.** Both returned `Date`s are absolute instants computed from the location's longitude and the day's solar declination. Their local representation is therefore the correct wall-clock time for that day, and it follows daylight-saving transitions because it is derived from the real UTC instant rather than from a fixed offset. **Longitude matters.** Solar noon at a location occurs at `720 - 4·longitude - eqTime` minutes UTC (east-positive longitude), and sunrise/sunset sit `±4·hourAngle` minutes either side of it. Treating that result as local clock time — which the previous implementation did, because it never applied the longitude term — put the switch at the wrong hour wherever the local time-zone meridian differs from the location's longitude. **`timeZone` resolves coordinates, not the clock.** It is used only to pick the latitude/longitude pair; the returned instants are read on the host's own clock. This API therefore does not support computing "sunrise in Tokyo" on a server in London: the coordinates would be Tokyo's but the day boundary and the displayed wall-clock time would be the server's. Pass explicit coordinates for the visitor's location, or run the calculation in the visitor's browser. **Polar day and polar night** are reported through SunTimes.polar. The hour-angle formula has no solution when the sun stays above or below the horizon, and the previous implementation clamped `cosH` into `[-1, 1]`, which produced a zero-length day: sunrise equal to sunset, so the daytime test was never true and a polar-day visitor got the dark theme at noon. ---

title: cancelThemeAnimation(target): void
text: cancelThemeAnimation(target): void Abort any in-flight theme animation for `target` and remove its styles. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `target` | `HTMLElement` | — | **Returns** `void` ---

title: chooseForeground(role, background, ctx): Oklch
text: chooseForeground(role, background, ctx): Oklch Choose the foreground for a role on a surface. ``` if the preferred ink meets the target: use it else if the other ink meets it: use that else: use the better of the two, and let the solver repair it ```

title: Why the target, and not the floor
text: Why the target, and not the floor The internal target (4.75) is used here rather than the published floor (4.5), because that is what makes the preference *free*: whenever the preferred ink clears 4.75 it is also the higher-ratio ink, so honouring the preference and maximising contrast agree. The two rules only diverge in the narrow band where white measures 4.50–4.58, and there the fallback takes the higher ratio. This is why the change is a refactor rather than a behaviour change for existing themes — see the note in `theme-generation.md`. What it buys is that the rule is now **explicit, per-role and testable**, instead of being an emergent property of a `>=` comparison inside `bestInk`. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `role` | `CoreColor` | The foreground role being generated. | | `background` | `Oklch` | The surface it will sit on. | | `ctx` | `PaletteContext` | The generation context. | **Returns** `Oklch` — The chosen ink. ---

title: clearMigrations(): void
text: clearMigrations(): void Remove all registered migration steps, resetting the migration system to an empty state. **Returns** `void` ---

title: colorName(hex): string | null
text: colorName(hex): string | null A short, readable name for a colour, chosen by its hue and tone. Intended for naming a generated theme family after its seed: the result is lowercase letters only — no separators, no digits — so it survives being used as an identifier stem (`indigoLight`) and reads as a name in a UI. Names are `hue` on its own (`indigo`) or a camelCase tone plus hue (`deepIndigo`, `paleAmber`). A seed with almost no chroma has no meaningful hue, so it is named for its tone instead (`ash`, `slate`). | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `hex` | `string` | A hex colour string. | **Returns** `string | null` — The name, or `null` when the string is not a valid colour. ```ts colorName("#6366f1"); // "indigo" colorName("#0b0b0f"); // "slate" colorName("not a colour"); // null ``` ---

title: composeTheme<TName extends string>(name, sources...): ThemeDefinition<TName>
text: composeTheme<TName extends string>(name, sources...): ThemeDefinition<TName> Compose a theme by layering multiple sources (e.g. a family theme, a mode override, and local tokens), later sources winning. **See also:** `mergeThemeDefinitions`, `defineTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `name` | `TName` | — | | ...sources | `ThemeDefinition<string>[]` | — | **Returns** `ThemeDefinition<TName>` ---

title: computeFingerprint(themes, defaultTheme?): string
text: computeFingerprint(themes, defaultTheme?): string Fingerprints a theme registry so a persisted selection from an older build — different themes, or a different `defaultTheme` — is ignored rather than applied against themes it was never valid for. **See also:** `ThemeBootstrapCookieSource`, `buildBootstrapPlan` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `themes` | `readonly ThemeDefinition<string>[]` | The theme registry to fingerprint. | | `defaultTheme` | `string` (optional) | The fallback theme name. Included in the fingerprint, so changing it invalidates previously persisted selections. | **Returns** `string` — A stable fingerprint string, or `""` when `themes` is empty. The result is written to the `theme-fingerprint` cookie and compared on the next request, so it is part of the **stable cookie contract** documented in `VERSIONING.md` — changing the format invalidates every visitor's persisted selection on their next visit. It lives here, in core, because four SSR integrations (Next, Nuxt, Astro, Remix) previously each carried a byte-identical private copy. Any edit to one of them would have silently broken cross-framework persistence with nothing to catch it. ---

title: contextFailures(theme): { advisory: ContextResult[]; required: ContextResult[] }
text: contextFailures(theme): { advisory: ContextResult[]; required: ContextResult[] } The contexts a theme fails, split by whether the generator promised them. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `theme` | `ThemeDefinition` | The theme to check. | **Returns** `{ advisory: ContextResult[]; required: ContextResult[] }` — `required` failures are bugs; `advisory` failures are declared gaps. ---

title: contrast(background): string
text: contrast(background): string Compute a readable foreground color for a given background color. Returns `#000000` when the background is light enough (relative luminance above `0.179`), otherwise `#ffffff`. Accepts a hex color with or without the leading `#`; non-hex input falls back to `#000000`. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `background` | `string` | The background color to contrast against. | **Returns** `string` — A black or white foreground color string. ---

title: createAccessibilityPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T>
text: createAccessibilityPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T> Creates a plugin that validates theme contrast for accessibility. The plugin runs a WCAG contrast check on the active theme after every theme change and reports any violations that fail AA normal contrast, either by emitting a `TV_A11Y_CONTRAST_VIOLATION` diagnostic or by invoking the `onViolation` callback. **See also:** `AccessibilityPluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `AccessibilityPluginOptions` (optional) | Accessibility configuration. | **Returns** `ThemePlugin<T>` — An `"accessibility"` theme plugin. Violations are reported only when the theme fails AA normal contrast and at least one check fails. `warnOnly` chooses the diagnostic's level. The failing checks travel as the diagnostic's structured context, so they stay available to the console and to any consumer of the diagnostics stream rather than being flattened into the message. ```ts const manager = createPluginManager(); manager.use(createAccessibilityPlugin({ warnOnly: true, onViolation: ({ themeName, checks }) => report(themeName, checks), })); ``` ---

title: createAdapterRegistry<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(runtime): AdapterRegistry<T>
text: createAdapterRegistry<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(runtime): AdapterRegistry<T> Create the runtime-owned adapter registry for a theme runtime. Registering an adapter installs it; the registry tracks reference counts so composition (React Strict Mode, Svelte lifecycles, nested providers) is deterministic. `use` is idempotent per adapter instance and returns an `AdapterRegistration` whose `dispose()` uninstalls exactly that instance when its own reference count drops to zero. Registering a different adapter instance under an already-used id replaces the previous one. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `runtime` | `ThemeRuntime<T>` | The theme runtime the adapters are installed into. | **Returns** `AdapterRegistry<T>` — The adapter registry bound to `runtime`. ```ts const registry = createAdapterRegistry(runtime); const handle = registry.use(adapter); // ... later handle.dispose(); ``` ---

title: createAnimationsPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T>
text: createAnimationsPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T> Creates a plugin that animates theme changes with CSS transitions. The plugin applies a CSS transition to the target element before a theme change so the resulting token updates animate smoothly, and removes the transition when the plugin is destroyed. **See also:** `AnimationsPluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `AnimationsPluginOptions` (optional) | Animation configuration. | **Returns** `ThemePlugin<T>` — An `"animations"` theme plugin. The plugin opts out of View Transitions by default; it provides CSS transition properties rather than page-level crossfades. `onDestroy` removes the transition from the target element. ```ts const manager = createPluginManager(); manager.use(createAnimationsPlugin({ transition: { duration: 500 } })); ``` ---

title: createBroadcastPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T>
text: createBroadcastPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T> Creates a plugin that synchronizes the theme selection across browser tabs and windows. The plugin subscribes to incoming selection messages when the runtime is created and applies the received mode/family to the runtime, and broadcasts the selection after every persist. It uses a `BroadcastChannel`-based adapter by default when available. **See also:** `BroadcastPluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `BroadcastPluginOptions` (optional) | Broadcast configuration. | **Returns** `ThemePlugin<T>` — A `"broadcast"` theme plugin. `onDestroy` unsubscribes from incoming messages and closes the default channel. When no adapter is available the plugin is inert. ```ts const manager = createPluginManager(); manager.use(createBroadcastPlugin({ channelName: "my-app-theme" })); ``` ---

title: createCSSVariablesBinding(store, options?): { destroy: void; setTransition: void } | null
text: createCSSVariablesBinding(store, options?): { destroy: void; setTransition: void } | null Create a binding that keeps CSS custom properties (`--theme-*`) on a target element (default `<html>`) in sync with the store. Applies the current theme immediately on creation and diffs updates. **See also:** `themeToCSSVariables`, `CSSVariablesOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `store` | `ThemeStore` | — | | `options` | `CSSVariablesOptions` (optional) | — | **Returns** `{ destroy: void; setTransition: void } | null` ---

title: createDebuggerPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T>
text: createDebuggerPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T> Creates a plugin that logs theme runtime activity to the console. The plugin logs theme changes, active theme tokens, and persistence events (before and after) to the console, gated by the corresponding options. **See also:** `DebuggerPluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `DebuggerPluginOptions` (optional) | Debugger configuration. | **Returns** `ThemePlugin<T>` — A `"debugger"` theme plugin. ```ts const manager = createPluginManager(); manager.use(createDebuggerPlugin({ label: "[my-app]" })); ``` ---

title: createDefaultPersistence(options?): ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter | null
text: createDefaultPersistence(options?): ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter | null Creates the default persistence adapter: a `localStorage`-backed selection adapter under the `"theme-selection"` key. Returns `null` when `window` is unavailable (SSR) or storage access throws. Cross-tab changes are surfaced through the `storage` event. **See also:** `ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter`, `createThemePersistence` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `{ key?: string }` (optional) | — | **Returns** `ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter | null` — A persistence adapter, or `null` when storage is unavailable. ---

title: createDevToolsPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T>
text: createDevToolsPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T> Creates a plugin that exposes the theme runtime to browser devtools. When enabled, the plugin registers a devtools hook on `window` that exposes the current themes, selection, active theme, and history, so a devtools extension can inspect the runtime state. **See also:** `DevToolsPluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `DevToolsPluginOptions` (optional) | Devtools configuration. | **Returns** `ThemePlugin<T>` — A `"devtools"` theme plugin. The hook is only registered in browser environments. `onDestroy` clears the internal runtime reference. Entries are added to the same `window.__THEMVORA_DEVTOOLS__` set that `@themvora/devtools`'s inspector plugin uses, and must satisfy that set's declared shape — `getState()`, `getEntries()`, `getPerformance()`. This plugin records no entries or performance samples, so those two return empty arrays; the point is that a consumer enumerating the set can call all three on every member without a type check. Use `@themvora/devtools`'s `createDevToolsPlugin` instead when you want the recorded entries and timings. ```ts const manager = createPluginManager(); manager.use(createDevToolsPlugin()); ``` ---

title: createDiagnostic(input): ThemeDiagnostic
text: createDiagnostic(input): ThemeDiagnostic Create a ThemeDiagnostic. Pure: no console access, no environment reads, no deduplication. The `docs` link is derived from the code so call sites never repeat it. **See also:** `emitDiagnostic` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `input` | `CreateDiagnosticInput` | The diagnostic fields. | **Returns** `ThemeDiagnostic` — A diagnostic value. Creating one has no side effects. ```ts const diagnostic = createDiagnostic({ code: "TV_MODE_INVALID", level: "warning", message: 'setMode() received an unknown mode "purple".', context: { api: "setMode", property: "mode", received: "purple", expected: "light | dark | system" }, hint: "Pass one of the three valid modes, or omit the call.", }); ``` ---

title: createDOMBinding(store, options?): { apply: type(theme: ThemeDefinition, emitOptions?: { suppressTransition?: boolean }): void; destroy: void; setTransition: void } | null
text: createDOMBinding(store, options?): { apply: type(theme: ThemeDefinition, emitOptions?: { suppressTransition?: boolean }): void; destroy: void; setTransition: void } | null Create a binding that syncs the store theme to the DOM: `data-theme`, `data-theme-mode`, `data-theme-family`, the `dark` class, and the `color-scheme` style — with transition support. **See also:** `DOMBindingOptions`, `createCSSVariablesBinding` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `store` | `ThemeStore` | — | | `options` | `DOMBindingOptions` (optional) | — | **Returns** `{ apply: __type(theme: ThemeDefinition, emitOptions?: { suppressTransition?: boolean }): void; destroy: void; setTransition: void } | null` ---

title: createGenerationPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): GenerationPlugin<T>
text: createGenerationPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): GenerationPlugin<T> Creates a plugin that participates in theme generation. The plugin is inert until GenerationPlugin.generate is called: it registers no tokens of its own and its `transformTokens` hook is the identity. Generating goes through `generateTheme`, so the plugin and the runtime cannot disagree about what a seed produces. **See also:** `GenerationPluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `GenerationPluginOptions` (optional) | Default seed, default generation options, and a hook. | **Returns** `GenerationPlugin<T>` — A `"theme-generation"` plugin with a `generate` method. ```ts const plugin = createGenerationPlugin({ seed: "#6366f1" }); const { light, dark } = plugin.generate({ family: "brand", style: "brand" }); ``` ---

title: createHistoryPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T>
text: createHistoryPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T> Creates a plugin that configures the runtime's theme history. The plugin applies the given history options (notably `maxSteps`) to the runtime's history when the runtime is created. **See also:** `HistoryPluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `HistoryPluginOptions` (optional) | History configuration. | **Returns** `ThemePlugin<T>` — A `"history"` theme plugin. ```ts const manager = createPluginManager(); manager.use(createHistoryPlugin({ maxSteps: 20 })); ``` ---

title: createMultiWindowSync(options?): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter
text: createMultiWindowSync(options?): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter Sync theme selection across browser tabs/windows via BroadcastChannel (with a SharedWorker + storage fallback). | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `MultiWindowSyncOptions` (optional) | — | **Returns** `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter` ---

title: createNoopSync(): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter
text: createNoopSync(): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter Create a no-op theme-selection sync adapter. Every method is a safe no-op: `post` discards the value, `subscribe` returns an unsubscribe that does nothing, and `destroy` does nothing. Used as the final fallback when no cross-tab strategy is available. **Returns** `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter` — A `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter` that performs no synchronization. ---

title: createNuxtThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string
text: createNuxtThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string Generate the blocking, inline bootstrap script that applies the persisted theme before first paint — the same zero-flash guarantee `@themvora/next` ships. The script reads the four theme cookies (same contract as Next), validates the config fingerprint, resolves the theme for the effective mode (`"system"` is resolved against `prefers-color-scheme`), and writes the CSS variables plus DOM effects onto `document.documentElement`. It delegates to the shared `@themvora/core` applier (`buildBootstrapPlan` + `serializeThemeBootstrapScript`), so every SSR integration emits the same correct script and cannot drift from the client runtime contract. Emit it in `<head>` with `tagPriority: "critical"` so it runs before the app stylesheets and the browser paints already themed. **See also:** `NuxtThemeBootstrapOptions`, `resolveThemeFromCookies` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `NuxtThemeBootstrapOptions<T>` | — | **Returns** `string` ---

title: createOverlayScrollbar(store, options?): OverlayScrollbarHandle | null
text: createOverlayScrollbar(store, options?): OverlayScrollbarHandle | null Framework-agnostic, theme-aware scrollbar overlay engine. The browser performs all scrolling — this only renders + animates a visual overlay that tracks it, so inertia, touch, wheel, keyboard and accessibility remain native. Colors come from Themvora tokens, so the overlay re-themes with the rest of the app (no flashes). It tracks the *document* plus every scrollable element on the page by default (anywhere a native scrollbar would appear); the native track is hidden automatically — no manual CSS required. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `store` | `ThemeStore` | — | | `options` | `OverlayScrollbarOptions` (optional) | — | **Returns** `OverlayScrollbarHandle | null` ---

title: createPersistencePlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T>
text: createPersistencePlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemePlugin<T> Creates a plugin that persists the theme selection and restores it on startup. The plugin reads the saved selection when the runtime is created (if `readOnInit` is enabled) and writes the selection to the adapter after every persist. It uses a `localStorage`-backed adapter by default in the browser and is inert in non-browser environments unless a custom adapter is given. **See also:** `PersistencePluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `PersistencePluginOptions` (optional) | Persistence configuration. | **Returns** `ThemePlugin<T>` — A `"persistence"` theme plugin. The default adapter also subscribes to cross-tab `storage` events so the selection stays in sync across tabs. `onDestroy` releases the adapter and runtime references. ```ts const manager = createPluginManager(); manager.use(createPersistencePlugin({ key: "my-app-theme" })); ``` ---

title: createPluginManager<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): PluginManager<T>
text: createPluginManager<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): PluginManager<T> Creates a PluginManager for registering and coordinating theme plugins. The returned manager stores plugins by name, orders them by ascending `priority` (default `10`) for hook dispatch, and coordinates destruction. **See also:** `PluginManager`, `ThemePlugin` **Returns** `PluginManager<T>` — A new, empty plugin manager. Registering a plugin whose name is already present is skipped with a console warning and returns a no-op disposer. `destroy` invokes `onDestroy` on every plugin (in priority order) and clears the registry. `destroy` is failure-isolated: a plugin whose `onDestroy` throws is reported with `TV_PLUGIN_DESTROY_FAILED` and the remaining plugins are still destroyed, so one broken plugin cannot leak the rest. ```ts const manager = createPluginManager<MyTheme>(); const dispose = manager.use(createPersistencePlugin()); manager.list(); // [persistence plugin] dispose(); // removes it ``` ---

title: createPrePaintScrollbarCSS(): string
text: createPrePaintScrollbarCSS(): string The hiding CSS, for SSR output (e.g. Next inlines it as a `<style>` in `<head>`). Use together with the `tv-scrollbar` class on `<html>`. **Returns** `string` ---

title: createPrePaintScrollbarScript(options?): string
text: createPrePaintScrollbarScript(options?): string Generate a blocking `<script>` that hides the native scrollbar before first paint. The script is idempotent — calling it multiple times is safe. On coarse-pointer devices it returns early (unless `touch` is forced), so native scrollbars are kept. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `PrePaintScrollbarOptions` (optional) | — | **Returns** `string` ---

title: createProvidedThemesSource<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(runtime): ProvidedThemesSource<T>
text: createProvidedThemesSource<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(runtime): ProvidedThemesSource<T> Create a reactive source over one provider's theme collection. The derivation runs once per settled change to the provider's registry and is cached in between, so: - the returned array is referentially stable while nothing changes, - a `register` / `unregister` / `use` / `configure` is reflected on the next read, - two providers never share a collection. **See also:** `normalizeProvidedThemes` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `runtime` | `ProvidedThemesRuntime<T>` | The provider's runtime. | **Returns** `ProvidedThemesSource<T>` — A source with `get()` and `subscribe()`. ```ts const source = createProvidedThemesSource(runtime); source.subscribe(() => console.log(source.get().length)); ``` ---

title: createScheduledPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): ThemePlugin<T>
text: createScheduledPlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): ThemePlugin<T> Creates a plugin that switches the theme selection by time of day. The plugin resolves a light/dark theme pair and installs a scheduled theme binding that applies the appropriate theme based on the visitor's local sunrise/sunset times. It re-resolves the pair when the theme family changes so auto-derived themes follow the current selection. **See also:** `ScheduledPluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ScheduledPluginOptions<T>` | Schedule configuration. | **Returns** `ThemePlugin<T>` — A `"scheduled"` theme plugin. When the light/dark pair cannot be resolved, the plugin emits a `TV_SCHEDULE_THEME_UNRESOLVED` diagnostic and does not install a binding. `onDestroy` destroys the binding, unsubscribes from the store, and clears all internal state. ```ts const manager = createPluginManager(); manager.use(createScheduledPlugin({ lightTheme: "day", darkTheme: "night", timeZone: "Asia/Kathmandu", })); ``` ---

title: createScheduledThemeBinding<T>(store, options): { destroy: void; getEnabled: void; getLocation: void; setEnabled: void; setLastSyncTime: void }
text: createScheduledThemeBinding<T>(store, options): { destroy: void; getEnabled: void; getLocation: void; setEnabled: void; setLastSyncTime: void } Create a scheduled theme binding that applies a light theme during daytime and a dark theme at night. The binding resolves a location (explicit coordinates, an explicit `timeZone`, or browser auto-detection), computes sunrise/sunset, applies the matching theme immediately, and re-checks on `checkInterval`. It can be toggled at runtime via `setEnabled` and stopped via `destroy` (which is idempotent and clears the timer). **See also:** `ScheduledThemeBindingOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `store` | `{ get: void; set: void }` | The store the scheduled theme is applied to. | | `options` | `ScheduledThemeBindingOptions<T>` | The scheduled-binding configuration. | **Returns** `{ destroy: void; getEnabled: void; getLocation: void; setEnabled: void; setLastSyncTime: void }` — A controller exposing `destroy`, `setLastSyncTime`, `setEnabled`, `getEnabled` and `getLocation`. ```ts const binding = createScheduledThemeBinding(store, { lightTheme, darkTheme, timeZone: "Asia/Kathmandu", }); // ... later binding.destroy(); ``` ---

title: createScopedThemeBinding<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(themes, target, selection, options?): { destroy: void; getTheme: void; refresh: void; setLocalThemes: void; setTransition: void; update: void }
text: createScopedThemeBinding<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(themes, target, selection, options?): { destroy: void; getTheme: void; refresh: void; setLocalThemes: void; setTransition: void; update: void } Create a scoped-theme binding for an element: applies the scoped theme's CSS variables inline on the element and cleans them up on destroy. **See also:** `ScopedThemeBindingOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `themes` | `readonly T[]` | — | | `target` | `HTMLElement` | — | | `selection` | `ScopedThemeSelection` | — | | `options` | `ScopedThemeBindingOptions` (optional) | — | **Returns** `{ destroy: void; getTheme: void; refresh: void; setLocalThemes: void; setTransition: void; update: void }` ---

title: createSharedWorkerSync(): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter | null
text: createSharedWorkerSync(): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter | null Create a theme-selection broadcast adapter backed by a `SharedWorker`. The adapter relays theme selections between tabs/windows through a shared worker, so every tab connected to the same worker receives the selection. It requires `SharedWorker` support; when unavailable (or when the worker cannot be created) it returns `null` (e.g. during SSR). **See also:** `destroySharedWorkerUrl` **Returns** `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter | null` — A `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter`, or `null` when `SharedWorker` is unavailable. ```ts const sync = createSharedWorkerSync(); sync?.post({ mode: "dark", family: "plum" }); ``` ---

title: createStorageEventSync(key?, view?): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter
text: createStorageEventSync(key?, view?): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter Create a theme-selection sync adapter backed by `localStorage` and the `storage` event. The adapter writes the selection as JSON under a single key and notifies subscribers of cross-tab changes through the `storage` event. It requires a `Window`; when none is available it returns a no-op adapter (e.g. during SSR). **See also:** `createThemeBroadcast`, `MultiWindowSyncOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `key` | `string` (optional) | Storage key used for the selection. | | `view` | `Window` (optional) | The `Window` used to access storage and listen for `storage` events. Defaults to the global `window` when present. | **Returns** `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter` — A `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter`. ```ts const sync = createStorageEventSync(); sync.post({ mode: "dark", family: "plum" }); ``` ---

title: createSyncFirstRoot<TRoot extends SyncFirstRenderRoot>(createRoot, flushSync, options?): CreateRootLike<TRoot>
text: createSyncFirstRoot<TRoot extends SyncFirstRenderRoot>(createRoot, flushSync, options?): CreateRootLike<TRoot> Wraps a React `createRoot` so the **first** `render` call on each root it creates is committed synchronously. **See also:** `themvoraVitePlugin` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `createRoot` | `CreateRootLike<TRoot>` | The real `createRoot` to delegate to. | | `flushSync` | `__type(callback: __type(): void): void` | React's `flushSync`. | | `options` | `SyncFirstRootOptions` (optional) | See SyncFirstRootOptions. | **Returns** `CreateRootLike<TRoot>` — A `createRoot` that commits its first render synchronously. React's concurrent root *schedules* the initial commit, so the browser can paint a frame with the container still empty before React commits — one frame, ~33 ms, visible as the UI blinking on reload. `flushSync` around that first render closes it, and it has to happen at the root: the offending frame is painted before any of the application's React code runs, so no provider, insertion effect or layout effect is in time. Only the **first** `render` of each root is flushed. Every later render keeps React's normal concurrent scheduling, so transitions, Suspense and time-slicing behave exactly as before. This is deliberately a plain function of its dependencies rather than something that reaches for React globals, so it can be unit-tested against stubs — the behaviour it encodes (first render flushed, later renders not) is otherwise only observable in a real browser. ---

title: createSystemThemeBinding<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(store, options): { destroy: void } | null
text: createSystemThemeBinding<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(store, options): { destroy: void } | null Create a binding that applies the theme for "system" mode, following `prefers-color-scheme` live. **See also:** `SystemThemeBindingOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `store` | `ThemeStore<T>` | — | | `options` | `SystemThemeBindingOptions<T>` | — | **Returns** `{ destroy: void } | null` ---

title: createThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string
text: createThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string Generate an inline, blocking script that applies the persisted theme before first paint, preventing a flash of the wrong (or missing) theme on reload. The script reads the saved selection from localStorage, resolves the theme for the effective mode (`"system"` is resolved against `prefers-color-scheme`), and writes the CSS variables plus DOM effects onto `document.documentElement`. **See also:** `buildThemeCssMap`, `createPrePaintScrollbarScript` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeBootstrapScriptOptions<T>` | — | **Returns** `string` ---

title: createThemeBroadcast(options?): ThemeBroadcastAdapter | null
text: createThemeBroadcast(options?): ThemeBroadcastAdapter | null Create a theme-mode broadcast adapter backed by `BroadcastChannel`. The adapter publishes the mode to a channel and notifies subscribers of modes broadcast by other tabs/windows. It requires `BroadcastChannel` support (or a custom `channel`); when neither is available it returns `null` (e.g. during SSR). **See also:** `createStorageEventSync`, `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeBroadcastOptions` (optional) | The broadcast configuration. | **Returns** `ThemeBroadcastAdapter | null` — A `ThemeBroadcastAdapter`, or `null` when no channel is available. ```ts const broadcast = createThemeBroadcast({ channelName: "my-theme-mode" }); broadcast?.post("dark"); ``` ---

title: createThemeDebugger<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(store, options?): ThemeDebugger<T>
text: createThemeDebugger<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(store, options?): ThemeDebugger<T> Create a debugger that records theme changes on a theme store. The debugger subscribes to the store and records an event whenever the current theme changes. Call ThemeDebugger.record before a change to attribute it to a specific source and label; otherwise the change is attributed to `"user"`. History is capped at `maxEvents` entries. **See also:** `ThemeDebugger` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `store` | `ThemeStore<T>` | The theme store to observe. | | `options` | `{ maxEvents?: number }` (optional) | Optional configuration. | **Returns** `ThemeDebugger<T>` — A ThemeDebugger bound to the store. ```ts const debugger = createThemeDebugger(store, { maxEvents: 100 }); debugger.record("user", "switched to dark"); ``` ---

title: createThemeDiff(prev, next, prefix?): ThemeDiff
text: createThemeDiff(prev, next, prefix?): ThemeDiff Theme Diff Engine. Compares the previously applied CSS variables against the incoming theme's variables per token group. Comparing the *final resolved values* (rather than raw theme definitions) means two themes that resolve to identical colors produce no diff — and nothing animates. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `prev` | `Map<string, string> \| null \| undefined` | — | | `next` | `Record<string, string>` | — | | `prefix` | `string` (optional) | — | **Returns** `ThemeDiff` ---

title: createThemeHistory<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(store, options?): ThemeHistory<T>
text: createThemeHistory<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(store, options?): ThemeHistory<T> Creates an undo/redo history controller for a theme store. **See also:** `ThemeHistory`, `ThemeStore` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `store` | `ThemeStore<T>` | The store to track. | | `options` | `ThemeHistoryOptions` (optional) | History configuration (see ThemeHistoryOptions). | **Returns** `ThemeHistory<T>` — A new theme history controller. ```ts const history = createThemeHistory(store, { maxSteps: 20 }); history.undo(); ``` ---

title: createThemeLifecycle<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): ThemeLifecycle<T>
text: createThemeLifecycle<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): ThemeLifecycle<T> Creates a typed lifecycle event emitter for runtime events. **See also:** `ThemeLifecycle`, `ThemeLifecycleEventMap` **Returns** `ThemeLifecycle<T>` — A new lifecycle controller. ```ts const lifecycle = createThemeLifecycle(); const off = lifecycle.on("afterThemeChange", ({ theme }) => log(theme)); lifecycle.emit("afterThemeChange", { theme }); off(); ``` ---

title: createThemeModeController<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): { setMode: type(nextMode: ThemeMode): void; destroy: void; getMode: void }
text: createThemeModeController<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): { setMode: type(nextMode: ThemeMode): void; destroy: void; getMode: void } Create a theme-mode controller that resolves a mode into a concrete theme and keeps it applied to the store. In `system` mode it follows the OS color-scheme preference live via a system binding; in `light`/`dark` mode it applies the corresponding theme directly. `setMode` refuses a value that is not `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"`: the call is ignored — nothing is applied, persisted or broadcast — and a `TV_MODE_INVALID` diagnostic is emitted, so `getMode()` never reports a mode the runtime cannot render. Mode changes are persisted and broadcast when the corresponding adapters are provided. The returned controller is safe to destroy: after `destroy()` its methods become no-ops and all subscriptions are released. A persistence or broadcast adapter that throws does not abort the change: the resolved theme is still applied and the failure is reported as a `TV_SYNC_FAILED` diagnostic, so `getMode()` never reports a mode the screen is not showing. **See also:** `ThemeSelectionState`, `createThemePersistence` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeModeControllerOptions<T>` | The controller configuration. | **Returns** `{ setMode: __type(nextMode: ThemeMode): void; destroy: void; getMode: void }` — A controller exposing `getMode`, `setMode` and `destroy`. ```ts const controller = createThemeModeController({ store, lightTheme, darkTheme, persistence: createThemePersistence(), }); controller.setMode("dark"); ``` ---

title: createThemePersistence(options?): ThemePersistenceAdapter | null
text: createThemePersistence(options?): ThemePersistenceAdapter | null Create a theme-mode persistence adapter backed by `Storage`. The adapter reads/writes the mode under a single key and notifies subscribers of cross-tab changes through the `storage` event. It requires a `Window`; when none is available it returns `null` (e.g. during SSR). **See also:** `createDefaultPersistence`, `ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemePersistenceOptions` (optional) | The persistence configuration. | **Returns** `ThemePersistenceAdapter | null` — A `ThemePersistenceAdapter`, or `null` when no `Window` is available. ```ts const persistence = createThemePersistence({ key: "my-theme-mode" }); persistence?.set("dark"); ``` ---

title: createThemePrePaintCss<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string
text: createThemePrePaintCss<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string Generate the render-blocking stylesheet for the declared theme collection. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemePrePaintCssOptions<T>` | The registry and fallback configuration. | **Returns** `string` — A stylesheet that themes the document before any JavaScript runs. The output has three layers, in cascade order: 1. `:root` carries the fallback theme's variables. It is the only layer a no-JavaScript page can rely on, so it is always a complete, readable palette — never a partial one. 2. When the fallback mode is `"system"`, a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block overrides the fallback while the root carries no resolved theme attribute. The guard is deliberate: once the boot script (or a server render) names a concrete theme, the media block must not override it. 3. One `:root[data-theme="…"], [data-theme="…"]` rule per declared theme. The generic half is what pre-styles a scoped element such as `<themvora-scope data-theme="plum-dark">` before it upgrades; the `:root` half is what a server-rendered document and the boot script select. Both use the same canonical identity attribute, so any declared theme can be painted without JavaScript. Variables come from themeToCSSVariables, the canonical serializer, so a token emitted here is byte-identical to the one the runtime writes inline. The stylesheet is returned as text for an inline `<style>` element. Inline is used rather than an emitted asset because the CSS has to be present in Vite development *and* in a production build with identical contents, and because the only consumer-visible cost is one extra block in the document head — no second request, no base-path rewriting and no build-only asset path that can drift from the config. ---

title: createThemeReadoutScript(): string
text: createThemeReadoutScript(): string Builds the inline script that fills in **bootstrap readouts** and reconciles **selection controls**: the parts of the page that display or reflect a theme-derived value the server cannot know. **See also:** `createThemeBootstrapScript`, `readBootstrapState` **Returns** `string` — The script body to emit at the **end of `<body>`**, after the elements it patches exist. Three kinds of element opt in, and all three are reconciled from the same three values — the resolved theme, the mode selection and the family selection — because a control that lags the canvas by one value is the same bug in a smaller window: | Attribute | Written | Meaning | | --------- | ------- | ------- | | `data-tv-readout` | `textContent` | `"theme"`, `"label"`, `"mode"`, `"effective-mode"`, `"family"`, or `"var:<custom-property>"` | | `data-tv-pressed` + `data-tv-value` | `aria-pressed` | this element represents that option of `"mode"` / `"family"` | | `data-tv-select` | `value` | this `<select>` edits `"mode"` / `"family"` | Why this exists: a server-rendered readout or control can only show the *server's* resolution, and for `"system"` mode — or for any prerendered page, which has no request to read a cookie from — that is a fallback the browser overrides before the first paint. The canvas is corrected by the bootstrap, but the text and the pressed state are not, so they settle once after hydration, which is the last visible difference on an otherwise static page. On a page that reloads repeatedly it reads as the label "fluctuating" between the two themes. `data-tv-pressed` writes `aria-pressed` and nothing else. That is the whole point: the accessible state *is* the visual state, so a token class keyed off `aria-pressed` needs no second attribute to keep in step, and a screen reader can never announce a pressed option the page does not show as pressed. Patching before the first paint closes that, but only if the framework then leaves the element alone. In React that means pairing a readout with `suppressHydrationWarning` on the same element: React renders its own value during hydration, sees the DOM already differs, and — with the attribute — neither warns nor rewrites. The framework's own post-hydration render then produces the live value, which is the same value the script wrote, so nothing moves. Without the suppression React would rewrite the text back to the server's fallback and re-introduce the settle. It is deliberately placed at the end of the body: the blocking script runs in `<head>`, before these elements have been parsed, so it cannot patch them. **It reads the live document, not the page's build-time state.** The values come from `<html>`'s own `data-theme` / `data-theme-selection-*` attributes, which by this point describe what the visitor is actually looking at, and only fall back to the published bootstrap payload when those attributes are absent. That is what makes the script idempotent, and idempotence is load-bearing rather than tidy: `<ClientRouter />` re-executes inline body scripts on a client-side navigation, so this runs again on every navigation — after the incoming page's readouts have already been brought up to date. A script that wrote the *initial* selection would undo that, and every readout would revert to the page-build default until the next theme change. Measured on the example app: with the payload as the source, navigating from `/` with `cocoa-dark` selected left the readouts at `mint-light` / `system` / `mint` while the document was painted `cocoa-dark`. ---

title: createThemeRegistry<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemeRegistry<T>
text: createThemeRegistry<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemeRegistry<T> Creates a theme registry. **See also:** `ThemeRegistry`, `resolveThemeRegistry` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeRegistryOptions<T>` (optional) | Initial themes and registry configuration. | **Returns** `ThemeRegistry<T>` — A new ThemeRegistry. ```ts const registry = createThemeRegistry({ themes: [lightTheme, darkTheme] }); registry.get("light"); ``` ---

title: createThemeRuntime<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemeRuntime<T>
text: createThemeRuntime<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemeRuntime<T> Creates an independent Themvora runtime — the single entry point for theming. The runtime wires together the theme store, selection controller (mode/family/system binding), persistence, broadcast (cross-tab sync), history, scheduling, the DOM + CSS-variable bindings, and the adapter registry. **See also:** `ThemeRuntime`, `createThemeStore` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeRuntimeOptions<T>` (optional) | Runtime configuration and initial theme definitions. | **Returns** `ThemeRuntime<T>` — A new `ThemeRuntime` instance. The returned runtime must be destroyed when its owning application lifecycle ends. ```ts const runtime = createThemeRuntime({ themes: [lightTheme, darkTheme], defaultTheme: "light", initialMode: "system", }); runtime.selection.setMode("dark"); ``` ---

title: createThemeSchedule<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(store, themes, options): ThemeSchedule
text: createThemeSchedule<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(store, themes, options): ThemeSchedule Framework-neutral sunrise/sunset scheduling controller. Wraps the core `createScheduledThemeBinding` engine with an explicit on/off switch and a reactive state snapshot (`sunrise`, `sunset`, `nextTransition`, ...) so frameworks can expose it through their native accessors. `lightTheme` and `darkTheme` are optional: when omitted the schedule derives them from the currently selected theme's family (e.g. current `plum-dark` → scheduled `plum-light`/`plum-dark`) and falls back to the built-in neutral `light`/`dark` themes, re-resolving whenever the user switches theme family. The engine itself lives entirely in core — every framework wrapper talks to this single contract. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `store` | `ThemeScheduleStore<T>` | — | | `themes` | `readonly T[]` | — | | `options` | `ThemeScheduleOptions<T>` | — | **Returns** `ThemeSchedule` ---

title: createThemeScrollbar(store, options?): OverlayScrollbarHandle | null
text: createThemeScrollbar(store, options?): OverlayScrollbarHandle | null Alias landing in the public API. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `store` | `ThemeStore` | — | | `options` | `OverlayScrollbarOptions` (optional) | — | **Returns** `OverlayScrollbarHandle | null` ---

title: createThemeSelectionBroadcast(options?): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter | null
text: createThemeSelectionBroadcast(options?): ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter | null Create a broadcast adapter that publishes selection changes to other tabs/windows and applies incoming changes. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeSelectionBroadcastOptions` (optional) | — | **Returns** `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter | null` ---

title: createThemeStore<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): ThemeStore<T>
text: createThemeStore<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): ThemeStore<T> Creates a theme store: a framework-free container for the active theme. The store holds the current theme and notifies subscribers when it changes. Use the higher-level `createThemeRuntime` for the full runtime; use the store directly when you only need a reactive current-theme container. **See also:** `ThemeStore`, `createThemeRuntime` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeStoreOptions<T>` | Store configuration, including the initial theme. | **Returns** `ThemeStore<T>` — A new theme store. ```ts const store = createThemeStore({ initialTheme: lightTheme }); store.subscribe((theme) => console.log(theme.name)); store.set(darkTheme); ``` ---

title: createTransitionPlan(diff, options?, env?): TransitionPlan | null
text: createTransitionPlan(diff, options?, env?): TransitionPlan | null Transition Planner. Turns a ThemeDiff into a concrete TransitionPlan: - colors animate through the registered theme custom properties on `:root`, - every other changed group contributes the concrete CSS properties it maps to (radius → border-radius, spacing → padding/margin/gap, …). Returns `null` when there is nothing animatable: transitions disabled, reduced motion, an "instant" preset, or a diff where only non-animatable groups (layout/z-index/breakpoints) changed. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `diff` | `ThemeDiff` | — | | `options` | `ThemeTransitionOptions` (optional) | — | | `env` | `{ reducedMotion?: boolean }` (optional) | — | **Returns** `TransitionPlan | null` ---

title: createVueThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string
text: createVueThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string Build the blocking zero-flash `<head>` script for a Vue app (SSR or SPA). Inlines core's `createThemeBootstrapScript` with the Vue defaults (`storageKey: "theme-selection"`, `prefix: "theme-"` — the same values the Vue `ThemeProvider` persistence and CSS variables use), so the persisted theme is applied before first paint. Emit the returned string as a blocking `<script>` inside `<head>`. **See also:** ``buildThemeCssMap`` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeBootstrapScriptOptions<T>` | — | **Returns** `string` ---

title: darkModeCSSTemplate(variables): string
text: darkModeCSSTemplate(variables): string Generate a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` CSS block carrying the given variables. **See also:** `systemModeCSSTemplate` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `variables` | `Record<string, string>` | The CSS variables to emit under the dark media query. | **Returns** `string` — A `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block targeting `:root`, escaped so it cannot terminate a `<style>` element (`</` becomes `</`, which CSS parses identically). This is a **pre-script** fallback only, and it cannot beat an inline `style` on the same element: inline declarations outrank every stylesheet rule regardless of specificity. So it is only safe when nothing inlines the light variables — do not pair it with a server render that writes them onto `<html>`, or an OS-dark visitor keeps the light ones and this block is inert. When the resolved mode is `"system"`, use systemModeCSSTemplate instead: it emits both schemes and expects no inline variables. ---

title: defineTheme<Name extends string, T extends ThemeDefinition<Name>>(theme): T
text: defineTheme<Name extends string, T extends ThemeDefinition<Name>>(theme): T Define a theme. Currently returns the definition unchanged; it exists to give themes a consistent shape and future validation. **See also:** `extendTheme`, `composeTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `theme` | `T` | — | **Returns** `T` ---

title: defineThemvoraConfig<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(config): ThemvoraConfig<T>
text: defineThemvoraConfig<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(config): ThemvoraConfig<T> Declares the application's Themvora configuration. **See also:** `ThemvoraConfig` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `config` | `ThemvoraConfig<T>` | The configuration. | **Returns** `ThemvoraConfig<T>` — The same object, typed. An identity function. Its job is to give the configuration a name, a type and a validation point, so the Vite plugin can discover it by convention and the provider can consume the same object rather than a copy of it. ```ts // At the project root import { defineTheme, defineThemvoraConfig } from "@themvora/core"; const themes = [ defineTheme({ name: "brand-light", meta: { family: "brand", mode: "light" }, tokens: { colors: { background: "#ffffff" } }, }), defineTheme({ name: "brand-dark", meta: { family: "brand", mode: "dark" }, tokens: { colors: { background: "#101014" } }, }), ]; export default defineThemvoraConfig({ themes, defaultTheme: "brand-light", initialMode: "system", }); ``` ---

title: describeRoleUsage(role): { advisory: { description: string; owner: ContextOwner }[]; restricted: string[]; supported: string[] }
text: describeRoleUsage(role): { advisory: { description: string; owner: ContextOwner }[]; restricted: string[]; supported: string[] } What a role is for — the "safe usage" description. The docs and Theme Studio show this instead of a bare hex, because *how a token may be used* is the thing a reader actually needs. A ratio answers "is it readable here"; this answers "is it readable here on purpose". | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `role` | `CoreColor` | The role to describe. | **Returns** `{ advisory: { description: string; owner: ContextOwner }[]; restricted: string[]; supported: string[] }` — Where the role is supported, and where it is not. ---

title: destroySharedWorkerUrl(): void
text: destroySharedWorkerUrl(): void Release the shared worker's blob URL. Revokes the object URL created for the shared worker script and resets the cached URL, so a subsequent createSharedWorkerSync call creates a fresh worker. Safe to call multiple times; it is a no-op when no URL is cached. **Returns** `void` ---

title: diffThemes(a, b, options?): ThemeDiffReport
text: diffThemes(a, b, options?): ThemeDiffReport Diff two themes, or two light/dark theme sets. Accepts a single theme or a `{ light, dark }` pair on either side. Resolves inheritance through `options.themes` when a definition declares `extends`, and resolves a `mode: "system"` selector through the same registry. Only `light` and `dark` are visual modes. `"system"` is a selector over that pair, resolved before any comparison, and never appears in the report. `hasChanges` reflects **token** changes only. Provenance differences are reported separately, because two themes with identical tokens but different seeds render identically. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `a` | `ThemeDefinition<string> \| ThemeSet` | The first theme, or light/dark set. | | `b` | `ThemeDefinition<string> \| ThemeSet` | The second theme, or light/dark set. | | `options` | `ThemeDiffOptions` (optional) | Registry, `prefersDark`, `includeUnchanged`, and mode filter. | **Returns** `ThemeDiffReport` — The diff report. ```ts const report = diffThemes(mintLight, irisLight); report.modes.light?.changes.forEach((c) => { console.log(c.path, c.before, "→", c.after); }); ``` ---

title: disposeThemeTransitionStyles(target): void
text: disposeThemeTransitionStyles(target): void Release every transition style the coordinator owns for `target`: cancels an in-flight run and detaches the persistent `:root` transition stylesheet and the descendant-suppression stylesheet. cancelThemeAnimation deliberately leaves the `:root { transition }` rule in place between runs — it is written once and reused, so every subsequent change keeps animating. That rule must go when the feature is turned off or the owner is disposed, otherwise later variable swaps still interpolate through it: a theme switch after `transition: false` would animate despite the plan being `null`. Scoped targets never install the `:root` rule (it is document-wide), so for them this only clears the suppression node and the animating flag. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `target` | `HTMLElement` | — | **Returns** `void` ---

title: emitDiagnostic(diagnostic, options?): void
text: emitDiagnostic(diagnostic, options?): void Emit a diagnostic to the console. Developer-facing Themvora diagnostics go through here rather than calling `console` directly, so that the level, the code, the deduplication and the development/production formatting stay consistent across packages. Repeated identical diagnostics are suppressed by default; see EmitDiagnosticOptions.dedupe. Use resetDiagnosticEmission to clear that memory. **See also:** `createDiagnostic`, `formatDiagnostic` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `diagnostic` | `ThemeDiagnostic` | The diagnostic to emit. | | `options` | `EmitDiagnosticOptions` (optional) | Environment, deduplication and sink overrides. | **Returns** `void` ---

title: emitInvalidOptionDiagnostic(option): void
text: emitInvalidOptionDiagnostic(option): void Report an unusable transition/scheduling option supplied to `configure()`. `level: "warning"` — the runtime keeps the previous setting for the affected subsystem (a defined state) rather than corrupting a healthy runtime or throwing. Deduplicated by emitDiagnostic, so an adapter that forwards the same invalid value on every render logs it once. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `option` | `InvalidOption` | — | **Returns** `void` ---

title: emitNeutralFallbackDiagnostic(): void
text: emitNeutralFallbackDiagnostic(): void Report that no usable theme was available and the neutral fallback was used. `level: "warning"` — the runtime recovers safely, so this is reported, not thrown. Deduplicated like every other diagnostic. **Returns** `void` ---

title: emitScheduledThemeUnresolvedDiagnostic(names): void
text: emitScheduledThemeUnresolvedDiagnostic(names): void Report that a `scheduled` configuration named light/dark themes that are not registered, so the schedule cannot drive the selection. `level: "warning"` — the schedule is installed but reports no light/dark pair, matching the existing `TV_SCHEDULE_THEME_UNRESOLVED` contract used by the scheduled plugin. Deduplicated by emitDiagnostic. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `names` | `{ darkTheme?: string; lightTheme?: string }` | — | **Returns** `void` ---

title: emitUnknownFamilyDiagnostic(requested, resolved, themes): void
text: emitUnknownFamilyDiagnostic(requested, resolved, themes): void Report a family that is not registered in the effective catalog. `level: "error"` because an explicitly requested family that cannot resolve is a configuration mistake, not a supported absence. Deduplication is handled by emitDiagnostic: the same invalid value reports once, a new invalid value reports again. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `requested` | `string` | — | | `resolved` | `string` | — | | `themes` | `readonly ThemeDefinition<string>[]` | — | **Returns** `void` ---

title: evaluateExpression(expr): string
text: evaluateExpression(expr): string Evaluate a numeric arithmetic expression and return the result as a string. Supports `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, parentheses, and an optional trailing CSS unit (e.g. `"1.5 * 2rem"` → `"3rem"`). Integer results are returned without a decimal point; non-integer results are rounded to two decimals. When the input is not a valid expression, or evaluation fails, the original string is returned unchanged. **See also:** `isExpression` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `expr` | `string` | The expression string to evaluate. | **Returns** `string` — The evaluated result string, or `expr` unchanged when it cannot be evaluated. ---

title: extendTheme<TName extends string, TBase extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(name, base, overrides?): ThemeDefinition<TName>
text: extendTheme<TName extends string, TBase extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(name, base, overrides?): ThemeDefinition<TName> Create a new theme by extending a base theme with overrides, merging token groups recursively. **See also:** `defineTheme`, `mergeTokens` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `name` | `TName` | — | | `base` | `TBase` | — | | `overrides` | `TokenOverrides & { meta?: Partial<ThemeMeta> }` (optional) | — | **Returns** `ThemeDefinition<TName>` ---

title: findGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(themes, active?): GeneratedThemeLookup<T>
text: findGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(themes, active?): GeneratedThemeLookup<T> Locate the generated theme among a provider's registered themes. Deterministic and non-throwing: - No generated theme registered → `"missing"`. - Exactly one → `"found"`. - More than one → `"found"` for the one whose name matches `active` (the current active selection); otherwise `"ambiguous"`. The first candidate is never returned on a tie. **See also:** `resolveGeneratedTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `themes` | `readonly T[]` | The themes registered with the provider, in registration order. | | `active` | `T` (optional) | The currently active theme, used to disambiguate multiple generated themes. Omitted on a surface with no active selection. | **Returns** `GeneratedThemeLookup<T>` — The lookup result. ---

title: flattenTokens(tokens): Record<string, string>
text: flattenTokens(tokens): Record<string, string> Flatten a theme's token groups into a single dot-path → value map. Nested token objects are flattened with dot-separated paths (e.g. `colors.primary`, `typography.fontSizes.base`). Only string values are included; non-string values are skipped. The result is the lookup surface used to resolve token references. **See also:** `resolveTokens` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `tokens` | `ThemeTokens` | The theme token groups to flatten. | **Returns** `Record<string, string>` — A flat map of dot-path keys to string token values. ---

title: formatDiagnostic(diagnostic, options?): string
text: formatDiagnostic(diagnostic, options?): string Render a diagnostic as a single log line. This is the environment-specific half of the model: the diagnostic itself is plain data, and this decides how much of it a given environment should see. In development the context, hint and docs link are appended, because that is where they are actionable. Outside development the message is emitted alone — the failure is never hidden, but the surrounding detail is not shipped to end users. **See also:** `emitDiagnostic` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `diagnostic` | `ThemeDiagnostic` | The diagnostic to render. | | `options` | `{ dev?: boolean }` (optional) | `dev` overrides environment detection. Intended for tests and for callers that already know which build they are in. | **Returns** `string` — A single-line, prefixed string. ---

title: generateTheme(options): GeneratedThemePair
text: generateTheme(options): GeneratedThemePair Generate a cohesive light/dark theme pair from a single seed color. Light and dark are generated **independently** from the same identity — the dark theme is not an inversion of the light one — so the brand hue survives the mode change. Every semantic pair is solved to the contrast contract with a safety margin before the theme is returned, and the seed is recorded in `meta.generation` as provenance. **See also:** `validateTheme`, `defineTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `GenerateThemeOptions` | The seed color and generation options. | **Returns** `GeneratedThemePair` — A `{ light, dark }` pair of theme definitions sharing one family. ```ts const { light, dark } = generateTheme({ seed: "#d97706", family: "brand" }); ``` ---

title: getContrastRatio(foreground, background): number
text: getContrastRatio(foreground, background): number Compute the WCAG contrast ratio between two colors. The ratio is `(L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)` where `L1`/`L2` are the relative luminances of the lighter and darker colors, yielding a value in the range 1 (identical colors) to 21 (black on white). Colors are parsed as hex. **See also:** `validateThemeContrast` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `foreground` | `string` | The foreground color (hex). | | `background` | `string` | The background color (hex). | **Returns** `number` — The contrast ratio, a number between 1 and 21. ---

title: getNeutralThemes(): [ThemeDefinition<string>, ThemeDefinition<string>]
text: getNeutralThemes(): [ThemeDefinition<string>, ThemeDefinition<string>] Build the neutral light and dark themes. These are the framework's baseline themes: a full token set (colors, radius, spacing, shadows, border widths, z-index, breakpoints, typography, and code) with no color family applied. They are the fallback when no family is selected. Their colors are generated, so they satisfy the same contrast contract as every preset. **Returns** `[ThemeDefinition<string>, ThemeDefinition<string>]` — A `[light, dark]` tuple of neutral theme definitions. ---

title: getPresetCatalog(kind?): PresetCatalogEntry[]
text: getPresetCatalog(kind?): PresetCatalogEntry[] The preset catalog, derived from the recipes. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `kind` | `PresetKind` (optional) | Restrict to `"default"` or `"brand"`. Omit for both. | **Returns** `PresetCatalogEntry[]` — The catalog entries, in recipe order. ---

title: getPresetThemes(overrides?): ThemeDefinition<string>[]
text: getPresetThemes(overrides?): ThemeDefinition<string>[] Build the curated preset theme set: a light and dark theme for each preset color family (oat, berry, mint, citrus, cocoa, plum, iris, sky, graphite). Each preset is generated from a recipe — seed, style and radius — by the same `semantic-v2` pipeline `generateTheme()` uses, so every preset already satisfies the contrast contract and the visual relationship checks before it is returned. Optional per-family, per-mode token overrides are applied on top, afterwards. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `overrides` | `Partial<Record<PresetFamily, Partial<Record<PresetVariant, PresetVariantOverride>>>>` (optional) | Optional per-family, per-mode token overrides. | **Returns** `ThemeDefinition<string>[]` — An array of preset theme definitions, one light and one dark per family. ```ts const themes = getPresetThemes({ plum: { light: { tokens: { colors: { primary: "#6d28d9" } } } }, }); ``` ---

text: getThemeMode(theme): ThemeMode Get the color mode of a theme. Uses `meta.mode` when present; otherwise infers it from the theme name (e.g. `"mint-dark"` → "dark"). This keeps simple theme definitions working: `[{ name: "light", ... }, { name: "dark", ... }]` resolve and toggle correctly without requiring `meta.mode`. **See also:** `resolveThemeName` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `theme` | `ThemeDefinition` | — | **Returns** `ThemeMode` ---

title: hideNativeScrollbar(): type(): void
text: hideNativeScrollbar(): type(): void Hide the native scrollbar and register a claim that keeps it hidden. Returns the release function for that claim. The hiding is applied idempotently (the class may already be server-rendered, the stylesheet may already exist), and it is released when the last claim goes away — so `createOverlayScrollbar` and its `destroy()` are a matched pair rather than a one-way switch. **Returns** `__type(): void` ---

title: isCoreColor(key): key is CoreColor

title: isExpression(value): boolean
text: isExpression(value): boolean Determine whether a string is a numeric arithmetic expression. An expression is a string containing `+`, `-`, `*`, or `/` over numbers and parentheses, optionally ending in a CSS unit (e.g. `"1.5 * 2rem"`). Function calls such as `contrast(...)` and `auto()` are not treated as expressions. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `value` | `string` | The string to test. | **Returns** `boolean` — `true` when `value` is a numeric arithmetic expression. ---

title: isGeneratedTheme(theme): boolean
text: isGeneratedTheme(theme): boolean Whether a theme was produced by the public generateTheme call. Matches on the explicit origin marker only. It deliberately does **not** infer from a theme's name, family, or colors: the built-in presets and the neutral baseline are produced by the same engine and would otherwise be mistaken for application-generated themes, and a hand-authored theme could impersonate one by adopting a familiar id. **See also:** `resolveGeneratedTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `theme` | `ThemeDefinition` | The theme definition to test. | **Returns** `boolean` — `true` when the theme carries the generator's origin marker. ---

text: isSelectionResolvable(themes, selection): boolean Whether a selection can be resolved to a usable theme in a catalog. A selection is resolvable when its family is registered in `themes` AND at least one theme for that family resolves the requested mode (treating `"system"` as the light variant for the check — the caller re-resolves the concrete mode). | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `themes` | `readonly ThemeDefinition<string>[]` | — | | `selection` | `ThemeSelectionState` | — | **Returns** `boolean` ---

title: isSettled(current, target, epsilon?): boolean
