title: createRemixThemePersistence(themes?, defaultTheme?, options): ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter | null
text: createRemixThemePersistence(themes?, defaultTheme?, options): ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter | null Creates the client-side persistence adapter for Remix. Mirrors the theme selection to `localStorage` (cross-tab sync, offline) AND to the theme cookies (`theme-family` / `theme-mode` / `theme-fingerprint`) so the server resolves the exact same state on the next request. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `ThemeHead` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `themes` | `readonly ThemeDefinition<string>[]` (optional) | The theme registry used to compute the config fingerprint. | | `defaultTheme` | `string` (optional) | Fallback theme name used in the fingerprint. | | `options` | `RemixThemePersistenceOptions` | Persistence options (see RemixThemePersistenceOptions). | **Returns** `ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter | null` — A persistence adapter, or `null` when running outside the browser. Returns `null` during SSR (no `window`), so the runtime falls back to its default persistence behavior on the server. The cookie contract matches `@themvora/next` and `@themvora/nuxt`. **Blocked storage degrades, it does not throw.** `window.localStorage` can throw on access and `setItem` throws when the quota is full; both are treated as "this browser cannot remember the selection". The cookie mirror is written either way, so the server still resolves the same theme on the next request. ```ts import { createRemixThemePersistence } from "@themvora/remix"; const persistence = createRemixThemePersistence(myThemes, "light", { key: "my-theme-selection", }); ``` ---

title: createThemeDocument<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(config): ThemeDocumentHandle<T>
text: createThemeDocument<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(config): ThemeDocumentHandle<T> Create a single-source theme configuration for a server-rendered document. The returned `Document` renders the blocking bootstrap in `<head>`, the matching theme attributes and CSS variables on `<html>`, the scrollbar class and pre-paint stylesheet when configured, and the runtime provider around the application tree. `resolveInitial` derives the request-specific state from the same configuration, so the loader, the script, the shell and the provider cannot drift apart. **See also:** `ThemeDocumentConfig` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `config` | `ThemeDocumentConfig<T>` | The registry, fallback selection, static runtime options (`transition`, `scheduled`, `themeOverride`) and document options. | **Returns** `ThemeDocumentHandle<T>` — The document handle: `resolveInitial`, `Document`, `Provider`, `config` and the static `fallback`. The configuration is copied and frozen, so changing the caller's `themes` array later cannot change what an already-created document renders. Request state is never stored on the handle: `resolveInitial` derives it from the `Request` it is given, which keeps concurrent requests isolated. The handler imports the server resolver lazily. The client bundle therefore does not include the cookie parser, while the loader still gets a synchronous configuration it can call. ```ts // app/root.tsx — React Router Framework Mode import { createThemeDocument } from "@themvora/remix/react-router"; import { getBuiltInThemes } from "@themvora/core"; import type { Route } from "./+types/root"; const themes = getBuiltInThemes(); const theming = createThemeDocument({ themes, defaultTheme: "light", mode: "system", transition: { enabled: true, preset: "smooth" }, scrollbar: true, }); export async function loader({ request }: Route.LoaderArgs) { return { theme: await theming.resolveInitial(request) }; } export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { const data = useRouteLoaderData<typeof loader>("root"); return ( <theming.Document initial={data?.theme} head={[<Meta key="meta" />, <Links key="links" />]} afterContent={<><ScrollRestoration /><Scripts /></>} > {children} </theming.Document> ); } ``` ---

title: getThemeShellProps<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(initial, options): ThemeShellProps
text: getThemeShellProps<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(initial, options): ThemeShellProps The `<html>` attributes the pre-paint bootstrap script writes, as React props. Spread them onto the document element rendered by `app/root.tsx`. **See also:** `ThemeHead` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `initial` | `InitialThemeResolution<T>` | The SSR-resolved initial state from `getInitialThemeState`. | | `options` | `ThemeShellOptions` | Extra classes, the scrollbar opt-in, and extra inline styles. | **Returns** `ThemeShellProps` — The `<html>` props: the theme attributes, the CSS variables, and the hydration suppression. Every value here is a *snapshot* of the server's resolution, and it exists for one reason: **hydration parity**. The blocking script in `<ThemeHead>` rewrites all of it before first paint, so React's virtual DOM has to start out agreeing with the DOM, or React reports a hydration mismatch on `<html>` and — because it never patches attributes up — keeps a virtual DOM that disagrees with the document for the rest of the session. That is not hypothetical. A Remix app that renders a bare `<html lang="en">` hydrates against seven attributes it never rendered (`data-theme`, `data-theme-mode`, `data-theme-family`, `data-theme-selection-mode`, `data-theme-selection-family`, `data-theme-ready` and `style`), and React logs "some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client properties" on every load. Rendering the snapshot removes six of the seven; `suppressHydrationWarning` covers the last one, which cannot be removed by construction: `data-theme-mode` is the *resolved* mode, so a `"system"` selection resolved against a dark `prefers-color-scheme` legitimately differs from the server's `"light"`. The same goes for the `dark` class the script toggles, which is deliberately not rendered here — the script owns it. The suppression is scoped to the `<html>` element and its own attributes. It does not hide mismatches in the application tree, so a genuine hydration bug in a route still reports. ```ts import { getBuiltInThemes } from "@themvora/core"; import { ThemeHead, getThemeShellProps } from "@themvora/remix"; const themes = getBuiltInThemes(); export function Layout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) { const { initial } = useLoaderData<typeof loader>(); return ( <html lang="en" {...getThemeShellProps(initial, { scrollbar: true })}> <head> <ThemeHead themes={themes} defaultTheme="light" scrollbar /> </head> <body>{children}</body> </html> ); } ``` ---

title: ThemeHead<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element
text: ThemeHead<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element Renders the blocking theme bootstrap in the document `<head>`. Emits an inline script that reads the persisted theme cookies and applies the CSS variables plus DOM effects before first paint (zero-flash), plus a `prefers-color-scheme` dark-mode fallback when the selection is `"system"`. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `ThemeHeadProps` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeHeadProps<T>` | The head props (see ThemeHeadProps). | **Returns** `Element` — A fragment containing the blocking `<script>` and optional dark-mode `<style>`. Place this inside the document `<head>` so the script runs before the app stylesheets and the browser paints already themed. Pair with `ThemeProvider` and `getInitialThemeState` for the full SSR-first setup. ```ts import { ThemeHead } from "@themvora/remix"; export function Layout({ children }) { return ( // `tv-scrollbar` must be rendered here, not added by a script. <html className="tv-scrollbar"> <head> <ThemeHead themes={myThemes} defaultTheme="light" scrollbar /> </head> <body>{children}</body> </html> ); } ``` ---

title: ThemeInspector(namedParameters?): Element
text: ThemeInspector(namedParameters?): Element A floating developer tool that inspects the active theme. Renders a fixed toggle button and an expandable panel showing the current theme name, family, mode, selection state, token values, and emitted CSS variables — useful while building themeable UI. **See also:** `useTheme` **Returns** `Element` The panel opens above the toggle with a gap, stays dismissible via the toggle, `Escape`, or clicking outside, and matches the provider's transition duration for its own fade. ```ts <ThemeInspector /> ``` ---

title: ThemeProvider<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element
text: ThemeProvider<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element Remix theme provider. Mounts the client theme runtime, wires the cookie persistence adapter, and — when an SSR-resolved `initial` state is supplied — mirrors the selection back to cookies so the server resolves the same state on the next request (zero-flash). **See also:** `ThemeHead`, `createRemixThemePersistence`, `ThemeProviderProps` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeProviderProps<T>` | The provider props (see ThemeProviderProps). | **Returns** `Element` — The provider tree wrapping the application content. Pair with `ThemeHead` in the document `<head>` and `getInitialThemeState` in the loader for the full SSR-first, zero-flash setup. When `initial` is omitted, the persisted selection is read on the client from `localStorage` and then from the theme cookies `ThemeHead`'s script reads — see ThemeProviderProps.initial for the hydration caveat. ```ts import { ThemeProvider } from "@themvora/remix"; export default function App({ children }) { return ( <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light" themes={myThemes}> {children} </ThemeProvider> ); } ``` ---

title: ThemeScope(namedParameters): Element
text: ThemeScope(namedParameters): Element Applies a theme to a subtree without replacing the global runtime. The scope resolves local themes (`themes` prop) before falling back to the parent runtime's theme registry. Nested scopes override their parent within their own boundary. Theme changes are reactive: `theme`/`family`/`mode` props and global mode changes re-resolve and animate in place without remounting. **See also:** `useScopedTheme` **Returns** `Element` Scope-local transitions inherit the parent transition configuration unless explicitly overridden or disabled. First paint is server-safe: explicit selections ship resolved variables inline, while OS-dependent selections (system mode / family-following scopes) ship no inline variables plus a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` override, so no flash occurs. ```ts <ThemeScope family="plum" mode="dark"> <Editor /> </ThemeScope> ``` ---

title: ThemeScrollbar(props): null
text: ThemeScrollbar(props): null ThemeScrollbar — overlay only. Creates the custom scrollbar overlay. Lifecycle: mount → create overlay → measure → attach listeners paint → add tv-scrollbar-ready destroy → remove overlay Props are four optional groups — `behavior`, `appearance`, `scope` and `icons` — plus `children`, which is accepted for JSX symmetry only. <ThemeScrollbar behavior={{ autoHide: true, smooth: true }} appearance={{ thickness: 8, radius: 999 }} scope={{ include: [".panel"] }} icons={{ up: <ArrowUpIcon />, size: 12 }} /> <ThemeScrollbar behavior={{ autoHide: true, smooth: true }} appearance={{ thickness: 8, radius: 999 }} icons={{ up: <ArrowUpIcon />, down: <ArrowDownIcon /> }} /> **See also:** `ThemeProvider` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeScrollbarProps` | — | **Returns** `null` ---

title: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): T
text: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): T The theme produced by `generateTheme()` and registered with the provider. Returns the registered theme that carries the generator's origin marker (`meta.generation.kind === "generated"`) — never a shipped preset, and never inferred from a theme's id, family or colors. Generate one and pass the result to `ThemeProvider`: ```tsx const generated = generateTheme({ seed: "#635BFF", family: "brand" }); <ThemeProvider themes={[generated.light, generated.dark]}>{children}</ThemeProvider> ``` When both halves of one `generateTheme()` call are registered, the theme the active selection resolves to is returned. If several generated themes are registered and none is active, the call throws rather than guessing. Throws `ThemeError` with code `TV_GENERATION_THEME_NOT_FOUND` when the provider holds no generated theme, and `TV_GENERATION_THEME_AMBIGUOUS` when several are registered and the active selection does not identify one. Re-resolves on every settled change to the registry, store, or selection; if the generated theme is later removed, the same error is raised at the next render rather than a stale theme being returned. **See also:** `useThemeValue` **Returns** `T` — The registered generated theme. ---

title: useProvidedThemes<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): readonly ProvidedThemeFamily<T>[]
text:
useProvidedThemes>(): readonly ProvidedThemeFamily[] The themes this provider was given, grouped by family. Returns exactly the collection supplied to the nearest `ThemeProvider` — not the built-in catalog, and not every theme that exists in the project. Build a theme picker from it instead of enumerating a separate preset source: ```tsx const themes = useProvidedThemes(); return themes.map((family) => (

{family.name}

{family.variants.map((variant) => ( ))}
)); ``` The collection is reactive: a `themes` prop change, a `runtime.use(pack)` install or a registry mutation re-renders the consumer. Entries keep their identity while their content is unchanged, so `React.memo` and dependency arrays behave. **See also:** `useTheme`, `normalizeProvidedThemes` **Returns** `readonly ProvidedThemeFamily[]` — The provider's theme families, in supplied order. ---

title: useSetThemeFamily<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): type(family: ThemeFamilies<readonly T[]>): void
text: useSetThemeFamily<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): type(family: ThemeFamilies<readonly T[]>): void Get a stable `setFamily` function (does not re-render on change). **See also:** `useThemeFamily` **Returns** `__type(family: ThemeFamilies<readonly T[]>): void` ---

title: useTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { effectiveMode: "light" | "dark"; family: string; mode: ThemeMode; setFamily: type(family: ThemeFamilies<readonly T[]>): void; setMode: type(mode: ModesOf<T>): void; theme: T; toggleTheme: type(): void }
text: useTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { effectiveMode: "light" | "dark"; family: string; mode: ThemeMode; setFamily: type(family: ThemeFamilies<readonly T[]>): void; setMode: type(mode: ModesOf<T>): void; theme: T; toggleTheme: type(): void } The primary Themvora hook. Returns the current theme, mode, family and the selection controls. When you pass the theme tuple element type, `setFamily` and `setMode` are constrained to the families/modes defined in your registry (the built-in set is used below so the example stands alone): ```ts import { getBuiltInThemes } from "@themvora/core"; const themes = getBuiltInThemes(); const { theme, mode, family, setMode, setFamily, toggleTheme } = useTheme<typeof themes[number]>(); setFamily("mint"); // autocomplete suggests your families setMode("dark"); ``` **See also:** `useThemeValue`, `useThemeMode`, `useEffectiveThemeMode`, `useThemeFamily` **Returns** `{ effectiveMode: "light" | "dark"; family: string; mode: ThemeMode; setFamily: __type(family: ThemeFamilies<readonly T[]>): void; setMode: __type(mode: ModesOf<T>): void; theme: T; toggleTheme: __type(): void }` ---

text: useThemeBatch(): type(callback: type(): void): void Get a batch function that defers all selection changes and DOM writes to a single flush. **See also:** `useTheme` **Returns** `__type(callback: __type(): void): void` ---

text: useThemeHistory(): { canRedo: boolean; canUndo: boolean; clear: type(): void; redo: type(): void; undo: type(): void } Subscribe to the runtime history (undo/redo/canUndo/canRedo/clear). **See also:** `useThemeTimeTravel` **Returns** `{ canRedo: boolean; canUndo: boolean; clear: __type(): void; redo: __type(): void; undo: __type(): void }` ---

text: useThemeLifecycle<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { on: type<K extends keyof ThemeLifecycleEventMap<ThemeDefinition<string>>>(event: K, listener: type(data: ThemeLifecycleEventMap<T>[K]): void): type(): void } Subscribe to runtime lifecycle events (theme changed, mode changed, …). The handler is typed per event name, so `on("beforeThemeChange", ({ next }) => …)` gives you the theme definitions rather than `unknown` — the same precision `runtime.lifecycle.on` has in `@themvora/core`. **See also:** `useTheme` **Returns** `{ on: __type<K extends keyof ThemeLifecycleEventMap<ThemeDefinition<string>>>(event: K, listener: __type(data: ThemeLifecycleEventMap<T>[K]): void): __type(): void }` ---

title: useThemeMode(): ThemeMode
text: useThemeMode(): ThemeMode Subscribe to the current selection mode ("light" | "dark" | "system"). This is the mode the visitor **asked for**. While a sunrise/sunset schedule is running, or while the selection is `"system"`, the appearance on screen can differ from it — use useEffectiveThemeMode to display what is actually applied. **See also:** `useEffectiveThemeMode`, `useSetThemeMode` **Returns** `ThemeMode` ---

title: useThemePacks(): type(pack: ThemePack<any>): void
text: useThemePacks(): type(pack: ThemePack<any>): void Get a function that applies a theme pack to the runtime. **See also:** `useTheme` **Returns** `__type(pack: ThemePack<any>): void` ---

title: useThemeRestore(): type(snapshot: ThemeRuntimeSnapshot): void
text: useThemeRestore(): type(snapshot: ThemeRuntimeSnapshot): void Get a restore function that re-applies a previously captured snapshot. **See also:** `useThemeSnapshot` **Returns** `__type(snapshot: ThemeRuntimeSnapshot): void` ---

title: useThemeRuntime<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): ThemeRuntime<T>
text: useThemeRuntime<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): ThemeRuntime<T> Get the active Themvora runtime from context. Throws when used outside a `ThemeProvider`. Pass the theme tuple element type to type the runtime's store/selection against your registry — any registry works, so the built-in set is used here to keep the example self-contained: ```ts import { getBuiltInThemes } from "@themvora/core"; const themes = getBuiltInThemes(); const runtime = useThemeRuntime<typeof themes[number]>(); ``` **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `useTheme` **Returns** `ThemeRuntime<T>` ---

title: useThemeSchedule(): ThemeSchedule | null
text: useThemeSchedule(): ThemeSchedule | null Reactive access to the runtime's sunrise/sunset scheduling controller. Requires the runtime to be created with the `scheduled` option (see `ThemeProvider` / `createThemeRuntime`). Returns `null` when the provider has no schedule configured. ```tsx const schedule = useThemeSchedule(); schedule?.enable(); schedule?.disable(); // schedule.enabled, schedule.active, schedule.sunrise, schedule.sunset, // schedule.nextTransition ... re-render reactively. ``` **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `useTheme` **Returns** `ThemeSchedule | null` The returned controller is a **reactive view**: its state reads come from the subscription below, not from the live controller. That is what makes it safe to render during SSR — the subscription hydrates from EMPTY_THEME_SCHEDULE_STATE, the same snapshot the server rendered, and only adopts the live state after mount. Returning the raw controller instead (which is what this hook used to do, discarding the subscription it had just created) handed consumers the *live* value during the hydration render, so React saw a mismatch against the server HTML and re-rendered the tree. ---

title: ThemeDocumentConfig<T extends ThemeDefinition>
text: ThemeDocumentConfig<T extends ThemeDefinition> The one description of a document-level theme installation. Every value here is static: it does not depend on the incoming request, so a module can declare one configuration and use it for the pre-paint script, the server-rendered `<html>` element and the client runtime. The request-specific result is the `initial` state produced by ThemeDocumentHandle.resolveInitial. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `bodyClassName` (optional) | `string` | Classes rendered on `<body>`. | | `bodyStyle` (optional) | `CSSProperties` | Inline styles rendered on `<body>`. | | `className` (optional) | `string` | Classes merged onto the `<html>` element alongside the theme's own. | | `defaultTheme` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Fallback theme when no selection is persisted. Accepts a theme **name** or a **family**; a family resolves to the variant for the mode in effect. | | `family` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Family used when nothing is persisted and `defaultTheme` names no family. A variant name is normalised to its family. | | `initialFamily` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Alias for ThemeDocumentConfig.family, matching the name the Remix provider prop has always used. `family` wins when both are supplied. | | `initialMode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Alias for ThemeDocumentConfig.mode, matching the name the Remix provider prop has always used. `mode` wins when both are supplied. | | `mode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Mode used when neither a persisted selection nor `themeOverride` applies. Defaults to the fallback theme's own mode. Pass `"system"` to follow `prefers-color-scheme` instead. | | `scheduled` (optional) | `false \| ScheduledThemeOptions<T>` | The solar schedule passed to the runtime, so light/dark can follow the visitor's sunrise and sunset. The document still resolves and paints the persisted selection; the schedule takes over once the runtime mounts. | | `scrollbar` (optional) | `boolean` | Hide the native scrollbar from the very first paint. Adds the `tv-scrollbar` class to `<html>` and emits the pre-paint hiding stylesheet. The application still imports `@themvora/core/scrollbar.css` itself: a CSS import is a bundler concern, not something a component can inject. | | `style` (optional) | `CSSProperties` | Inline styles merged after the theme's CSS variables on `<html>`. | | `themeOverride` (optional) | `ThemeOverride<ThemeIdentifier<T>>` | An explicit theme override applied over any persisted selection. The pre-paint script, the shell and the runtime all receive the same value. | | `themes` | `readonly T[]` | The theme registry the selection is resolved against. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition configuration passed to the runtime: `true`, `false`, or `{ enabled, duration, easing, preset, … }`. Same contract as the Remix provider's `transition` prop, so a document-level setup can express animations without falling back to the lower-level `ThemeProvider`. | ---

Used by `Document` when `initial` is missing or `null`. | | `Document` | `ReactElement` | — | | `Provider` | `ReactElement` | — | | `resolveInitial` | `Promise<InitialThemeResolution<T>>` | — | ---

title: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition>
text: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition> Props for the Remix `ThemeProvider`. Configures the theme registry, the fallback selection, and the optional SSR-resolved initial state. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `ThemeHead` | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `children` | `ReactNode` | The application content rendered inside the provider. | | `defaultTheme` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Fallback theme when no selection is persisted. Accepts a supplied theme **name** (`"cocoa-light"`) or a **family** (`"cocoa"`); a family resolves to the variant for the mode in effect. | | `initial` (optional) | `InitialThemeResolution<T>` | The SSR-resolved initial theme state (from `getInitialThemeState`). When provided, it wins on first paint so hydration matches exactly and the selection is mirrored back to cookies. | | `initialFamily` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Family used when neither `initial` nor a persisted selection is available. Pair it with `initialMode` for the same reason. Constrained to the identifiers in `themes` when they are statically known. A variant name is accepted and normalised to its family; its mode applies only when `initialMode` is absent. | | `initialMode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Mode used when neither `initial` nor a persisted selection is available. Optional: the runtime and `ThemeHead`'s script both derive the fallback mode from `defaultTheme` by default, so they already agree. Set this to pin a mode the script would not derive — e.g. `"system"` to follow `prefers-color-scheme` — and pass the same value to `ThemeHead`. Ignored when `initial` is provided, since the SSR resolution wins. | | `scheduled` (optional) | `false \| ScheduledThemeOptions<T>` | Sunrise/sunset schedule forwarded to the runtime. Same contract as `@themvora/react`'s provider; `createThemeDocument()` forwards its `scheduled` option through this prop. | | `themeOverride` (optional) | `ThemeOverride<ThemeIdentifier<T>>` | An explicit theme override applied over any persisted selection. Applied once per value, never written to the theme cookies, and it does not fight a later manual selection. For a flash-free override, pass the same value to ThemeHead so the pre-paint script resolves it too. | | `themes` (optional) | `readonly T[]` | The theme registry the selection is resolved against. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition configuration forwarded to the runtime: `true`, `false`, or `{ enabled, duration, easing, preset, … }`. Same contract as `@themvora/react`'s provider. `createThemeDocument()` forwards its `transition` option through this prop, so the new single-configuration API can express everything the provider accepts. | ---

title: getInitialThemeState<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(request, options): Promise<InitialThemeResolution<T>>
text: getInitialThemeState<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(request, options): Promise<InitialThemeResolution<T>> Resolves the initial theme state server-side from the request's theme cookies, so the browser paints already themed (zero-flash). Pair with `ThemeProvider` (pass the result as `initial`) and `ThemeHead` in the document `<head>`. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `ThemeHead` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `request` | `Request` | The incoming request. | | `options` | `ResolveInitialThemeOptions<T>` | The theme registry and fallback selection. | **Returns** `Promise<InitialThemeResolution<T>>` — The resolved initial theme state. The saved selection is only honoured when the `theme-fingerprint` cookie matches the current registry: a cookie written by an older build — different themes, or a different `defaultTheme` — is ignored. That is the same rule `ThemeHead`'s pre-paint script and `createRemixThemePersistence` apply, and without it the server rendered the stale cookie's theme while the client rejected it, producing a hydration mismatch and a visible flash for returning visitors. A **missing** fingerprint is still accepted, which is the legacy cookie contract every integration shares. ---

title: createRemixThemePersistence(themes?, defaultTheme?, options): ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter | null
text: createRemixThemePersistence(themes?, defaultTheme?, options): ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter | null Creates the client-side persistence adapter for Remix. Mirrors the theme selection to `localStorage` (cross-tab sync, offline) AND to the theme cookies (`theme-family` / `theme-mode` / `theme-fingerprint`) so the server resolves the exact same state on the next request. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `ThemeHead` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `themes` | `readonly ThemeDefinition<string>[]` (optional) | The theme registry used to compute the config fingerprint. | | `defaultTheme` | `string` (optional) | Fallback theme name used in the fingerprint. | | `options` | `RemixThemePersistenceOptions` | Persistence options (see RemixThemePersistenceOptions). | **Returns** `ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter | null` — A persistence adapter, or `null` when running outside the browser. Returns `null` during SSR (no `window`), so the runtime falls back to its default persistence behavior on the server. The cookie contract matches `@themvora/next` and `@themvora/nuxt`. **Blocked storage degrades, it does not throw.** `window.localStorage` can throw on access and `setItem` throws when the quota is full; both are treated as "this browser cannot remember the selection". The cookie mirror is written either way, so the server still resolves the same theme on the next request. ```ts import { createRemixThemePersistence } from "@themvora/remix"; const persistence = createRemixThemePersistence(myThemes, "light", { key: "my-theme-selection", }); ``` ---

title: createThemeDocument<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(config): ThemeDocumentHandle<T>
text: createThemeDocument<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(config): ThemeDocumentHandle<T> Create a single-source theme configuration for a server-rendered document. The returned `Document` renders the blocking bootstrap in `<head>`, the matching theme attributes and CSS variables on `<html>`, the scrollbar class and pre-paint stylesheet when configured, and the runtime provider around the application tree. `resolveInitial` derives the request-specific state from the same configuration, so the loader, the script, the shell and the provider cannot drift apart. **See also:** `ThemeDocumentConfig` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `config` | `ThemeDocumentConfig<T>` | The registry, fallback selection, static runtime options (`transition`, `scheduled`, `themeOverride`) and document options. | **Returns** `ThemeDocumentHandle<T>` — The document handle: `resolveInitial`, `Document`, `Provider`, `config` and the static `fallback`. The configuration is copied and frozen, so changing the caller's `themes` array later cannot change what an already-created document renders. Request state is never stored on the handle: `resolveInitial` derives it from the `Request` it is given, which keeps concurrent requests isolated. The handler imports the server resolver lazily. The client bundle therefore does not include the cookie parser, while the loader still gets a synchronous configuration it can call. ```ts // app/root.tsx — React Router Framework Mode import { createThemeDocument } from "@themvora/remix/react-router"; import { getBuiltInThemes } from "@themvora/core"; import type { Route } from "./+types/root"; const themes = getBuiltInThemes(); const theming = createThemeDocument({ themes, defaultTheme: "light", mode: "system", transition: { enabled: true, preset: "smooth" }, scrollbar: true, }); export async function loader({ request }: Route.LoaderArgs) { return { theme: await theming.resolveInitial(request) }; } export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { const data = useRouteLoaderData<typeof loader>("root"); return ( <theming.Document initial={data?.theme} head={[<Meta key="meta" />, <Links key="links" />]} afterContent={<><ScrollRestoration /><Scripts /></>} > {children} </theming.Document> ); } ``` ---

title: getThemeShellProps<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(initial, options): ThemeShellProps
text: getThemeShellProps<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(initial, options): ThemeShellProps The `<html>` attributes the pre-paint bootstrap script writes, as React props. Spread them onto the document element rendered by `app/root.tsx`. **See also:** `ThemeHead` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `initial` | `InitialThemeResolution<T>` | The SSR-resolved initial state from `getInitialThemeState`. | | `options` | `ThemeShellOptions` | Extra classes, the scrollbar opt-in, and extra inline styles. | **Returns** `ThemeShellProps` — The `<html>` props: the theme attributes, the CSS variables, and the hydration suppression. Every value here is a *snapshot* of the server's resolution, and it exists for one reason: **hydration parity**. The blocking script in `<ThemeHead>` rewrites all of it before first paint, so React's virtual DOM has to start out agreeing with the DOM, or React reports a hydration mismatch on `<html>` and — because it never patches attributes up — keeps a virtual DOM that disagrees with the document for the rest of the session. That is not hypothetical. A Remix app that renders a bare `<html lang="en">` hydrates against seven attributes it never rendered (`data-theme`, `data-theme-mode`, `data-theme-family`, `data-theme-selection-mode`, `data-theme-selection-family`, `data-theme-ready` and `style`), and React logs "some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client properties" on every load. Rendering the snapshot removes six of the seven; `suppressHydrationWarning` covers the last one, which cannot be removed by construction: `data-theme-mode` is the *resolved* mode, so a `"system"` selection resolved against a dark `prefers-color-scheme` legitimately differs from the server's `"light"`. The same goes for the `dark` class the script toggles, which is deliberately not rendered here — the script owns it. The suppression is scoped to the `<html>` element and its own attributes. It does not hide mismatches in the application tree, so a genuine hydration bug in a route still reports. ```ts import { getBuiltInThemes } from "@themvora/core"; import { ThemeHead, getThemeShellProps } from "@themvora/remix"; const themes = getBuiltInThemes(); export function Layout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) { const { initial } = useLoaderData<typeof loader>(); return ( <html lang="en" {...getThemeShellProps(initial, { scrollbar: true })}> <head> <ThemeHead themes={themes} defaultTheme="light" scrollbar /> </head> <body>{children}</body> </html> ); } ``` ---

title: ThemeHead<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element
text: ThemeHead<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element Renders the blocking theme bootstrap in the document `<head>`. Emits an inline script that reads the persisted theme cookies and applies the CSS variables plus DOM effects before first paint (zero-flash), plus a `prefers-color-scheme` dark-mode fallback when the selection is `"system"`. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `ThemeHeadProps` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeHeadProps<T>` | The head props (see ThemeHeadProps). | **Returns** `Element` — A fragment containing the blocking `<script>` and optional dark-mode `<style>`. Place this inside the document `<head>` so the script runs before the app stylesheets and the browser paints already themed. Pair with `ThemeProvider` and `getInitialThemeState` for the full SSR-first setup. ```ts import { ThemeHead } from "@themvora/remix"; export function Layout({ children }) { return ( // `tv-scrollbar` must be rendered here, not added by a script. <html className="tv-scrollbar"> <head> <ThemeHead themes={myThemes} defaultTheme="light" scrollbar /> </head> <body>{children}</body> </html> ); } ``` ---

title: ThemeInspector(namedParameters?): Element
text: ThemeInspector(namedParameters?): Element A floating developer tool that inspects the active theme. Renders a fixed toggle button and an expandable panel showing the current theme name, family, mode, selection state, token values, and emitted CSS variables — useful while building themeable UI. **See also:** `useTheme` **Returns** `Element` The panel opens above the toggle with a gap, stays dismissible via the toggle, `Escape`, or clicking outside, and matches the provider's transition duration for its own fade. ```ts <ThemeInspector /> ``` ---

title: ThemeProvider<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element
text: ThemeProvider<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element Remix theme provider. Mounts the client theme runtime, wires the cookie persistence adapter, and — when an SSR-resolved `initial` state is supplied — mirrors the selection back to cookies so the server resolves the same state on the next request (zero-flash). **See also:** `ThemeHead`, `createRemixThemePersistence`, `ThemeProviderProps` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeProviderProps<T>` | The provider props (see ThemeProviderProps). | **Returns** `Element` — The provider tree wrapping the application content. Pair with `ThemeHead` in the document `<head>` and `getInitialThemeState` in the loader for the full SSR-first, zero-flash setup. When `initial` is omitted, the persisted selection is read on the client from `localStorage` and then from the theme cookies `ThemeHead`'s script reads — see ThemeProviderProps.initial for the hydration caveat. ```ts import { ThemeProvider } from "@themvora/remix"; export default function App({ children }) { return ( <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light" themes={myThemes}> {children} </ThemeProvider> ); } ``` ---

title: ThemeScope(namedParameters): Element
text: ThemeScope(namedParameters): Element Applies a theme to a subtree without replacing the global runtime. The scope resolves local themes (`themes` prop) before falling back to the parent runtime's theme registry. Nested scopes override their parent within their own boundary. Theme changes are reactive: `theme`/`family`/`mode` props and global mode changes re-resolve and animate in place without remounting. **See also:** `useScopedTheme` **Returns** `Element` Scope-local transitions inherit the parent transition configuration unless explicitly overridden or disabled. First paint is server-safe: explicit selections ship resolved variables inline, while OS-dependent selections (system mode / family-following scopes) ship no inline variables plus a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` override, so no flash occurs. ```ts <ThemeScope family="plum" mode="dark"> <Editor /> </ThemeScope> ``` ---

title: ThemeScrollbar(props): null
text: ThemeScrollbar(props): null ThemeScrollbar — overlay only. Creates the custom scrollbar overlay. Lifecycle: mount → create overlay → measure → attach listeners paint → add tv-scrollbar-ready destroy → remove overlay Props are four optional groups — `behavior`, `appearance`, `scope` and `icons` — plus `children`, which is accepted for JSX symmetry only. <ThemeScrollbar behavior={{ autoHide: true, smooth: true }} appearance={{ thickness: 8, radius: 999 }} scope={{ include: [".panel"] }} icons={{ up: <ArrowUpIcon />, size: 12 }} /> <ThemeScrollbar behavior={{ autoHide: true, smooth: true }} appearance={{ thickness: 8, radius: 999 }} icons={{ up: <ArrowUpIcon />, down: <ArrowDownIcon /> }} /> **See also:** `ThemeProvider` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeScrollbarProps` | — | **Returns** `null` ---

title: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): T
text: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): T The theme produced by `generateTheme()` and registered with the provider. Returns the registered theme that carries the generator's origin marker (`meta.generation.kind === "generated"`) — never a shipped preset, and never inferred from a theme's id, family or colors. Generate one and pass the result to `ThemeProvider`: ```tsx const generated = generateTheme({ seed: "#635BFF", family: "brand" }); <ThemeProvider themes={[generated.light, generated.dark]}>{children}</ThemeProvider> ``` When both halves of one `generateTheme()` call are registered, the theme the active selection resolves to is returned. If several generated themes are registered and none is active, the call throws rather than guessing. Throws `ThemeError` with code `TV_GENERATION_THEME_NOT_FOUND` when the provider holds no generated theme, and `TV_GENERATION_THEME_AMBIGUOUS` when several are registered and the active selection does not identify one. Re-resolves on every settled change to the registry, store, or selection; if the generated theme is later removed, the same error is raised at the next render rather than a stale theme being returned. **See also:** `useThemeValue` **Returns** `T` — The registered generated theme. ---

title: useProvidedThemes<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): readonly ProvidedThemeFamily<T>[]
text:
useProvidedThemes>(): readonly ProvidedThemeFamily[] The themes this provider was given, grouped by family. Returns exactly the collection supplied to the nearest `ThemeProvider` — not the built-in catalog, and not every theme that exists in the project. Build a theme picker from it instead of enumerating a separate preset source: ```tsx const themes = useProvidedThemes(); return themes.map((family) => (

{family.name}

{family.variants.map((variant) => ( ))}
)); ``` The collection is reactive: a `themes` prop change, a `runtime.use(pack)` install or a registry mutation re-renders the consumer. Entries keep their identity while their content is unchanged, so `React.memo` and dependency arrays behave. **See also:** `useTheme`, `normalizeProvidedThemes` **Returns** `readonly ProvidedThemeFamily[]` — The provider's theme families, in supplied order. ---

title: useTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { effectiveMode: "light" | "dark"; family: string; mode: ThemeMode; setFamily: type(family: ThemeFamilies<readonly T[]>): void; setMode: type(mode: ModesOf<T>): void; theme: T; toggleTheme: type(): void }
text: useTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { effectiveMode: "light" | "dark"; family: string; mode: ThemeMode; setFamily: type(family: ThemeFamilies<readonly T[]>): void; setMode: type(mode: ModesOf<T>): void; theme: T; toggleTheme: type(): void } The primary Themvora hook. Returns the current theme, mode, family and the selection controls. When you pass the theme tuple element type, `setFamily` and `setMode` are constrained to the families/modes defined in your registry (the built-in set is used below so the example stands alone): ```ts import { getBuiltInThemes } from "@themvora/core"; const themes = getBuiltInThemes(); const { theme, mode, family, setMode, setFamily, toggleTheme } = useTheme<typeof themes[number]>(); setFamily("mint"); // autocomplete suggests your families setMode("dark"); ``` **See also:** `useThemeValue`, `useThemeMode`, `useEffectiveThemeMode`, `useThemeFamily` **Returns** `{ effectiveMode: "light" | "dark"; family: string; mode: ThemeMode; setFamily: __type(family: ThemeFamilies<readonly T[]>): void; setMode: __type(mode: ModesOf<T>): void; theme: T; toggleTheme: __type(): void }` ---

text: useThemeHistory(): { canRedo: boolean; canUndo: boolean; clear: type(): void; redo: type(): void; undo: type(): void } Subscribe to the runtime history (undo/redo/canUndo/canRedo/clear). **See also:** `useThemeTimeTravel` **Returns** `{ canRedo: boolean; canUndo: boolean; clear: __type(): void; redo: __type(): void; undo: __type(): void }` ---

title: useThemeLifecycle<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { on: type<K extends keyof ThemeLifecycleEventMap<ThemeDefinition<string>>>(event: K, listener: type(data: ThemeLifecycleEventMap<T>[K]): void): type(): void }
text: useThemeLifecycle<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { on: type<K extends keyof ThemeLifecycleEventMap<ThemeDefinition<string>>>(event: K, listener: type(data: ThemeLifecycleEventMap<T>[K]): void): type(): void } Subscribe to runtime lifecycle events (theme changed, mode changed, …). The handler is typed per event name, so `on("beforeThemeChange", ({ next }) => …)` gives you the theme definitions rather than `unknown` — the same precision `runtime.lifecycle.on` has in `@themvora/core`. **See also:** `useTheme` **Returns** `{ on: __type<K extends keyof ThemeLifecycleEventMap<ThemeDefinition<string>>>(event: K, listener: __type(data: ThemeLifecycleEventMap<T>[K]): void): __type(): void }` ---

title: useThemeMode(): ThemeMode
text: useThemeMode(): ThemeMode Subscribe to the current selection mode ("light" | "dark" | "system"). This is the mode the visitor **asked for**. While a sunrise/sunset schedule is running, or while the selection is `"system"`, the appearance on screen can differ from it — use useEffectiveThemeMode to display what is actually applied. **See also:** `useEffectiveThemeMode`, `useSetThemeMode` **Returns** `ThemeMode` ---

title: useThemePacks(): type(pack: ThemePack<any>): void
text: useThemePacks(): type(pack: ThemePack<any>): void Get a function that applies a theme pack to the runtime. **See also:** `useTheme` **Returns** `__type(pack: ThemePack<any>): void` ---

title: useThemeRestore(): type(snapshot: ThemeRuntimeSnapshot): void
text: useThemeRestore(): type(snapshot: ThemeRuntimeSnapshot): void Get a restore function that re-applies a previously captured snapshot. **See also:** `useThemeSnapshot` **Returns** `__type(snapshot: ThemeRuntimeSnapshot): void` ---

title: useThemeRuntime<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): ThemeRuntime<T>
text: useThemeRuntime<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): ThemeRuntime<T> Get the active Themvora runtime from context. Throws when used outside a `ThemeProvider`. Pass the theme tuple element type to type the runtime's store/selection against your registry — any registry works, so the built-in set is used here to keep the example self-contained: ```ts import { getBuiltInThemes } from "@themvora/core"; const themes = getBuiltInThemes(); const runtime = useThemeRuntime<typeof themes[number]>(); ``` **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `useTheme` **Returns** `ThemeRuntime<T>` ---

title: useThemeSchedule(): ThemeSchedule | null
text: useThemeSchedule(): ThemeSchedule | null Reactive access to the runtime's sunrise/sunset scheduling controller. Requires the runtime to be created with the `scheduled` option (see `ThemeProvider` / `createThemeRuntime`). Returns `null` when the provider has no schedule configured. ```tsx const schedule = useThemeSchedule(); schedule?.enable(); schedule?.disable(); // schedule.enabled, schedule.active, schedule.sunrise, schedule.sunset, // schedule.nextTransition ... re-render reactively. ``` **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `useTheme` **Returns** `ThemeSchedule | null` The returned controller is a **reactive view**: its state reads come from the subscription below, not from the live controller. That is what makes it safe to render during SSR — the subscription hydrates from EMPTY_THEME_SCHEDULE_STATE, the same snapshot the server rendered, and only adopts the live state after mount. Returning the raw controller instead (which is what this hook used to do, discarding the subscription it had just created) handed consumers the *live* value during the hydration render, so React saw a mismatch against the server HTML and re-rendered the tree. ---

title: useThemeSnapshot(): type(): ThemeRuntimeSnapshot
text: useThemeSnapshot(): type(): ThemeRuntimeSnapshot Get a snapshot function that captures the full runtime state. **See also:** `useThemeRestore` **Returns** `__type(): ThemeRuntimeSnapshot` ---

title: ThemeDocumentConfig<T extends ThemeDefinition>
text: ThemeDocumentConfig<T extends ThemeDefinition> The one description of a document-level theme installation. Every value here is static: it does not depend on the incoming request, so a module can declare one configuration and use it for the pre-paint script, the server-rendered `<html>` element and the client runtime. The request-specific result is the `initial` state produced by ThemeDocumentHandle.resolveInitial. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `bodyClassName` (optional) | `string` | Classes rendered on `<body>`. | | `bodyStyle` (optional) | `CSSProperties` | Inline styles rendered on `<body>`. | | `className` (optional) | `string` | Classes merged onto the `<html>` element alongside the theme's own. | | `defaultTheme` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Fallback theme when no selection is persisted. Accepts a theme **name** or a **family**; a family resolves to the variant for the mode in effect. | | `family` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Family used when nothing is persisted and `defaultTheme` names no family. A variant name is normalised to its family. | | `initialFamily` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Alias for ThemeDocumentConfig.family, matching the name the Remix provider prop has always used. `family` wins when both are supplied. | | `initialMode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Alias for ThemeDocumentConfig.mode, matching the name the Remix provider prop has always used. `mode` wins when both are supplied. | | `mode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Mode used when neither a persisted selection nor `themeOverride` applies. Defaults to the fallback theme's own mode. Pass `"system"` to follow `prefers-color-scheme` instead. | | `scheduled` (optional) | `false \| ScheduledThemeOptions<T>` | The solar schedule passed to the runtime, so light/dark can follow the visitor's sunrise and sunset. The document still resolves and paints the persisted selection; the schedule takes over once the runtime mounts. | | `scrollbar` (optional) | `boolean` | Hide the native scrollbar from the very first paint. Adds the `tv-scrollbar` class to `<html>` and emits the pre-paint hiding stylesheet. The application still imports `@themvora/core/scrollbar.css` itself: a CSS import is a bundler concern, not something a component can inject. | | `style` (optional) | `CSSProperties` | Inline styles merged after the theme's CSS variables on `<html>`. | | `themeOverride` (optional) | `ThemeOverride<ThemeIdentifier<T>>` | An explicit theme override applied over any persisted selection. The pre-paint script, the shell and the runtime all receive the same value. | | `themes` | `readonly T[]` | The theme registry the selection is resolved against. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition configuration passed to the runtime: `true`, `false`, or `{ enabled, duration, easing, preset, … }`. Same contract as the Remix provider's `transition` prop, so a document-level setup can express animations without falling back to the lower-level `ThemeProvider`. | ---

Used by `Document` when `initial` is missing or `null`. | | `Document` | `ReactElement` | — | | `Provider` | `ReactElement` | — | | `resolveInitial` | `Promise<InitialThemeResolution<T>>` | — | ---

title: ThemeDocumentProps<T extends ThemeDefinition>
text: ThemeDocumentProps<T extends ThemeDefinition> Props for the document component created by createThemeDocument. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `afterContent` (optional) | `ReactNode` | Framework body-end content (for example `<ScrollRestoration />` and `<Scripts />`). | | `bodyProps` (optional) | `ThemeDocumentBodyProps` | Extra props for `<body>`; see ThemeDocumentBodyProps. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | The application tree rendered inside the theme provider. | | `head` (optional) | `readonly ThemeDocumentHeadContent[]` | Framework head content, as an array of head elements. Only head-valid intrinsic elements (`meta`, `link`, `title`, `style`, `script`, `base`, `noscript`, `template`) and components such as React Router's `<Meta />`/`<Links />` are accepted. The array is deliberate: React 19 types every JSX expression as `ReactElement<any, any>`, so invalid children inside `<>…</>` would slip through. The array rejects a fragment at the prop boundary; an invalid intrinsic element that reaches the array is rejected with a clear error when the document renders. | | `htmlProps` (optional) | `ThemeDocumentHtmlProps` | Extra props for `<html>`. Theme-owned attributes win over the same keys here. See ThemeDocumentHtmlProps for the documented `lang`, `className`, `style` and `dir` behaviour. | | `initial` (optional) | `InitialThemeResolution<T> \| null` | The request-resolved state from ThemeDocumentHandle.resolveInitial. Optional on purpose: React Router can render the root `Layout` while the root loader is unavailable (an error response, a hydration fallback). When it is missing or `null`, the document renders the configuration's static fallback instead of throwing a second error inside the boundary. | ---

title: ThemeHeadProps<T extends ThemeDefinition>
text: ThemeHeadProps<T extends ThemeDefinition> Props for the Remix `ThemeHead` component. Describes the theme registry and the fallback selection used to build the blocking bootstrap script and the dark-mode CSS fallback. **See also:** `ThemeProvider` | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `defaultTheme` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Fallback theme name when no selection is persisted. | | `mode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Fallback mode when no selection is persisted. Defaults to the fallback theme's own mode — whatever `defaultTheme` resolves to. Pass `"system"` to follow `prefers-color-scheme` instead, and give `ThemeProvider` the matching `initialMode` so the script and the runtime resolve the same theme on a first visit. Leaving the two out of step produces a wrong-theme flash: the script paints one theme and the runtime corrects it. | | `scrollbar` (optional) | `boolean` | Hide the native scrollbar from the very first paint, so the Themvora overlay (`ThemeScrollbar`) is the only scrollbar from frame one — no native-bar-then-overlay swap while the bundle hydrates. Defaults to `false`. | | `themeOverride` (optional) | `ThemeOverride<ThemeIdentifier<T>>` | An explicit theme override, applied by the pre-paint script over any persisted selection. Pass the same value given to ThemeProvider. | | `themes` | `readonly T[]` | The theme registry the blocking script resolves against. | ---

title: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition>
text: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition> Props for the Remix `ThemeProvider`. Configures the theme registry, the fallback selection, and the optional SSR-resolved initial state. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `ThemeHead` | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `children` | `ReactNode` | The application content rendered inside the provider. | | `defaultTheme` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Fallback theme when no selection is persisted. Accepts a supplied theme **name** (`"cocoa-light"`) or a **family** (`"cocoa"`); a family resolves to the variant for the mode in effect. | | `initial` (optional) | `InitialThemeResolution<T>` | The SSR-resolved initial theme state (from `getInitialThemeState`). When provided, it wins on first paint so hydration matches exactly and the selection is mirrored back to cookies. | | `initialFamily` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Family used when neither `initial` nor a persisted selection is available. Pair it with `initialMode` for the same reason. Constrained to the identifiers in `themes` when they are statically known. A variant name is accepted and normalised to its family; its mode applies only when `initialMode` is absent. | | `initialMode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Mode used when neither `initial` nor a persisted selection is available. Optional: the runtime and `ThemeHead`'s script both derive the fallback mode from `defaultTheme` by default, so they already agree. Set this to pin a mode the script would not derive — e.g. `"system"` to follow `prefers-color-scheme` — and pass the same value to `ThemeHead`. Ignored when `initial` is provided, since the SSR resolution wins. | | `scheduled` (optional) | `false \| ScheduledThemeOptions<T>` | Sunrise/sunset schedule forwarded to the runtime. Same contract as `@themvora/react`'s provider; `createThemeDocument()` forwards its `scheduled` option through this prop. | | `themeOverride` (optional) | `ThemeOverride<ThemeIdentifier<T>>` | An explicit theme override applied over any persisted selection. Applied once per value, never written to the theme cookies, and it does not fight a later manual selection. For a flash-free override, pass the same value to ThemeHead so the pre-paint script resolves it too. | | `themes` (optional) | `readonly T[]` | The theme registry the selection is resolved against. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition configuration forwarded to the runtime: `true`, `false`, or `{ enabled, duration, easing, preset, … }`. Same contract as `@themvora/react`'s provider. `createThemeDocument()` forwards its `transition` option through this prop, so the new single-configuration API can express everything the provider accepts. | ---

title: ThemeScrollbarProps
text: ThemeScrollbarProps Props for the ThemeScrollbar overlay component. Options are grouped into `behavior`, `appearance`, and `icons` — but every option is also accepted as a flat, top-level prop (flat props win over the grouped ones). | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `appearance` (optional) | `ThemeScrollbarAppearance` | The look and size of every rail. | | `behavior` (optional) | `ThemeScrollbarBehavior` | How the overlay scrolls and hides. | | `children` (optional) | `ReactNode` | Renders nothing visible; kept for API symmetry (the overlay is created against the runtime, not the component tree). It is deliberately ignored by option resolution and change detection. | | `icons` (optional) | `ThemeScrollbarIcons` | Arrow button icons, plus the shared glyph size. | | `scope` (optional) | `ThemeScrollbarScope` | Which scrollable containers the overlay tracks. | ---

title: ThemeShellOptions
text: ThemeShellOptions Extra props merged onto the shell attributes computed by getThemeShellProps. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `className` (optional) | `string` | Classes rendered on `<html>` alongside the theme's own. Kept stable across renders: the overlay scrollbar engine adds `tv-scrollbar-ready` to the same attribute, and React rewrites `class` wholesale whenever the prop it was given changes — which would take the engine's marker with it and leave the overlay permanently faded out. | | `scrollbar` (optional) | `boolean` | Render the `tv-scrollbar` class, so the pre-paint stylesheet hides the native bar from the first frame. Pair it with `scrollbar` on ThemeHead: the class scopes the CSS and the CSS does the hiding, so either half alone does nothing. This is the Remix-side equivalent of `@themvora/next`'s `scrollbar` prop — Remix owns the document, so the class has to come from the layout. | | `style` (optional) | `CSSProperties` | Inline styles merged after the theme's CSS variables. | ---

title: ThemeShellProps
text: ThemeShellProps The `<html>` props produced by getThemeShellProps: the theme attributes and CSS variables the pre-paint script writes, plus the hydration suppression that covers the parts of them the server cannot know. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `className` (optional) | `string` | Extra classes, plus `tv-scrollbar` when `scrollbar` was requested. | | `data-theme` | `string` | The resolved theme's name, as `data-theme`. | | `data-theme-family` (optional) | `string` | The resolved theme's family, when it declares one. | | `data-theme-mode` | `"light" \| "dark"` | The resolved mode (`light` / `dark`) the theme was painted with. | | `data-theme-ready` | `"true"` | Completion marker: the bootstrap ran, so the document is themed. | | `data-theme-selection-family` (optional) | `string` | The visitor's chosen family, when one was resolved. | | `data-theme-selection-mode` | `ThemeMode` | The visitor's chosen mode, which `"system"` is not reduced from. | | `style` | `CSSProperties` | `color-scheme` plus the resolved theme's `--theme-*` variables. | | `suppressHydrationWarning` | `true` | Suppresses React's attribute diff for this element only. Always `true`. | Assignable to a React `<html>` element by construction — spread it and add the app's own props (`lang`, a `className`) around it. ---

title: ThemeDocumentHeadContent
text: ThemeDocumentHeadContent Framework head content accepted by `<theming.Document head={[…]}>`. `head` is an **array**, not a fragment. React 19 types every JSX expression as `ReactElement<any, any>`, so TypeScript cannot distinguish `<div>` from `<meta>` by element type. The array rejects fragments at the prop boundary; the document then validates the rendered tree and throws a descriptive error for an invalid intrinsic element such as `<div>`. `ThemeDocumentHeadElement | readonly ThemeDocumentHeadContent[] | string | number | boolean | null | undefined` ---

title: createShadcnAdapter<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): ThemeAdapter<T>
text: createShadcnAdapter<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): ThemeAdapter<T> Creates a shadcn/ui adapter. The adapter is a DOM-only, framework-free adapter: it depends only on `@themvora/core` and the DOM. On install it injects the shadcn/ui compatibility stylesheet (when enabled) and a `<style>` element of CSS variables derived from the active theme, then subscribes to the runtime store and rewrites the variables whenever the theme selection changes. It does not render any component or require a React tree. On uninstall it removes the injected styles and unsubscribes from the store. **See also:** `useShadcnTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `CreateShadcnAdapterOptions` | Adapter options. Defaults to `{}`. | **Returns** `ThemeAdapter<T>` — A `ThemeAdapter` for shadcn/ui. ```ts import { createShadcnAdapter } from "@themvora/shadcn"; runtime.adapters.use(createShadcnAdapter()); ``` ---

title: useShadcnTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(runtime, options): ThemeAdapter<T>
text: useShadcnTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(runtime, options): ThemeAdapter<T> Vue composable that installs the shadcn/ui adapter onto the given Themvora runtime. title: createShadcnAdapter<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): ThemeAdapter<T>
text: createShadcnAdapter<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): ThemeAdapter<T> Creates a shadcn/ui adapter. The adapter is a DOM-only, framework-free adapter: it depends only on `@themvora/core` and the DOM. On install it injects the shadcn/ui compatibility stylesheet (when enabled) and a `<style>` element of CSS variables derived from the active theme, then subscribes to the runtime store and rewrites the variables whenever the theme selection changes. It does not render any component or require a React tree. On uninstall it removes the injected styles and unsubscribes from the store. **See also:** `useShadcnTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `CreateShadcnAdapterOptions` | Adapter options. Defaults to `{}`. | **Returns** `ThemeAdapter<T>` — A `ThemeAdapter` for shadcn/ui. ```ts import { createShadcnAdapter } from "@themvora/shadcn"; runtime.adapters.use(createShadcnAdapter()); ``` ---

title: createSolidThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string
text: createSolidThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string Build the blocking zero-flash `<head>` script for a SolidJS app (SSR or SPA). Inlines core's `createThemeBootstrapScript` with the Solid defaults (`storageKey: "theme-selection"`, `prefix: "theme-"` — the same values the Solid `ThemeProvider` persistence and CSS variables use), so the persisted theme is applied before first paint. Emit the returned string as a blocking `<script>` inside `<head>`. **See also:** ``createThemeBootstrapScript`` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeBootstrapScriptOptions<T>` | — | **Returns** `string` ---

title: ThemeInspector(props): Element
text: ThemeInspector(props): Element Renders the floating theme inspector for the active runtime. Defines and mounts the `<themvora-inspector>` custom element, forwarding the given position, size, z-index, `class`, and `style` props. The inspector reads the active theme from the runtime and lets users inspect and switch themes at runtime. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `useTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeInspectorProps` | The inspector configuration. | **Returns** `Element` ---

title: ThemeProvider<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element
text: ThemeProvider<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(props): Element Provides a ThemeRuntime to the Solid component tree via context. When no `runtime` prop is given the provider creates and owns a runtime from the remaining ThemeProviderProps (which extend ThemeRuntimeOptions), wiring up DOM and CSS-variable bindings on mount and destroying the runtime on cleanup. When a `runtime` prop is supplied the provider adopts that caller-owned runtime and does not destroy it. Renders no DOM of its own — it only supplies context to its children. **See also:** `useTheme`, `ThemeScope`, `useThemeRuntime` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeProviderProps<T>` | The provider options and children. | **Returns** `Element` The provider must be mounted before any hook that reads the runtime (`useTheme`, `useThemeRuntime`, …) is called, since those hooks throw when no provider context exists. On the server the provider renders its children without DOM bindings; the persisted selection is applied client-side before first paint via an injected bootstrap script. ```ts import { ThemeProvider } from "@themvora/solid"; function App() { return ( <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light"> <YourApp /> </ThemeProvider> ); } ``` ---

title: ThemeScope(props): Element
text: ThemeScope(props): Element Creates a nested theme boundary that overrides the selection for its subtree. Renders a wrapper `<div>` carrying the resolved theme's `data-theme`, `data-mode`, and CSS-variable inline styles, and keeps it in sync as the scope's props or the provider's selection change. On the server no wrapper is rendered — the children are returned directly so the provider's `:root` attributes apply client-side. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `useTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeScopeProps` | The scope configuration and children. | **Returns** `Element` The scope does not create a second runtime; it resolves against the provider's theme registry, with any `themes` prop shadowing same-named parent themes. Family-based and boundary-only scopes follow the provider's live mode, flipping light/dark when the global mode changes. ---

title: ThemeScrollbar(props): null
text: ThemeScrollbar(props): null Applies an overlay scrollbar to the runtime's scrollable content. Installs an overlay scrollbar bound to the active theme's store on mount and destroys it on cleanup. Renders no DOM of its own — it returns `null` and only manages the scrollbar lifecycle for the surrounding content. **See also:** `ThemeProvider` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `props` | `ThemeScrollbarProps` | The scrollbar options and children. | **Returns** `null` ---

title: useEffectiveThemeMode(): Accessor<"light" | "dark">
text: useEffectiveThemeMode(): Accessor<"light" | "dark"> Reactive access to the mode actually **applied** — `"light"` or `"dark"`, never `"system"` — as a Solid signal. Render this when a control states the current appearance. useThemeMode reports what the visitor asked for: it stays `"system"` while that choice stands and it does not move at a sunrise/sunset transition, so a label bound to it kept announcing the old mode while the page changed colour. **See also:** `useThemeMode`, `useThemeSchedule` **Returns** `Accessor<"light" | "dark">` — A Solid signal holding the applied mode. ---

title: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): Accessor<T>
text: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): Accessor<T> Reactive access to the theme produced by `generateTheme()` and registered with the provider, as a Solid signal. Resolves the registered theme that carries the generator's origin marker (`meta.generation.kind === "generated"`); shipped presets never qualify. When both halves of one `generateTheme()` call are registered, the signal tracks the theme the active selection resolves to. The subscription is disposed on component cleanup. Throws `ThemeError` with code `TV_GENERATION_THEME_NOT_FOUND` when the provider holds no generated theme, and `TV_GENERATION_THEME_AMBIGUOUS` when several are registered and the active selection does not identify one. Re-resolves on every settled change to the registry, store, or selection; if the generated theme is later removed, the same error is raised at the next reactive read rather than a stale theme being returned. **See also:** `useThemeValue` **Returns** `Accessor<T>` — A Solid signal holding the registered generated theme. ---

title: useProvidedThemes<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): Accessor<readonly ProvidedThemeFamily<T>[]>
text:
useProvidedThemes>(): Accessor[]> Reactive access to the themes this provider was given, grouped by family. Returns exactly the collection supplied to the nearest `ThemeProvider` — not the built-in catalog. The accessor tracks the provider's registry, so a `themes` prop change, a theme-pack install or a registry mutation re-runs every consumer of it, and the array instance is stable while nothing changes. ```tsx const families = useProvidedThemes(); {(family) =>

{family.name}

} ``` **See also:** `useThemeValue` **Returns** `Accessor[]>` — An accessor holding the provider's theme families. ---

title: useTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { effectiveMode: Accessor<"light" | "dark">; family: Accessor<string>; mode: Accessor<ThemeMode>; setFamily: type(nextFamily: string): void; setMode: type(nextMode: ThemeMode): void; theme: Accessor<T>; toggleTheme: type(): void }
text: useTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { effectiveMode: Accessor<"light" | "dark">; family: Accessor<string>; mode: Accessor<ThemeMode>; setFamily: type(nextFamily: string): void; setMode: type(nextMode: ThemeMode): void; theme: Accessor<T>; toggleTheme: type(): void } Reactive access to the current theme selection plus actions to change it. Combines the reactive signals from `useThemeValue`, `useThemeMode`, `useEffectiveThemeMode` and `useThemeFamily` with imperative setters that drive the runtime selection. Must be called inside a component rendered within a `ThemeProvider`. `mode` is the visitor's request; `effectiveMode` is what is on screen — they differ while a sunrise/sunset schedule runs, or while the selection is `"system"`. **See also:** `useThemeValue`, `useThemeMode`, `useEffectiveThemeMode`, `useThemeFamily` **Returns** `{ effectiveMode: Accessor<"light" | "dark">; family: Accessor<string>; mode: Accessor<ThemeMode>; setFamily: __type(nextFamily: string): void; setMode: __type(nextMode: ThemeMode): void; theme: Accessor<T>; toggleTheme: __type(): void }` — An object with reactive `theme`, `mode`, `effectiveMode` and `family` signals and the `setMode`, `setFamily`, and `toggleTheme` actions. ```ts import { useTheme } from "@themvora/solid"; function ThemeToggle() { const { effectiveMode, toggleTheme } = useTheme(); return ( <button onClick={toggleTheme}> Current mode: {effectiveMode()} </button> ); } ``` ---

title: useThemeBatch(): type(callback: type(): void): void
text: useThemeBatch(): type(callback: type(): void): void Returns a function that batches multiple runtime mutations into a single store update. The returned callback forwards to the runtime's `batch` method, coalescing several selection changes so subscribers observe one consolidated change. **See also:** `useThemeRuntime`, `useTheme` **Returns** `__type(callback: __type(): void): void` — A function accepting a callback whose mutations are batched. ---

title: useThemeFamily(): Accessor<string>
text: useThemeFamily(): Accessor<string> Reactive access to the current theme family as a Solid signal. Returns a signal tracking the runtime selection's theme family name. The signal is seeded on mount and kept in sync with the store; the subscription is disposed on component cleanup. **See also:** `useTheme` **Returns** `Accessor<string>` — A Solid signal holding the current theme family name. ---

title: useThemeHistory<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { clear: type(): void; jump: type(index: number): void; redo: type(): void; undo: type(): void; canRedo: void; canUndo: void; history: void }
text: useThemeHistory<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { clear: type(): void; jump: type(index: number): void; redo: type(): void; undo: type(): void; canRedo: void; canUndo: void; history: void } Reactive access to the runtime's theme history (undo/redo). Returns reactive `canUndo`, `canRedo`, and `history` getters plus the `undo`, `redo`, `clear`, and `jump` actions. The reactive state is seeded on mount and refreshed whenever the store changes; the subscription is disposed on component cleanup. **See also:** `useThemeRuntime`, `useThemeBatch` **Returns** `{ clear: __type(): void; jump: __type(index: number): void; redo: __type(): void; undo: __type(): void; canRedo: void; canUndo: void; history: void }` — An object exposing the history state and navigation actions. ---

title: useThemeLifecycle(): { on: type(event: keyof ThemeLifecycleEventMap<ThemeDefinition<string>>, listener: type(data: unknown): void): type(): void }
text: useThemeLifecycle(): { on: type(event: keyof ThemeLifecycleEventMap<ThemeDefinition<string>>, listener: type(data: unknown): void): type(): void } Returns a function that subscribes to runtime lifecycle events. The returned `on` callback forwards to the runtime's lifecycle emitter, registering a listener for the given ThemeLifecycleEventName. **See also:** `useThemeRuntime`, `useTheme` **Returns** `{ on: __type(event: keyof ThemeLifecycleEventMap<ThemeDefinition<string>>, listener: __type(data: unknown): void): __type(): void }` — An object exposing an `on` function to register lifecycle listeners. ---

title: useThemeMode(): Accessor<ThemeMode>
text: useThemeMode(): Accessor<ThemeMode> Reactive access to the current theme mode as a Solid signal. Returns a signal tracking the runtime selection's mode (`light`, `dark`, or `system`). The signal is seeded on mount and kept in sync with the store; the subscription is disposed on component cleanup. **See also:** `useTheme` **Returns** `Accessor<ThemeMode>` — A Solid signal holding the current theme mode. ---

title: useThemePacks(): type(pack: ThemePack<any>): void
text: useThemePacks(): type(pack: ThemePack<any>): void Returns a function that installs a theme pack onto the runtime. The returned callback forwards to the runtime's `use` method, registering a ThemePack so its themes become available to the selection. **See also:** `useThemeRuntime`, `useTheme` **Returns** `__type(pack: ThemePack<any>): void` — A function accepting a theme pack to install. ---

title: useThemeRestore(): type(snapshot: ThemeRuntimeSnapshot): void
text: useThemeRestore(): type(snapshot: ThemeRuntimeSnapshot): void Returns a function that restores the runtime from a previously captured snapshot. The returned callback forwards to the runtime's `restore` method, applying the given ThemeRuntimeSnapshot back onto the runtime. **See also:** `useThemeSnapshot` **Returns** `__type(snapshot: ThemeRuntimeSnapshot): void` — A function accepting a snapshot to restore. ---

title: useThemeRuntime<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): ThemeRuntime<T>
text: useThemeRuntime<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): ThemeRuntime<T> Returns the active ThemeRuntime from the nearest ThemeProvider. Must be called inside a component (owner) rendered within a `ThemeProvider`; otherwise it throws. The returned runtime is the same object the provider owns or adopts, so it is not reactive by itself — use the dedicated hooks (`useThemeValue`, `useThemeMode`, …) for reactive reads. **See also:** `ThemeProvider`, `useThemeValue` **Returns** `ThemeRuntime<T>` — The active theme runtime. ---

title: useThemeSchedule<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { disable: type(): void; enable: type(): void; set: type(options: ThemeScheduleSetOptions): void; active: void; darkTheme: void; enabled: void; lightTheme: void; nextActivation: void; nextDeactivation: void; nextTransition: void; status: void; sunrise: void; sunset: void } | null
text: useThemeSchedule<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { disable: type(): void; enable: type(): void; set: type(options: ThemeScheduleSetOptions): void; active: void; darkTheme: void; enabled: void; lightTheme: void; nextActivation: void; nextDeactivation: void; nextTransition: void; status: void; sunrise: void; sunset: void } | null Reactive access to the runtime's sunrise/sunset scheduling controller. Returns `null` when the provider was created without the `scheduled` option. Reads of `enabled`/`active`/`status`/`sunrise`/`sunset`/`nextTransition` track the underlying state reactively. ```tsx const schedule = useThemeSchedule(); schedule?.enable(); schedule?.disable(); ``` **Returns** `{ disable: __type(): void; enable: __type(): void; set: __type(options: ThemeScheduleSetOptions): void; active: void; darkTheme: void; enabled: void; lightTheme: void; nextActivation: void; nextDeactivation: void; nextTransition: void; status: void; sunrise: void; sunset: void } | null` ---

title: useThemeSnapshot(): type(): ThemeRuntimeSnapshot<ThemeDefinition<string>>
text: useThemeSnapshot(): type(): ThemeRuntimeSnapshot<ThemeDefinition<string>> Returns a function that captures the runtime's current state as a snapshot. The returned callback forwards to the runtime's `snapshot` method, producing a ThemeRuntimeSnapshot that can later be passed to `useThemeRestore`. **See also:** `useThemeRestore` **Returns** `__type(): ThemeRuntimeSnapshot<ThemeDefinition<string>>` — A function returning the current runtime snapshot. ---

title: useThemeTokens<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): Accessor<ThemeTokens | undefined>
text: useThemeTokens<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): Accessor<ThemeTokens | undefined> Reactive access to the active theme's token group as a Solid signal. Returns a signal whose value is the `tokens` object of the current theme selection, or `undefined` when the active theme defines no tokens. The signal updates whenever the store's theme changes and the subscription is disposed on component cleanup. **See also:** `useThemeValue` **Returns** `Accessor<ThemeTokens | undefined>` — A Solid signal holding the active theme's tokens. ---

title: useThemeValue<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): Accessor<T>
text: useThemeValue<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): Accessor<T> Reactive access to the current theme selection as a Solid signal. Returns a signal whose value tracks the runtime store's active theme. The signal is seeded from the store on mount and updated on every store change; the subscription is disposed automatically when the owning component is cleaned up. **See also:** `useTheme`, `useThemeRuntime` **Returns** `Accessor<T>` — A Solid signal holding the active theme. ---
