title: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition>
text: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition> **Extends** `ThemeRuntimeOptions<T>` Props accepted by ThemeProvider. Extends ThemeRuntimeOptions so the provider can build and own a runtime from the same options used by `createThemeRuntime`. When `runtime` is supplied the provider adopts that caller-owned runtime instead of creating one. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `adapters` (optional) | `ThemeAdapter<T>[]` | Library adapters installed when the runtime is created. The runtime owns the registry and notifies every adapter whenever the theme changes; it never knows anything about the libraries themselves. | | `broadcast` (optional) | `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter \| null` | Cross-tab broadcast adapter. When omitted, a `BroadcastChannel`-based adapter on channel `"theme-selection"` is created; pass `null` to disable cross-tab sync. | | `children` (optional) | `Element` | The subtree rendered inside the provider's context. | | `cssVariables` (optional) | `false \| CSSVariablesOptions` | CSS-variable binding configuration. `false` disables the binding. | | `defaultTheme` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Theme to activate when no persisted or explicit selection exists. Accepts a **variant** name (`"cocoa-dark"`) or a **family** name (`"cocoa"`); a family resolves to the variant the mode contract picks (see resolveThemeReference). A variant also supplies its own mode unless `initialMode` is given. | | `dom` (optional) | `false \| DOMBindingOptions` | DOM attribute/class binding configuration. `false` disables the binding. | | `initial` (optional) | `InitialThemeResolution<T>` | Explicit initial theme resolution, bypassing default + persistence based resolution. | | `initialFamily` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Initial family used when nothing else is given. A **variant** name is also accepted and normalised to its family; the variant's own mode is used only when initialMode is absent, so an explicit mode always wins and the two props cannot silently disagree. | | `initialMode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Initial mode used when nothing else is given. | | `persistence` (optional) | `ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter \| null` | Persistence adapter for the theme selection. Pass `null` to disable persistence entirely. | | `plugins` (optional) | `ThemePlugin<T>[]` | Runtime plugins installed at creation. | | `prefix` (optional) | `string` | CSS custom property prefix used by the CSS-variables binding. | | `readPersistenceOnInit` (optional) | `boolean` | Whether a persisted selection is read at runtime creation. | | `runtime` (optional) | `ThemeRuntime<T>` | An existing runtime to adopt. When omitted the provider creates and owns its own runtime from the remaining props. | | `scheduled` (optional) | `false \| ScheduledThemeOptions<T>` | Sunrise/sunset scheduling configuration. `false` disables scheduling. | | `storageKey` (optional) | `string` | The `localStorage` key the default persistence adapter reads and writes. | | `themeOverride` (optional) | `ThemeOverride<ThemeIdentifier<T>>` | An explicit theme to apply, outranking a saved selection. Unlike defaultTheme, which is only a fallback, an override is applied even when `localStorage` or a cookie already names another theme — which is what makes "preview this theme" expressible as a prop. It is a one-shot signal, not a controlled selection: it is applied when its value changes, it is never re-asserted on later renders, and it does not write to persistence. See ThemeOverride. | | `themes` (optional) | `readonly T[]` | Initial theme definitions. Duplicate names are dropped (first wins). When omitted, the registry starts empty. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition configuration. `true` enables transitions with defaults, `false` disables them, and an object provides explicit options. | | `view` (optional) | `Window` | The `window` to bind to. Defaults to the global `window` when available; omit (or pass `undefined`) in SSR environments. | ---

title: ThemeScopeProps
text: ThemeScopeProps Props accepted by ThemeScope. Configures a nested theme boundary that overrides the global selection for its subtree. `theme` wins over `family`/`mode`; when none are given the scope mirrors the provider's selection inside its own boundary. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `children` (optional) | `Element` | The subtree rendered inside the scope's wrapper. | | `className` (optional) | `string` | CSS class applied to the scope's wrapper `<div>`. | | `family` (optional) | `string` | Theme family for the scoped subtree. When `mode` is omitted the scope follows the provider's current mode (light/dark/system). | | `mode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Mode for a family-based scope. Optional — defaults to the provider's current mode so `family="plum"` flips light/dark with the page. | | `theme` (optional) | `string` | Exact theme name, family name, or a `{ family, mode }`-style object. When `family`/`mode` are also passed, `theme` wins (it's the explicit selection). Omit to follow the global selection inside a new boundary. | | `themes` (optional) | `readonly ThemeDefinition<string>[]` | Local theme definitions for genuinely isolated components. Resolved FIRST (they shadow same-named parent themes), then the provider's registry falls back — no second runtime is created. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition for this scope's own theme changes. `undefined` inherits the `<ThemeProvider/>` transition, `false` disables it, `true` inherits, and an object is merged over the provider's config (local keys win). | ---

title: ThemeScrollbarProps
text: ThemeScrollbarProps **Extends** `ScrollbarGroupedOptions` Props accepted by ThemeScrollbar. Extends OverlayScrollbarOptions so the scrollbar can be configured with the same options used by `createOverlayScrollbar`. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `appearance` (optional) | `ScrollbarAppearanceOptions` | — | | `behavior` (optional) | `ScrollbarBehaviorOptions` | Grouped settings - the canonical form; a flat option wins over it. | | `children` (optional) | `Element` | The subtree the scrollbar is applied to. | | `icons` (optional) | `ScrollbarIconOptions<string>` | Arrow button icons: the arrow entry covers all four directions (per-direction entries win), plus the shared glyph size in CSS px. | | `scope` (optional) | `ScrollbarScopeOptions` | — | ---

title: Related docs
text: Related docs - [Families & Modes](/core-concepts) — A selection is a family (which palette) plus a mode (light/dark/system); every framework exposes the same read/write surface for it. - [Theme Discovery & Overrides](/advanced-features) — A provider exposes exactly the themes it was given — grouped by family, with variants and resolved tokens — and accepts an explicit one-shot themeOverride that outranks a saved selection. - [Runtime](/architecture) — One runtime per app owns the store, selection, registry, history, lifecycle and adapters; every framework binding is a thin view over it. - [ThemeScope](/scoped-theme) — Apply a different family/mode (or a local theme definition) to a subtree, with scoped CSS variables and pre-paint support. - [Persistence](/persistence) — Persist the selection across reloads and requests, with fingerprint validation, storage adapters and theme migrations. - [Theme generation](/theme-studio) — Generate a complete, accessible light/dark theme pair from a single seed color, ready to drop into the runtime. - [Plugins](/plugins) — Extend the runtime through a first-class plugin manager and adapter registry; theme packs install ready-made behaviour. - [Zero-flash bootstrap](/zero-flash) — Paint the correct theme on the first frame: a blocking script plus server-resolved initial state, with a Vite plugin for SPA builds. - [Custom scrollbar](/custom-scrollbar) — Themed overlay scrollbars that match the active theme and pre-paint before hydration. - [DevTools](/devtools) — Inspect and drive the live runtime from a panel: adapters, history, snapshots and performance entries. - [Solid](/framework-guides/solid) — the framework integration

title: @themvora/svelte
text: @themvora/svelte Themvora Svelte integration. title: createSvelteThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string
text: createSvelteThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string Build the blocking zero-flash `<head>` script for a Svelte app (SSR or SPA). Inlines core's `createThemeBootstrapScript` with the Svelte defaults (`storageKey: "theme-selection"`, `prefix: "theme-"` — the same values the Svelte `ThemeProvider` persistence and CSS variables use), so the persisted theme is applied before first paint. title: useEffectiveThemeMode(): { value: void; subscribe: void }
text: useEffectiveThemeMode(): { value: void; subscribe: void } Reactive access to the mode actually **applied** — `"light"` or `"dark"`, never `"system"` — as a readable Svelte store. Use this to display the current appearance. useThemeMode reports what the visitor asked for: it stays `"system"` for as long as that choice stands, and it does not move at a sunrise/sunset transition, so a label bound to it kept announcing the old mode while the page changed colour. Must be called during component initialization inside a `ThemeProvider` subtree. **See also:** `useThemeMode`, `useThemeSchedule` **Returns** `{ value: void; subscribe: void }` — A readable store whose value is the applied mode. ---

title: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { value: void; subscribe: void }
text: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { value: void; subscribe: void } Reactive access to the theme produced by `generateTheme()` and registered with the provider, as a readable Svelte store. Resolves the registered theme that carries the generator's origin marker (`meta.generation.kind === "generated"`); shipped presets never qualify. When both halves of one `generateTheme()` call are registered, the store tracks the theme the active selection resolves to. Must be called during component initialization inside a `ThemeProvider` subtree. Throws `ThemeError` with code `TV_GENERATION_THEME_NOT_FOUND` when the provider holds no generated theme, and `TV_GENERATION_THEME_AMBIGUOUS` when several are registered and the active selection does not identify one. Re-resolves on every settled change to the registry, store, or selection. If the generated theme is later removed, the store's value is cleared (the theme is no longer readable) rather than retaining a stale one; Svelte's store contract has no read-time getter, so a fresh subscription to a removed theme throws. **See also:** `useThemeValue` **Returns** `{ value: void; subscribe: void }` — A readable store whose value is the registered generated theme. ---

title: useProvidedThemes<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): { value: void; subscribe: void }
text:
useProvidedThemes>(): { value: void; subscribe: void } Reactive access to the themes this provider was given, grouped by family. Returns exactly the collection supplied to the nearest `ThemeProvider` — not the built-in catalog. The store emits a new value when the provider's `themes` prop changes, when a theme pack is installed, or when the registry is mutated, and it keeps the previous array instance while nothing changes. Must be called during component initialization inside a `ThemeProvider` subtree. ```svelte {#each $families as family (family.id)}

{family.name}

{#each family.variants as variant (variant.name)} {/each} {/each} ``` **See also:** `useThemeValue` **Returns** `{ value: void; subscribe: void }` — A readable store whose value is the provider's theme families. ---

title: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition>
text: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition> **Extends** `ThemeRuntimeOptions<T>` Props accepted by the Svelte `ThemeProvider` component. Extends the core runtime options (themes, default theme, initial mode and family, persistence, transition, scheduling, DOM/CSS binding options). When `runtime` is omitted the provider creates and owns a runtime from the remaining options; when supplied, the provider adopts the given runtime and does not destroy it on unmount. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `adapters` (optional) | `ThemeAdapter<T>[]` | Library adapters installed when the runtime is created. The runtime owns the registry and notifies every adapter whenever the theme changes; it never knows anything about the libraries themselves. | | `broadcast` (optional) | `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter \| null` | Cross-tab broadcast adapter. When omitted, a `BroadcastChannel`-based adapter on channel `"theme-selection"` is created; pass `null` to disable cross-tab sync. | | `children` (optional) | `Snippet<[]>` | The Svelte snippet rendered inside the provider. Must be provided as a snippet (Svelte 5 `{@snippet}`) so it is instantiated after the runtime context is set. | | `cssVariables` (optional) | `false \| CSSVariablesOptions` | CSS-variable binding configuration. `false` disables the binding. | | `defaultTheme` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Theme to activate when no persisted or explicit selection exists. Accepts a **variant** name (`"cocoa-dark"`) or a **family** name (`"cocoa"`); a family resolves to the variant the mode contract picks (see resolveThemeReference). A variant also supplies its own mode unless `initialMode` is given. | | `dom` (optional) | `false \| DOMBindingOptions` | DOM attribute/class binding configuration. `false` disables the binding. | | `initial` (optional) | `InitialThemeResolution<T>` | Explicit initial theme resolution, bypassing default + persistence based resolution. | | `initialFamily` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Initial family used when nothing else is given. A **variant** name is also accepted and normalised to its family; the variant's own mode is used only when initialMode is absent, so an explicit mode always wins and the two props cannot silently disagree. | | `initialMode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Initial mode used when nothing else is given. | | `persistence` (optional) | `ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter \| null` | Persistence adapter for the theme selection. Pass `null` to disable persistence entirely. | | `plugins` (optional) | `ThemePlugin<T>[]` | Runtime plugins installed at creation. | | `prefix` (optional) | `string` | CSS custom property prefix used by the CSS-variables binding. | | `readPersistenceOnInit` (optional) | `boolean` | Whether a persisted selection is read at runtime creation. | | `runtime` (optional) | `ThemeRuntime<T>` | A runtime owned by the caller. When provided, the provider does not create or destroy it. When omitted, the provider creates its own runtime from the other props and destroys it on unmount. | | `scheduled` (optional) | `false \| ScheduledThemeOptions<T>` | Sunrise/sunset scheduling configuration. `false` disables scheduling. | | `storageKey` (optional) | `string` | The `localStorage` key the default persistence adapter reads and writes. | | `themeOverride` (optional) | `ThemeOverride<ThemeIdentifier<T>>` | An explicit theme to apply, outranking a saved selection. Unlike defaultTheme, which is only a fallback, an override is applied even when `localStorage` or a cookie already names another theme — which is what makes "preview this theme" expressible as a prop. It is a one-shot signal, not a controlled selection: it is applied when its value changes, it is never re-asserted on later renders, and it does not write to persistence. See ThemeOverride. | | `themes` (optional) | `readonly T[]` | Initial theme definitions. Duplicate names are dropped (first wins). When omitted, the registry starts empty. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition configuration. `true` enables transitions with defaults, `false` disables them, and an object provides explicit options. | | `view` (optional) | `Window` | The `window` to bind to. Defaults to the global `window` when available; omit (or pass `undefined`) in SSR environments. | ---

title: ThemeScopeProps
text: ThemeScopeProps Props accepted by the Svelte `ThemeScope` component. Applies a scoped theme to a subtree without changing the provider's global selection. `theme`/`family`/`mode` are read at mount; family-based and boundary scopes keep following the provider's light/dark/system mode while mounted. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `children` | `Snippet<[]>` | The Svelte snippet rendered inside the scoped wrapper. | | `className` (optional) | `string` | CSS class applied to the wrapper `div` created for the scope. | | `family` (optional) | `string` | Theme family for the scoped subtree. When `mode` is omitted the scope follows the provider's current mode (light/dark/system). | | `mode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Mode for a family-based scope. Optional — defaults to the provider's current mode so `family="plum"` flips light/dark with the page. | | `theme` (optional) | `string` | Exact theme name, family name, or a `{ family, mode }`-style object. When `family`/`mode` are also passed, `theme` wins (it's the explicit selection). Omit to follow the global selection inside a new boundary. | | `themes` (optional) | `readonly ThemeDefinition<string>[]` | Local theme definitions for genuinely isolated components. Resolved FIRST (they shadow same-named parent themes), then the provider's registry falls back — no second runtime is created. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition for this scope's own theme changes. `undefined` inherits the `<ThemeProvider/>` transition, `false` disables it, `true` inherits, and an object is merged over the provider's config (local keys win). | ---

title: ThemeScrollbarProps
text: ThemeScrollbarProps **Extends** `ScrollbarGroupedOptions` Props accepted by the Svelte `ThemeScrollbar` component. Extends the core overlay scrollbar options to configure the overlay engine (auto-hide, thickness, colors, axes, touch, direction, and so on). title: ThemeProvider
text: ThemeProvider The Themvora provider component (Svelte 5 runes: `$props` + `$effect`). Compiled from `theme-provider.svelte` by `scripts/compile-svelte.mjs`. A changed configuration prop is forwarded to the shared `runtime.configure()` contract, so the UI updates without a reload. The two compiled variants are picked at runtime, so an SSR bundle never runs the client component. **See also:** `ThemeScope` `Component<ThemeProviderProps<ThemeDefinition>>` ---

title: ThemeScope
text: ThemeScope The scoped theming component (Svelte 5 runes). Compiled from `theme-scope.svelte`. A changed `theme`/`family`/`mode`/ `themes`/`transition` re-resolves the scope without a remount. **See also:** `ThemeProvider` `Component<ThemeScopeProps>` ---

title: ThemeScrollbar
text: ThemeScrollbar The overlay scrollbar component. See ThemeScrollbarProps. Compiled from `theme-scrollbar.svelte` by `scripts/compile-svelte.mjs` — a runes component, so `$effect` re-runs when an option changes and the overlay is rebuilt with the new value. A plain function component in this `.ts` module could not do that: Svelte never re-runs one, so a changed prop was ignored until the page was reloaded. The two compiled variants are picked at runtime, so an SSR bundle never runs the client component (and vice versa). **See also:** `ThemeProvider` `Component<ThemeScrollbarProps>` ---

title: Related docs
text: Related docs - [Families & Modes](/core-concepts) — A selection is a family (which palette) plus a mode (light/dark/system); every framework exposes the same read/write surface for it. - [Theme Discovery & Overrides](/advanced-features) — A provider exposes exactly the themes it was given — grouped by family, with variants and resolved tokens — and accepts an explicit one-shot themeOverride that outranks a saved selection. - [Runtime](/architecture) — One runtime per app owns the store, selection, registry, history, lifecycle and adapters; every framework binding is a thin view over it. - [ThemeScope](/scoped-theme) — Apply a different family/mode (or a local theme definition) to a subtree, with scoped CSS variables and pre-paint support. - [Persistence](/persistence) — Persist the selection across reloads and requests, with fingerprint validation, storage adapters and theme migrations. - [Theme generation](/theme-studio) — Generate a complete, accessible light/dark theme pair from a single seed color, ready to drop into the runtime. - [Plugins](/plugins) — Extend the runtime through a first-class plugin manager and adapter registry; theme packs install ready-made behaviour. - [Zero-flash bootstrap](/zero-flash) — Paint the correct theme on the first frame: a blocking script plus server-resolved initial state, with a Vite plugin for SPA builds. - [Custom scrollbar](/custom-scrollbar) — Themed overlay scrollbars that match the active theme and pre-paint before hydration. - [DevTools](/devtools) — Inspect and drive the live runtime from a panel: adapters, history, snapshots and performance entries. - [Svelte 5](/framework-guides/svelte) — the framework integration

title: createVueThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string
text: createVueThemeBootstrapScript<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options): string Build the blocking zero-flash `<head>` script for a Vue app (SSR or SPA). Inlines core's `createThemeBootstrapScript` with the Vue defaults (`storageKey: "theme-selection"`, `prefix: "theme-"` — the same values the Vue `ThemeProvider` persistence and CSS variables use), so the persisted theme is applied before first paint. Emit the returned string as a blocking `<script>` inside `<head>`. **See also:** ``buildThemeCssMap`` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemeBootstrapScriptOptions<T>` | — | **Returns** `string` ---

text: provideThemeRuntime<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(runtime): void Provides a Themvora runtime to the current Vue component subtree. title: useEffectiveThemeMode(): Ref<"light" | "dark">
text: useEffectiveThemeMode(): Ref<"light" | "dark"> Reactive ref of the mode actually **applied** — `"light"` or `"dark"`, never `"system"`. Render this when a control states the current appearance. useThemeMode reports what the visitor asked for, which does not move at a sunrise/sunset transition and stays `"system"` for as long as that choice stands — so a label bound to it kept announcing the old mode while the page changed colour. Call inside Vue `setup` scope within a `<ThemeProvider>`. Subscribes to the appearance (store and effective-selection channels) and is cleaned up on unmount. **See also:** `useThemeMode`, `useThemeSchedule` **Returns** `Ref<"light" | "dark">` — A `Ref` holding the applied mode. ---

title: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): Ref<T>
text: useGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(): Ref<T> Reactive ref of the theme produced by `generateTheme()` and registered with the provider. Resolves the registered theme that carries the generator's origin marker (`meta.generation.kind === "generated"`); shipped presets never qualify. When both halves of one `generateTheme()` call are registered, the ref tracks the theme the active selection resolves to and updates on selection changes. Call inside a Vue `setup` scope within a `<ThemeProvider>`. Throws `ThemeError` with code `TV_GENERATION_THEME_NOT_FOUND` when the provider holds no generated theme, and `TV_GENERATION_THEME_AMBIGUOUS` when several are registered and the active selection does not identify one. Re-resolves on every settled change to the registry, store, or selection; if the generated theme is later removed, the same error is raised at the next reactive read rather than a stale theme being returned. **See also:** `useThemeValue` **Returns** `Ref<T>` — A `Ref` holding the registered generated theme. ---

title: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition>
text: ThemeProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition> **Extends** `ThemeRuntimeOptions<T>` Props accepted by the Vue `<ThemeProvider>` component. Extends ThemeRuntimeOptions with an optional pre-built runtime. When `runtime` is omitted, the provider creates and owns its own runtime from the remaining props and destroys it on unmount. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `adapters` (optional) | `ThemeAdapter<T>[]` | Library adapters installed when the runtime is created. The runtime owns the registry and notifies every adapter whenever the theme changes; it never knows anything about the libraries themselves. | | `broadcast` (optional) | `ThemeSelectionBroadcastAdapter \| null` | Cross-tab broadcast adapter. When omitted, a `BroadcastChannel`-based adapter on channel `"theme-selection"` is created; pass `null` to disable cross-tab sync. | | `cssVariables` (optional) | `false \| CSSVariablesOptions` | CSS-variable binding configuration. `false` disables the binding. | | `defaultTheme` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Theme to activate when no persisted or explicit selection exists. Accepts a **variant** name (`"cocoa-dark"`) or a **family** name (`"cocoa"`); a family resolves to the variant the mode contract picks (see resolveThemeReference). A variant also supplies its own mode unless `initialMode` is given. | | `dom` (optional) | `false \| DOMBindingOptions` | DOM attribute/class binding configuration. `false` disables the binding. | | `initial` (optional) | `InitialThemeResolution<T>` | Explicit initial theme resolution, bypassing default + persistence based resolution. | | `initialFamily` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Initial family used when nothing else is given. A **variant** name is also accepted and normalised to its family; the variant's own mode is used only when initialMode is absent, so an explicit mode always wins and the two props cannot silently disagree. | | `initialMode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Initial mode used when nothing else is given. | | `persistence` (optional) | `ThemeSelectionPersistenceAdapter \| null` | Persistence adapter for the theme selection. Pass `null` to disable persistence entirely. | | `plugins` (optional) | `ThemePlugin<T>[]` | Runtime plugins installed at creation. | | `prefix` (optional) | `string` | CSS custom property prefix used by the CSS-variables binding. | | `readPersistenceOnInit` (optional) | `boolean` | Whether a persisted selection is read at runtime creation. | | `runtime` (optional) | `ThemeRuntime<T>` | An existing runtime to provide. When omitted, the provider creates and owns a runtime from the other props. | | `scheduled` (optional) | `false \| ScheduledThemeOptions<T>` | Sunrise/sunset scheduling configuration. `false` disables scheduling. | | `storageKey` (optional) | `string` | The `localStorage` key the default persistence adapter reads and writes. | | `themeOverride` (optional) | `ThemeOverride<ThemeIdentifier<T>>` | An explicit theme to apply, outranking a saved selection. Unlike defaultTheme, which is only a fallback, an override is applied even when `localStorage` or a cookie already names another theme — which is what makes "preview this theme" expressible as a prop. It is a one-shot signal, not a controlled selection: it is applied when its value changes, it is never re-asserted on later renders, and it does not write to persistence. See ThemeOverride. | | `themes` (optional) | `readonly T[]` | Initial theme definitions. Duplicate names are dropped (first wins). When omitted, the registry starts empty. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition configuration. `true` enables transitions with defaults, `false` disables them, and an object provides explicit options. | | `view` (optional) | `Window` | The `window` to bind to. Defaults to the global `window` when available; omit (or pass `undefined`) in SSR environments. | ---

title: ThemeScrollbar
text: ThemeScrollbar Vue component that replaces the native scrollbar with a themed overlay scrollbar. Renders nothing (returns `null`) and instead installs an overlay scrollbar on the target element (see ThemeScrollbarProps.tag) once mounted. Injects the pre-paint hiding CSS synchronously during `setup` so the native bar never flashes. title: Related docs
text: Related docs - [Families & Modes](/core-concepts) — A selection is a family (which palette) plus a mode (light/dark/system); every framework exposes the same read/write surface for it. - [Theme Discovery & Overrides](/advanced-features) — A provider exposes exactly the themes it was given — grouped by family, with variants and resolved tokens — and accepts an explicit one-shot themeOverride that outranks a saved selection. - [Runtime](/architecture) — One runtime per app owns the store, selection, registry, history, lifecycle and adapters; every framework binding is a thin view over it. - [ThemeScope](/scoped-theme) — Apply a different family/mode (or a local theme definition) to a subtree, with scoped CSS variables and pre-paint support. - [Persistence](/persistence) — Persist the selection across reloads and requests, with fingerprint validation, storage adapters and theme migrations. - [Theme generation](/theme-studio) — Generate a complete, accessible light/dark theme pair from a single seed color, ready to drop into the runtime. - [Plugins](/plugins) — Extend the runtime through a first-class plugin manager and adapter registry; theme packs install ready-made behaviour. - [Zero-flash bootstrap](/zero-flash) — Paint the correct theme on the first frame: a blocking script plus server-resolved initial state, with a Vite plugin for SPA builds. - [Custom scrollbar](/custom-scrollbar) — Themed overlay scrollbars that match the active theme and pre-paint before hydration. - [DevTools](/devtools) — Inspect and drive the live runtime from a panel: adapters, history, snapshots and performance entries. - [Vue 3](/framework-guides/vue) — the framework integration

title: themvoraVitePlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemvoraVitePlugin
text: themvoraVitePlugin<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(options?): ThemvoraVitePlugin Vite plugin that injects the theme bootstrap as a blocking inline script at the top of `index.html`, so the persisted theme is applied before the first paint. Prevents the flash-of-wrong-theme on reload for client-rendered apps. **See also:** `ThemvoraVitePluginOptions` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `options` | `ThemvoraVitePluginOptions<T>` (optional) | Build-time options. Optional; the default discovery path needs none. | **Returns** `ThemvoraVitePlugin` — A Vite plugin, to be added to `plugins`. **Config discovery.** The plugin looks for the application's `theme.config.ts` in Vite's root (`config.root`, or `process.cwd()` when unset), trying `theme.config.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.mjs`, `.js` and `.cjs` in that order. The file must have a default export — the object defineThemvoraConfig returns. Discovery goes through Vite's own `loadConfigFromFile`, so a TypeScript config resolves its imports exactly as `vite.config.ts` does. **What it injects.** Three things, all derived from that one configuration and emitted in this order (`head-prepend`, `enforce: "pre"`): 1. a render-blocking `<style>` from createThemePrePaintCss — the fallback theme, the `prefers-color-scheme` dark fallback when the mode is `"system"`, and one rule per declared theme; 2. `window.__THEMVORA_CONFIG__`, the serializable ThemeBootstrapConfig projection the provider reads; 3. the classic blocking bootstrap script that restores the persisted selection. When `scrollbar` is enabled, the pre-paint scrollbar script follows. The stylesheet is what themes a page with JavaScript disabled; the script is what restores a saved non-default theme before the body is parsed. **Validation.** The provider in the transformed HTML is parsed and checked against the config: unknown theme names, a default theme outside the generated collection, an invalid `initial-mode`, and a provider that resolves a different initial theme all fail the build with an actionable message. Provider JSON theme definitions are added to the generated collection, so a runtime-only catalog the plugin can see is still painted. **Development.** `transformIndexHtml` runs on every dev page load, so the injected resources are always current for the running process. The *discovered config* is resolved once and memoized, so editing `theme.config.ts` needs a dev-server restart; editing `vite.config.ts` restarts Vite anyway, so the plugin's own options do not. **Production.** The resources are injected into the generated HTML at build time and run before the application bundle. They are not emitted as separate chunks. **Limitations.** The plugin only validates a provider that is present in the document it transforms; a provider inserted later from framework state is runtime-only. It does not serve SSR HTML: frameworks that render on the server (Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, Astro) have their own packages, which emit the same bootstrap from the server. Themes registered imperatively with `runtime.use()` after load are not in the generated CSS. ```ts // Nothing to configure beyond registering the plugin. import { themvoraVitePlugin } from "@themvora/core/vite"; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react(), themvoraVitePlugin()], }); ``` ---

title: @themvora/web
text: @themvora/web Themvora web components — framework-free theming for any app. Provides the custom elements `ThemvoraProvider`, `ThemvoraScope`, `ThemvoraToggle`, `ThemvoraSelect`, `ThemvoraScrollbar`, and `ThemvoraInspector`, plus the `useTheme*` hooks, `getProviderRuntime`, `getThemeSchedule`, and the `defineCustomElements` registration helper. ## HTML-first usage Importing this entry is enough: it registers the built-in elements and injects their stylesheet once, so the consumer writes semantic HTML and nothing else. ```html <themvora-provider themes="light dark plum-dark" default-theme="light"> <themvora-toggle></themvora-toggle> <themvora-select type="family"></themvora-select> <themvora-scope theme="plum-dark">…</themvora-scope> </themvora-provider> ``` ```ts import "@themvora/web"; ``` Registration is idempotent and browser-only: importing the package during a server render is a no-op, so Next.js, Remix, Nuxt, Astro and SvelteKit can import it without a browser guard. > Generated from `packages/web/src` by `apps/docs/scripts/generate-api-reference.mjs`. Do not edit by hand — run `pnpm --filter @themvora/docs api:generate`.

title: defineCustomElements(): void
text: defineCustomElements(): void Registers all Themvora custom elements with the browser and injects the built-in component stylesheet. Framework-free (vanilla JS). Defines `<themvora-provider>`, `<themvora-scope>`, `<themvora-toggle>`, `<themvora-select>`, `<themvora-scrollbar>` and `<themvora-inspector>` if not already registered, and adds the component stylesheet once. Safe to call more than once, and a no-op on the server. **See also:** `ThemvoraProvider` **Returns** `void` Importing `@themvora/web` already calls this, so a consumer normally never calls it. It stays public for two cases: a consumer who wants to register a different tag name (`ThemvoraProvider.define("my-provider")`), and a consumer who needs the registration to happen at a specific point rather than at module evaluation. ```ts import { defineCustomElements } from "@themvora/web"; defineCustomElements(); ``` ---

title: injectComponentStyles(): boolean
text: injectComponentStyles(): boolean Injects COMPONENT_CSS into the document once. Idempotent: repeated calls, duplicate bundle evaluation and a consumer who already pasted the stylesheet into their own `<style id="themvora-elements-style">` all leave exactly one copy in the document. A no-op on the server. **Returns** `boolean` — `true` when this call inserted the stylesheet, `false` when it was already present or the environment has no DOM. ---

title: injectPrePaintScrollbarCSS(): void
text: injectPrePaintScrollbarCSS(): void Injects the pre-paint scrollbar-hiding CSS and class into the document. Framework-free (vanilla JS). Adds a `<style>` carrying the pre-paint scrollbar CSS and the `tv-scrollbar` class to the document root so the native scrollbar is hidden before first paint. Idempotent and a no-op on the server. This is a manual bootstrap helper for a page that wants the native bar hidden before its own script runs. It is *not* how ThemvoraScrollbar hides the bar — that happens through `createOverlayScrollbar`, which claims the hiding and gives it back on `destroy()`. Calling this directly therefore hides the bar without registering a claim, so pair it with `restoreNativeScrollbar()` if you later want the native bar back. **See also:** `ThemvoraScrollbar` **Returns** `void` ---

title: observeEffectiveThemeMode(listener): type(): void
text: observeEffectiveThemeMode(listener): type(): void Calls `listener` whenever the applied mode changes, and returns an unsubscribe function. Framework-free (vanilla JS). Requires an initialized `<themvora-provider>`. The listener is **not** called once up front — read useEffectiveThemeMode for the current value and call it again from the listener. ```ts const stop = observeEffectiveThemeMode(() => { label.textContent = useEffectiveThemeMode(); }); ``` **See also:** `useEffectiveThemeMode` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `listener` | `__type(selection: ThemeEffectiveSelection): void` | Called after the applied mode changes. | **Returns** `__type(): void` — An unsubscribe function. ---

text: resolveGeneratedTheme<T extends ThemeDefinition<string>>(themes, active?): T Resolve the single generated theme registered with a provider, or throw. The throwing counterpart of findGeneratedTheme, for call sites that need a theme rather than a status — the framework accessors, which surface the failure to the caller. **See also:** `- isGeneratedTheme - findGeneratedTheme` | Parameter | Type | Description | | --------- | ---- | ----------- | | `themes` | `readonly T[]` | The themes registered with the provider. | | `active` | `T` (optional) | The currently active theme, used to disambiguate multiple generated themes. | **Returns** `T` — The resolved generated theme. ---

title: useEffectiveThemeMode(): "light" | "dark"
text: useEffectiveThemeMode(): "light" | "dark" Returns the mode actually **applied** — `"light"` or `"dark"`, never `"system"`. Framework-free (vanilla JS). Requires an initialized `<themvora-provider>`. Use this when a control states the current appearance. useThemeMode reports what the visitor asked for: it stays `"system"` while that choice stands and it does not move at a sunrise/sunset transition, so a label bound to it kept announcing the old mode while the page changed colour. Pair it with observeEffectiveThemeMode to re-render on change. **See also:** `useThemeMode`, `observeEffectiveThemeMode` **Returns** `"light" | "dark"` — The applied mode. ---

title: useGeneratedTheme(): ThemeDefinition<string>
text: useGeneratedTheme(): ThemeDefinition<string> Returns the theme produced by `generateTheme()` and registered with the active `<themvora-provider>`. Resolves the registered theme that carries the generator's origin marker (`meta.generation.kind === "generated"`); shipped presets never qualify. When both halves of one `generateTheme()` call are registered, the theme the active selection resolves to is returned. Framework-free (vanilla JS). Requires an initialized `<themvora-provider>`. Throws `ThemeError` with code `TV_GENERATION_THEME_NOT_FOUND` when the provider holds no generated theme, and `TV_GENERATION_THEME_AMBIGUOUS` when several are registered and the active selection does not identify one. Reads live on every call, so a theme removed from the registry is reported immediately rather than a stale value being returned. **See also:** `useThemeValue` **Returns** `ThemeDefinition<string>` — The registered generated theme. ---

title: useProvidedThemes(): readonly ProvidedThemeFamily<ThemeDefinition<string>>[]
text: useProvidedThemes(): readonly ProvidedThemeFamily<ThemeDefinition<string>>[] Returns the themes the active `<themvora-provider>` was given, grouped by family. Framework-free (vanilla JS). Reads live on every call, so a theme registered after the provider initialized appears immediately — the vanilla surface has no reactive wrapper by design, matching useThemeValue. For a push notification, listen for the provider's `themes-change` event. ```js const families = useProvidedThemes(); families.forEach((family) => { console.log(family.family, family.variants.map((v) => v.mode)); }); ``` **See also:** `useThemeRuntime`, `normalizeProvidedThemes` **Returns** `readonly ProvidedThemeFamily<ThemeDefinition<string>>[]` — The provider's theme families, in supplied order. ---

title: useThemeMode(): ThemeMode
text: useThemeMode(): ThemeMode Returns the current theme mode (`system`, `light`, or `dark`). Framework-free (vanilla JS). Requires an initialized `<themvora-provider>`. **See also:** `useThemeRuntime`, `defineCustomElements` **Returns** `ThemeMode` — The current mode. ---

title: useThemeRuntime(): ThemeRuntime<ThemeDefinition<string>>

Must be called after a `<themvora-provider>` has initialized. **Multiple providers:** this returns the *first* provider in document order that has a runtime. It is a page-level convenience, not a way to address a specific provider — use `getProviderRuntime(element)` when more than one provider exists, or when the element you hold is not the first. **See also:** `getProviderRuntime`, `defineCustomElements` **Returns** `ThemeRuntime<ThemeDefinition<string>>` — The provider's runtime. ```ts const runtime = useThemeRuntime(); runtime.selection.setMode("dark"); ``` ---

title: class ThemvoraProvider
text: class ThemvoraProvider **Extends** `CustomElementBase` Custom element `<themvora-provider>` that owns a Themvora runtime and applies the active theme to the document. Framework-free (vanilla JS). Creates and destroys its runtime across its lifecycle, applies DOM/CSS variable bindings, and dispatches a bubbling `theme-ready` event once initialized. Observes the `themes`, `default-theme`, `initial-mode`, `initial-family`, `scheduled`, and `transition` attributes. **See also:** `ThemvoraProviderProps`, `defineCustomElements`, `ThemvoraScope`, `ThemvoraToggle`, `ThemvoraSelect` | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `constructor` | `ThemvoraProvider` | — | | `accessKey` | `string` | The **`HTMLElement.accessKey`** property sets the keystroke which a user can press to jump to a given element. `void` | — | **Attributes.** All six are observed and applied to the live runtime. - `themes` — the catalog. Either space-separated registered identifiers (`"light dark plum-light"`) or a JSON array of full theme definitions (`'[{"name":"brand","tokens":{…}}]'`). An unknown identifier is reported and skipped; an empty or unusable list falls back to the neutral light/dark pair (`TV_THEME_NEUTRAL_FALLBACK`). - `default-theme` — theme name used when nothing is persisted. Supplies both the fallback theme's family and its mode; an unknown name resolves to the catalog's first theme. - `initial-mode` — `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"` (case-insensitive). Overrides the mode `default-theme` implies. An invalid value is reported (`TV_CONFIG_OPTION_INVALID`) and ignored. - `initial-family` — family used when nothing is persisted. Overrides the family `default-theme` implies; an unregistered one is reported (`TV_THEME_FAMILY_UNKNOWN`) and normalised. - `transition` — `true`, `false`, or JSON (`'{"enabled":true,"duration":250,"easing":"ease-in-out"}'`). Changing it reconfigures the live bindings; removing it returns to no transition. - `scheduled` — JSON sunrise/sunset options (`'{"latitude":27.7,"longitude":85.3}'`). Removing it tears the schedule down. **Properties.** None of its own beyond the standard `HTMLElement` surface. The runtime is reached with getProviderRuntime (or useThemeRuntime for the first provider on the page). **Events.** `theme-ready` (bubbles, composed) once the runtime exists and the first theme is applied; `themes-change` (bubbles, composed) on a microtask after the catalog changes, with `detail.themes` holding the new names. **Slots.** Its children are ordinary light-DOM content — the consumer's markup and the other `<themvora-*>` elements. The element renders no wrapper and styles nothing of its own. When an observed attribute changes after initialization, the change is applied to the live runtime through the shared `configure()` contract — the runtime is never destroyed and recreated, so history, persistence and the current selection survive, and the transition/schedule subsystems are reconciled in place. **Removing an attribute never resets the runtime.** A removed `themes`, `default-theme`, `initial-mode` or `initial-family` stops contributing to the configuration; the live catalog and selection stay as they are, and the removal takes effect on the next mount (where `resolveRuntimeOptions` runs again). `transition` and `scheduled` are the exception: removing them turns the subsystem off, because "off" is expressible for them. The element never writes its own observed attributes, so an attribute change always originates from the consumer and cannot feed back into itself. The `configuring` guard additionally covers a consumer that reflects state into the attribute during `themes-change`. ```ts <themvora-provider themes="light dark plum-dark" default-theme="light"> ... </themvora-provider> ``` ---

title: class ThemvoraRuntimeConsumer
text: class ThemvoraRuntimeConsumer **Extends** `CustomElementBase` Base class for a Themvora element that reads and follows the nearest `<themvora-provider>`'s runtime.

title: The lifecycle problem it solves
text: The lifecycle problem it solves A descendant element can connect before, after, or instead of its provider initializing, and a provider that is removed and re-added creates a *new* runtime. Handling that by hand produced three defects that this base class removes: 1. **A one-shot listener that never fires.** The provider dispatches `theme-ready` on itself with `bubbles: true`, which travels *up* the tree and can never reach a descendant. Listening on the element itself only worked when the provider happened to initialize first. 2. **Duplicate subscriptions.** Every reconnection ran `init()` again and added another store listener, so a re-mounted element updated twice, three times, and so on. 3. **Stale runtimes.** After a provider was recreated, an element kept listening to the destroyed runtime and silently stopped updating. Subclasses implement ThemvoraRuntimeConsumer.onRuntime to subscribe and ThemvoraRuntimeConsumer.onDetach to release what they took. Reconnection re-runs the pair, so a subscription can never outlive its connection or be created twice. The catalog subscription is taken by this class, not by each subclass: every consumer that resolves themes itself (a scope, a family selector) must see a catalog change, and the runtime's registry notification is the one signal that reports it in the same task. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `constructor` | `ThemvoraRuntimeConsumer` | — | | `accessKey` | `string` | The **`HTMLElement.accessKey`** property sets the keystroke which a user can press to jump to a given element. text: class ThemvoraScope **Extends** `ThemvoraRuntimeConsumer` Custom element `<themvora-scope>` that applies a scoped theme to its subtree. Framework-free (vanilla JS). Applies the theme named by the `theme` attribute as CSS variables on the element, overriding the provider's selection for the subtree. Omit to disable the scope. An unavailable value falls back to the catalog's first theme and is reported (`TV_CONFIG_OPTION_INVALID`). - `theme-transition` — `true`, `false`, or JSON (`'{"duration":300,"easing":"ease"}'`). Omitted → inherits the provider's transition. Malformed JSON is reported and ignored. **Properties.** None of its own beyond the standard `HTMLElement` surface. **Events.** Dispatches nothing of its own. **Slots.** Its children are ordinary light-DOM content and inherit the scoped variables. **One implementation of the variables.** The element delegates entirely to the canonical `createScopedThemeBinding`, which owns the variable set, the `--color-*` / `--radius-*` aliases, the `data-theme` / `data-mode` / `.dark` attributes, the transition animation, and the cleanup of variables that are no longer part of the new theme. Nothing about the token model is re-implemented here. **Isolation.** The variables are written inline on this element only, so a nested scope overrides its ancestor and never the reverse, and siblings are untouched. **Fallbacks.** `theme` accepts a theme name (`plum-dark`) or a family name (`plum`, resolved to that family's theme for the current mode). An unavailable value is reported and falls back to the catalog's first theme — the same rule the framework `ThemeScope` components use and the documented contract. Removing the attribute is different: the binding is destroyed, so the subtree inherits the surrounding theme and no stale variables survive. **Re-resolution.** The element re-applies when `theme` changes, when the provider's catalog changes (`themes-change`), and when a provider creates a new runtime (`theme-ready`), so a scope never holds a theme that the provider no longer knows about. Requires an ancestor `<themvora-provider>`. ```ts <themvora-provider default-theme="light"> <themvora-scope theme="plum-dark">...</themvora-scope> </themvora-provider> ``` ---

title: class ThemvoraScrollbar
text: class ThemvoraScrollbar **Extends** `ThemvoraRuntimeConsumer` Phase 2 — ThemvoraScrollbar (Web Component): overlay only. Creates the custom scrollbar overlay. Lifecycle: connectedCallback → resolve the runtime ↓ onRuntime → hide native bar (Phase 1) → create overlay → attach ↓ (Phase 2) later → add tv-scrollbar-ready ↓ (Phase 3) onDetach / destroy → remove overlay → restore native bar Phase 1 happens synchronously inside the overlay's construction. For static HTML served via the Vite plugin (scrollbar: true), the pre-paint script in <head> runs before first paint; for an SSR'd provider the class and CSS are in the markup. This component's own hiding is the fallback for dynamically-inserted elements (which may have already painted). The teardown is a real teardown. The hiding is claimed, not switched on, so removing the element gives the native scrollbar back instead of leaving the page with no scrollbar at all — and an attribute change swaps the overlay without ever passing through the "hidden, but nothing drawn" state. **See also:** `ThemvoraProvider` | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `constructor` | `ThemvoraScrollbar` | — | | `accessKey` | `string` | The **`HTMLElement.accessKey`** property sets the keystroke which a user can press to jump to a given element. Booleans are presence-based: present (any value except `false` or `0`) enables, absent or `false` disables. Numbers are unitless pixels. - Behaviour — `auto-hide`, `auto-hide-delay`, `hover-expand`, `draggable`, `click-to-jump`, `smooth`, `overscroll`, `touch`. - Arrows — `arrows`, `arrow-icon`, `arrow-up-icon`, `arrow-down-icon`, `arrow-left-icon`, `arrow-right-icon` (SVG markup or URL). - Geometry — `thickness`, `hover-thickness`, `radius`, `min-thumb-size`, `icon-size`, `offset` (uniform inset), `offset-top`, `offset-right`, `offset-bottom`, `offset-left` (per-side insets win over `offset`). - Motion and paint — `track-opacity`, `thumb-opacity`, `duration`, `animation-duration`, `thumb-color`, `track-color`, `active-thumb-color`, `thumb-hover-color`. Colors default to the active theme's tokens. - Placement — `z-index`, `dir` (`ltr` / `rtl` / `auto`), `axes` (comma-separated `vertical` / `horizontal`), `include` / `exclude` (comma-separated CSS selectors for the containers to track). **Properties.** None of its own beyond the standard `HTMLElement` surface. **Events.** Dispatches nothing of its own; it adds `tv-scrollbar-ready` to the element once the overlay is measured and attached. **Slots.** None — the element renders nothing into the document flow; the overlay it creates lives outside it. ---

title: class ThemvoraSelect
text: class ThemvoraSelect **Extends** `ThemvoraRuntimeConsumer` Custom element `<themvora-select>` that renders a `<select>` for choosing the theme mode or family. Framework-free (vanilla JS). `togglePopover` | `boolean` | — | | `webkitMatchesSelector` | `boolean` | — | | `define` | `void` | — | **Attributes.** - `type` — `"mode"` (default) or `"family"`. Anything else is reported and treated as `"mode"`. - `label` — accessible name for the inner `<select>` (sets `aria-label`). Omitted → `"Theme mode"` / `"Theme family"`, chosen by `type`. **Properties.** None of its own; the inner `<select>` is reachable as `el.querySelector("select")` for a consumer that needs it. **Events.** Dispatches nothing of its own. A change calls `runtime.selection.setMode()` / `setFamily()`, which the rest of the page observes through the runtime (`store`, `selection`, `registry`) or the provider's `themes-change`. **Slots.** None — the element owns its content. **Options come from the runtime.** The family list is derived from `runtime.themes` on every store tick and every `themes-change` event, so a theme removed from the catalog cannot linger as a stale option and a newly registered one appears without a reload. The element keeps no family list of its own. **Accessibility.** The inner `<select>` is native — keyboard behaviour, type-ahead and platform rendering are the browser's. Its accessible name is the `label` attribute when supplied, otherwise `"Theme mode"` / `"Theme family"`. **Cleanup.** Subscriptions are released on disconnection and re-established on reconnection; the rendered `<select>` is reused rather than recreated, so re-mounting cannot double the change listener. Requires an ancestor `<themvora-provider>`. ```ts <themvora-provider default-theme="light"> <themvora-select type="mode"></themvora-select> <themvora-select type="family" label="Theme family"></themvora-select> </themvora-provider> ``` ---

`void` | — | **Attributes.** None are observed: the control is driven entirely by the runtime. Its state is exposed for consumer styling as `data-mode` on the element (`light` / `dark` / `system`) and `aria-pressed` on the inner button (`true` / `false` / `mixed`). **Properties.** None of its own beyond the standard `HTMLElement` surface. **Events.** Dispatches nothing of its own; a click calls `runtime.selection.toggleTheme()`. **Slots.** None — the element owns the button and its icon. **State.** The element reflects the *selection*, and shows three states: the sun while the mode is explicitly `light`, the moon while it is explicitly `dark`, and a monitor while the selection is `system` — so a visitor who picked "System" in `<themvora-select>` can see that the control is following the operating system rather than pinned. `data-mode` reports the same value (`light` / `dark` / `system`). Activating the toggle always pins an explicit mode through `runtime.selection.toggleTheme()`, which resolves the *applied* appearance first — so a `system` selection flips to the opposite of what is on screen. **Accessibility.** The inner button is a real `<button>`, so focus, Enter and Space behave natively — the element itself is not a tab stop and carries no `role`. Its accessible name is the stable `"Dark mode"`; `aria-pressed` carries the state, and is `"mixed"` while the selection is `system` (neither on nor off, by design). Icon, name and state therefore always agree. **Reactivity.** The element subscribes to both the selection (mode changes from another control or the runtime API) and the store (an OS appearance change while the selection is `system`). Subscriptions are released on disconnection and re-established on reconnection, so re-mounting never doubles them. Requires an ancestor `<themvora-provider>`. ```ts <themvora-provider default-theme="light"> <themvora-toggle></themvora-toggle> </themvora-provider> ``` ---

text: ThemvoraProviderProps<T extends ThemeDefinition> Configuration for the `<themvora-provider>` custom element, parsed from its attributes. | Member | Type | Description | | ------ | ---- | ----------- | | `defaultTheme` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | The default theme. Parsed from the `default-theme` attribute. Accepts a supplied theme **name** (`"cocoa-light"`) or a **family** (`"cocoa"`); a family resolves to the variant for the mode in effect. | | `initialFamily` (optional) | `ThemeIdentifier<T>` | Family used when no selection is persisted. Parsed from the `initial-family` attribute. Pair it with `initialMode` for the same reason. A variant name is accepted and normalised to its family. | | `initialMode` (optional) | `ThemeMode` | Mode used when no selection is persisted. Parsed from the `initial-mode` attribute (`"light" \| "dark" \| "system"`). Optional: both the runtime and the pre-paint script derive the same fallback mode from `default-theme` by default. Set it only to pin a mode the script would not derive — e.g. `"system"` to follow `prefers-color-scheme` — and give `themvoraVitePlugin` the same `initialMode`. | | `scheduled` (optional) | `ThemeScheduleOptions<ThemeDefinition<string>>` | Sunrise/sunset scheduling options. Parsed from the `scheduled` attribute (JSON). | | `themes` (optional) | `readonly ThemeDefinition<string>[]` | Theme definitions, parsed from the `themes` attribute. The attribute accepts either syntax: - a space- or comma-separated list of **theme names** already registered in the canonical catalog — `themes="light dark plum-dark"`; - a JSON array of full theme definitions — `themes='[{"name":"brand",…}]'`. Names are resolved against the built-in catalog plus any theme already registered on the live runtime; an unknown name is reported and skipped. A list that resolves nothing is reported and the built-in set is used. | | `transition` (optional) | `boolean \| ThemeTransitionOptions` | Transition configuration.
