title: Feature map
text: Feature map **Server** - **ThemeProvider (Server Component)** — Reads `theme-mode`, `theme-family`, `theme-fingerprint` cookies, validates the fingerprint, resolves the initial theme, and renders `<html data-theme>` with inline CSS variables before hydration. - **Blocking bootstrap script** — Emits a blocking script in `<head>` that applies the persisted theme before first paint. - **Dark-mode CSS fallback** — Emits `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` styles when the persisted mode is `system`. - **scheduled prop** — Pass `scheduled={{ lightTheme, darkTheme }}` to the server ThemeProvider to enable sunrise/sunset switching app-wide. Coordinates are optional — each visitor's timezone is auto-detected on the client. **Client** - **@themvora/next/client** — The client entry point. Exports ClientThemeProvider, ThemeBootstrap, createNextThemePersistence, every React hook, and ThemeScope / ThemeInspector / ThemeModeButton. - **ClientThemeProvider** — Runtime for client components that need theme state. Mounts the runtime, syncs the `.dark` class, and persists the selection. - **ThemeBootstrap** — Injects the SSR dark-mode CSS via `useServerInsertedHTML`. - **createNextThemePersistence()** — Builds the adapter `ClientThemeProvider` uses: localStorage plus the `theme-mode`, `theme-family` and `theme-fingerprint` cookies the server reads on the next request. - **useThemeSchedule()** — Reactive sunrise/sunset controller: `enabled`, `active`, `status`, `sunrise`, `sunset`, `nextTransition` plus `enable()`/`disable()`/`set()`. - **useProvidedThemes()** — The families the server provider was given, as a client component sees them. Pair it with `useThemeFamily()` for the current selection and `useSetThemeFamily()` to change it — select by `entry.family`, not `entry.name`, because the name is only the display label. **Transition** - **transition prop** — Built-in runtime transition support. Configure duration/easing once on the provider; Themvora generates the transition styles at runtime, so applications do not need to maintain theme-transition rules in global CSS. - **runtime.store.set(theme, { suppressTransition: true })** — Per-update escape hatch from `@themvora/next/client`: call `runtime.store.set(theme, { suppressTransition: true })` when a switch must be instantaneous. **Scrollbar** - **scrollbar prop** — Enables Themvora's custom overlay scrollbar. The SSR bootstrap hides the native scrollbar before first paint, then the overlay engine synchronizes with browser scrolling without replacing native scroll behavior. - **scrollbar option** — Configure the overlay appearance from semantic tokens, including an explicit color token when needed. The overlay remains theme-aware and updates with runtime theme changes.

title: Notes
text: Notes - **Zero-flash:** Included. `ThemeProvider` resolves the first paint on the server and renders the pre-paint script into `<head>` itself. There is no bundler plugin to add. - **Starting mode:** The server resolves the mode from the persisted cookies, so a first-time visitor starts on `defaultTheme`. Once they pick System, that choice is stored and reused on every later request. - **Configuration:** Themes and the starting mode come from the provider in `app/layout.tsx`. title: Notes
text: Notes - **Zero-flash:** Automatic during SSR. `provideTheme()` emits the critical CSS and blocking bootstrap into the rendered `<head>` before the bundle loads. `createBlockingScriptContent()` remains available when you need custom server placement. - **Starting mode:** `provideTheme({ defaultTheme, initialMode })` chooses the starting theme. `initialMode: "system"` follows the visitor's OS. - **Configuration:** Themes and the starting mode are passed to `provideTheme()` when the app bootstraps. Angular does not use Vite, so there is no bundler plugin to add: the provider emits the pre-paint script. The stylesheet lives in `src/styles.css`, which the Angular CLI already registers in `angular.json`.

title: Web Components (@themvora/web)
text: Web Components (@themvora/web) HTML-first theming for any page: import the package once, then write custom elements and CSS variables. **Tags:** No framework · Custom elements · HTML-first

title: Feature map
text: Feature map **Setup** - **import "@themvora/web"** — One side-effect import registers `<themvora-provider>`, `<themvora-scope>`, `<themvora-toggle>`, `<themvora-select>`, `<themvora-scrollbar>` and `<themvora-inspector>`, and injects their stylesheet once. No manual registration step. - **defineCustomElements()** — The explicit form, kept for advanced cases: call it yourself, or register a single element under your own tag with `ThemvoraProvider.define("my-provider")`. Idempotent, and a no-op on the server. - **themvoraVitePlugin()** — Zero flash on Vite, with no `<script>` tag of your own. Add the plugin from `@themvora/core/vite` to `vite.config.ts`, declare the catalog once in `theme.config.ts`, and the blocking pre-paint script is injected into the served HTML. The provider adopts what that script painted. Pass `scrollbar: true` as well when the page uses `<themvora-scrollbar>` — the same pre-paint pass then hides the native bar. Keep `theme.config.ts` and the `themes` attribute listing the same catalog. - **VS Code IntelliSense** — The package ships `html-data.json`, an HTML custom-data file covering every element and attribute. Point VS Code at it with `"html.customData": ["./node_modules/@themvora/web/html-data.json"]` for tag completion, attribute suggestions and hover documentation. VS Code does not load it automatically. **Configuration** - **themes** — Two syntaxes. Names: `themes="light dark plum-dark"` resolves each identifier against the registered catalog. Definitions: `themes='[{"name":"brand","tokens":{…}}]'` registers your own. An unknown name is reported and skipped; nothing is constructed from a bare name. - **default-theme** — The theme used when nothing is persisted. Changing it re-resolves the selection; removing it does not disturb the live selection. - **initial-mode** — `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"` (case-insensitive). Any other value is reported and ignored, and the mode falls back to the one derived from `default-theme`. - **initial-family** — The family used when nothing is persisted. An unregistered family is reported by the runtime (`TV_THEME_FAMILY_UNKNOWN`) and normalised. - **transition** — JSON: `true`, `false`, or `{"enabled":true,"duration":250,"easing":"ease-in-out"}`. Changing it reconfigures the live bindings; removing it returns to no configured transition. - **scheduled** — JSON sunrise/sunset options, e.g. `{"latitude":27.7,"longitude":85.3}`. Removing the attribute tears the schedule down. **Elements** - **<themvora-provider>** — Owns the runtime for a page or subtree and applies the active theme to the document. Reacts to every configuration attribute without a reload. - **<themvora-scope>** — Applies a theme to its subtree via the `theme` attribute, in the light DOM. Accepts an exact theme name or a family name — a family follows the provider's mode, an exact name pins its own. Re-resolves when the provider's catalog changes, and falls back to the catalog's first theme (reported) when the name is unknown. Removing the attribute destroys the binding, so the subtree inherits the surrounding theme. - **<themvora-toggle>** — A native button with built-in sun, moon and monitor icons. It reports three states, not two: `data-mode` is `light`, `dark` or `system`, and `aria-pressed` is `true`, `false` or `mixed` — so a page following the OS reads as `system` rather than pretending to be light or dark. Activating it pins an explicit mode. No icon package, stylesheet or script required. - **<themvora-select>** — A native `<select>` for `type="mode"` or `type="family"`. Options come from the runtime, so a catalog change updates them; `label` sets the accessible name. - **<themvora-scrollbar>** — Overlay scrollbar bound to the provider runtime. Every option is an attribute; changing one rebuilds the overlay. It needs the pre-paint class: pass `scrollbar: true` to `themvoraVitePlugin()`, or load the pre-paint script yourself. Without it the browser paints a native scrollbar for a frame before the overlay mounts. - **<themvora-inspector>** — Floating theme inspector: identity, selection, tokens and resolved CSS variables, live. **Events** - **theme-ready** — Dispatched once by `<themvora-provider>` after its runtime exists and the first theme is applied. Bubbles and is composed, so a `document` listener sees it. - **themes-change** — Dispatched when the runtime's catalog changed — a `themes` attribute, `runtime.use(pack)` or `runtime.restore()` — with `detail.themes` naming the new catalog. A catalog change can leave the active theme untouched, so `store.subscribe()` alone cannot report it. Dispatched on a microtask, after the change has been applied, so a listener may safely write back to `themes`. - **runtime.store.subscribe()** — The canonical subscription for the active theme. Re-read state inside the callback; the runtime's helpers are getters, not subscriptions. - **runtime.selection.subscribe()** — Fires for a selection change that resolves to the same theme (`system` following the OS, for example), which the store subscription does not report. **Imperative** - **getProviderRuntime(providerEl)** — The runtime attached to a specific provider. Returns `undefined` before that element has upgraded — use it whenever more than one provider exists. - **useThemeRuntime()** — Page-level convenience: the runtime of the first initialized provider in document order. Throws when none has initialized. - **Mode and family control** — From the runtime: `selection.setMode("dark")`, `setFamily("plum")` and `toggleTheme()`. The built-in controls call exactly these, so a custom control needs no other API. - **useEffectiveThemeMode() / observeEffectiveThemeMode()** — The mode actually applied (`light` or `dark`) and a subscription to it. Render this in a label that states the current appearance: `useThemeMode()` reports the configured mode, which does not move at a sunrise/sunset transition.

title: Notes
text: Notes - **Zero-flash:** Two ways, one outcome. On Vite, `themvoraVitePlugin()` from `@themvora/core/vite` injects the blocking pre-paint script for you: declare the catalog once in `theme.config.ts` and add the plugin to `vite.config.ts` — no `<script>` tag, no build step of your own. Everywhere else, generate the script with `createThemeBootstrapScript()` and load it in `<head>` before the module script (see More Examples). Either way the provider adopts the selection the script painted instead of replacing it with a different default. Loading the package from a CDN with no pre-paint script has no zero-flash guarantee. - **Starting mode:** `default-theme` chooses the starting theme and `initial-mode="system"` follows the visitor's OS instead of the theme's own mode. Give the pre-paint script the same `defaultTheme` and `initialMode`, or the script and the runtime resolve different themes and the page flashes. - **Configuration:** Every provider option is an attribute, and every attribute is live: changing one reconciles the running runtime, so controls, scopes, variables and displayed text update without a reload. `themes` accepts either a list of registered names (`themes="light dark plum-dark"`) or a JSON array of theme definitions. Removing `themes`, `default-theme`, `initial-mode` or `initial-family` stops that attribute contributing without resetting the live selection; `transition` and `scheduled` are the exception, where removing the attribute turns the feature off. Invalid values are reported once through the standard diagnostic pipeline and ignored, never thrown.

title: Tailwind CSS v4 (@themvora/tailwind)

text: Feature map **Integration** - **@import "@themvora/tailwind"** — One import maps tokens to `@theme` variables: `--color-*`, `--radius-*`, `--spacing-*`, `--font-*`, `--shadow-*`. - **Dark-mode variant** — `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *))` — scoped to the `.dark` class Themvora maintains. - **synchronizeDarkClass(theme)** — Keeps the `.dark` class in sync with the active theme. - **CSS layers** — Ships `theme.css`, `dark.css` and `preflight.css` layers. **Transition** - **CSS transition variables** — Themvora exposes transition variables for Tailwind-aware styling, while the runtime owns the actual theme-change orchestration; you do not need to hand-author a global transition block just to get smooth theme changes. - **createTailwindPlugin({ themes, defaultTheme })** — Registers Themvora tokens with Tailwind from a JS config, for projects that configure Tailwind in JavaScript rather than CSS. - **themeCSS** — Tailwind-compatible `@theme` variable block generated from your Themvora tokens, imported via the package's CSS entry.

title: Notes
text: Notes - **Zero-flash:** Tailwind is build-time only — it maps tokens to utilities and never runs. Zero-flash comes from whichever Themvora runtime you mount (`@themvora/react`, `-vue`, `-svelte`, `-solid`, `-angular` or `-web`); Tailwind does not choose one for you. - **Starting mode:** Tailwind maps tokens to utilities — it has no runtime of its own, so the starting mode comes from the adapter you install alongside it. - **Configuration:** This CSS import is the whole Tailwind integration — Tailwind maps tokens to utilities at build time and never runs in the browser. Switching themes needs a Themvora runtime, a separate package of your choosing.

title: Astro (@themvora/astro)
text: Astro (@themvora/astro) Astro-native theming: an integration for the pre-paint bootstrap, a React-free <html> layout, a native <ThemeToggle />, and opt-in client islands. **Tags:** Integration · Components · Islands · Zero-flash

title: Feature map
text: Feature map **Astro integration** - **theme.config.ts discovery** — `themvora()` finds `theme.config.ts` at the project root and derives everything from it — the pre-paint bootstrap and the runtime's configuration. Nothing is repeated in `astro.config.mjs`. - **Configuration transport** — Injects the bootstrap projection as `window.__THEMVORA_CONFIG__` from `<head>`. The island reads it instead of taking theme props, so its server-rendered and hydrated markup come from the same registry. - **themvora() in astro.config.mjs** — Registers the integration and injects the pre-paint bootstrap into every page's <head> with `injectScript("head-inline")`. - **Zero-flash bootstrap** — Reads the persisted cookies, resolves the effective mode against `prefers-color-scheme`, and applies the CSS variables plus `data-theme` before first paint. - **navigation: true (default)** — Keeps the resolved theme across `<ClientRouter />` navigations — Astro otherwise copies each incoming page's `<html>` attributes over the live root. Inert without `<ClientRouter />`. - **No client framework required** — `@themvora/astro` imports no React — the integration, the server helpers, the `<ThemeToggle />` component and the browser runtime are all framework-neutral. React is an optional peer, pulled in only by an island. **Astro components (no React)** - **provider.astro** — Server-renders the themed `<html data-theme>` from the request cookies. A concrete mode inlines that theme's variables; `system` emits both schemes as media blocks instead, since an inline variable would outrank the dark block. - **ThemeToggle.astro** — A native Astro toggle: a real `<button>`, so keyboard and focus behaviour come from the platform. No island, no `client:load`, and no per-page `initialMode` / `initialFamily`. `showMode` makes its text the live mode. - **ThemeFamilySelect.astro** — A native `<select>` over the families in the registry. It renders from `theme.config.ts`, forwards `class` to the `<select>` itself, and needs no script of its own. A mode select is the same contract by hand: `<select data-tv-select="mode">`. - **data-tv-select** — The selection-control contract. A `change` event is delegated from `document`, and the live selection is written back into the element's `value` — so every control of a kind agrees, a restored selection is shown rather than the first option, and a control swapped in by navigation works without re-running a script. The pre-paint bootstrap writes it too, so a `<select>` never shows its first option on a page painted in another theme. - **ThemeScope.astro** — A subtree painted with a theme of its own, resolved in the frontmatter — so the server markup already carries the scoped variables and nothing repaints. Independent of the app-wide selection, and it ships no client JavaScript unless a runtime already exists. - **ThemeScrollbar.astro** — The overlay scrollbar as a native component — no island, no client framework. Pair it with `scrollbar` on `provider.astro` (or `themvora({ scrollbar })`), which is what puts the hiding class and CSS in the server-rendered HTML so the native bar is never painted. The component installs the app-wide runtime itself when the page has none, so the overlay is live on the first load instead of waiting for a theme change. - **getThemeController()** — The framework-neutral browser API, from `@themvora/astro/runtime`. Not a hook: a plain object with `getMode()`, `setMode()`, `setFamily()`, `toggleTheme()` and `subscribe()`, valid in any `<script>`. Idempotent — one runtime per document, shared with every other consumer. - **installThemeBindings()** — Registers the delegated `click` / `change` listeners for `[data-tv-toggle]` and `[data-tv-select]` once per document, and mirrors the live selection into `[data-tv-select]` and `[data-tv-pressed]` on every change. The Themvora components call it for you; call it yourself when the markup is hand-written. - **data-tv-readout** — Marks an element whose text Themvora owns. `theme` (the machine name), `label` (the theme's `meta.label`), `mode`, `family`, or `var:--theme-color-primary`. The pre-paint bootstrap patches it from `<head>`, before the body is parsed, and the controller keeps it in sync afterwards — so a server-rendered label is never painted and then corrected. - **data-tv-pressed** — Marks an element as one option of a segmented control: `data-tv-pressed="mode"` or `"family"`, with `data-tv-value` naming the option it represents. Themvora owns its `aria-pressed` — written before the first paint and kept live afterwards — so a server-rendered control never asserts a selection the page is not showing. Only `aria-pressed` is written, which is what lets a token class keyed off it (`aria-pressed:bg-primary`) keep the visual and accessible states in step. - **getInitialThemeState()** — Resolves the initial state from `Astro.request` so a client island hydrates against exactly what the document rendered. Needs the registry (`config` or `themes`) and a request, so it belongs on a server-rendered page. - **createAstroThemePersistence() / computeFingerprint()** — Cookie + localStorage persistence adapter, plus config fingerprinting to reject stale cookies. **Scoped themes** - **ThemeScope.astro** — Wrap any subtree and give it its own theme: `<ThemeScope theme="cocoa-dark">`. The variables are resolved during render, so the scoped panel is correct in the first paint — an implementation that applied them from a `<script>` would paint the page theme first and repaint, which is a visible flash on every load. - **Props** — `theme` (required), `themes` (only outside a provider), `as` (wrapper element, default `div`), `class`, `id`, `transition`. `class` merges with the `dark` marker the component adds for a dark theme, so Tailwind's `dark:` variants work inside the scope on the first paint. - **Independent of the selection** — A scope does not read or change the app-wide selection. A page can show a cocoa panel next to a mint page, and switching the page theme leaves the panel alone. - **No client JavaScript by default** — A scope is static markup. The component's script only refreshes an existing runtime's scopes when the registry is reconfigured, and honours `transition` — it never creates a runtime, so a page that only displays a scoped panel stays a page with no client framework on it. - **Any number per page** — Scopes are matched by the `data-tv-scope` attribute, not by an id, so the same component can be rendered as many times as the page needs. **Client islands (opt-in)** - **@themvora/astro/client** — The only entry that depends on React. Exports the `ThemeProviderClient` island, the `useTheme*` hooks, the React `ThemeScope`, and `ThemeReadout`. - **No theme props needed** — The registry, default theme and initial mode/family come from the transported `theme.config.ts`. Restating `initialMode` / `initialFamily` is a second source of truth: when it drifts from the config, the island's server markup disagrees with its hydrated markup (React error #418) and the text fluctuates on every load. - **client:load, not client:only** — Astro server-renders the island and hydrates it in place, so the panel is in the first paint and hydration only attaches handlers. `client:only` renders nothing on the server, which is the flash the integration exists to prevent. - **One island, not several** — Astro hydrates islands in an unspecified order, so two separate islands would race. Write one island whose tree contains both the provider and its consumers — `ThemeProviderClient` renders nothing itself; it is the provider half of that tree. - **One runtime, shared** — `ThemeProviderClient` adopts a runtime that already exists — one a `<ThemeToggle />` or `getThemeController()` script created — instead of making a second one, and leaves its destruction to the owner. Islands and native controls can share a page. - **Framework renderers stay optional** — React is an optional peer dependency. Astro-only projects never install it — choosing a React island is what pulls it in. - **Adding the renderer** — Opting in is one explicit step: install `@astrojs/react` and `react`, then add `react()` next to `themvora()` in `astro.config.mjs`. The Astro + React path shows that config; the Astro-only path never registers a renderer. - **Client bundle cost** — `<ThemeToggle />` and `getThemeController()` pull in the theme runtime — persistence, cross-tab sync and the DOM contract all come from `@themvora/core` rather than a second implementation. A page that only needs the *themed* document, with no interactive control, ships no client JavaScript at all: `provider.astro` and the inline bootstrap do that work on the server. **Transition** - **transition in theme.config.ts** — Declare `transition` once in `theme.config.ts` — `{ enabled, duration, easing, useViewTransition }`, or `true` / `false`. The runtime is built from the transported config, so native controls, the overlay scrollbar and a React island all cross-fade without per-island props. The island provider still accepts `transition` as an override for that island. - **runtime.store.set(theme, { suppressTransition: true })** — Applies the theme immediately, without animating. Use it for a one-off instant switch. The configured `transition` is live: change it on the runtime and the next theme change uses the new options (no reload, no remount). Compose the core diff/plan/runner APIs for custom animation. **Scrolling** - **Zero-flash scroll restoration** — On a reload or cross-document back/forward, `<ClientRouter />` stores the position in `history.state` and restores it from its deferred module — which can run after the first paint. `@themvora/astro` restores that same Astro-managed position from an inline end-of-body script, so the first frame is already at the saved position. Native restoration is left alone, no sessionStorage key is involved, and there is nothing to enable. - **ThemeScrollbar keeps native scrolling** — The overlay draws rails over the page and never replaces `document.scrollingElement` or changes document height. Reload, back/forward and client-side navigation keep working with or without it. Pass `scrollbar` to the provider (or `themvora({ scrollbar })`) only to hide the native bar before first paint.

title: Notes
text: Notes - **Zero-flash:** Included. `themvora()` injects the pre-paint bootstrap and `provider.astro` server-renders the themed `<html>`, so the first paint is already correct. - **Starting mode:** `theme.config.ts` declares the starting theme and mode once, and both the integration and the provider read it. - **Configuration:** Declared in `theme.config.ts` at the project root. `themvora()` in `astro.config.mjs` discovers it and injects the pre-paint bootstrap, and `provider.astro` reads the same file — so nothing is repeated.

title: Nuxt 4 (@themvora/nuxt)
text: Nuxt 4 (@themvora/nuxt) Nuxt 4 module with server-rendered theming, cookie sync, auto-imported composables, and config-driven options. **Tags:** Module · SSR · Zero-flash · Auto-import

title: Feature map
text: Feature map **Server** - **SSR-first theme resolution** — Reads `theme-name`, `theme-mode`, `theme-family`, `theme-fingerprint` cookies, validates the fingerprint, resolves the initial theme, and renders `<html data-theme>` with inline CSS variables before hydration. - **Blocking bootstrap script** — Emits a blocking script in `<head>` that applies the persisted theme before first paint. - **Dark-mode CSS fallback** — Emits `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` styles when the persisted mode is `system`. - **Cookie + localStorage sync** — The client mirrors selection back to cookies so the server renders the right theme on the next request — same contract as `@themvora/next`. **Client** - **Runtime plugin** — A Nuxt plugin installs one app-wide runtime, provided to `useTheme()`, `useThemeRuntime()` and every auto-imported composable. - **Auto-imports** — Composables (`useTheme`, `useThemeMode`, `useThemeHistory`, …) and components (`ThemeScope`, `ThemeScrollbar`) are auto-imported — no manual imports. Outside the auto-import scope, import them from `@themvora/vue`; Nuxt's import protection rejects a module's entry point in app code. - **configKey: "themvora"** — Configure `themes`, `defaultTheme`, `initialMode`, `initialFamily`, `transition`, `scrollbar`, `storageKey` and `scheduled` in `nuxt.config.ts`. - **useThemeSchedule()** — Auto-imported composable exposing the sunrise/sunset schedule: reactive `state` (`enabled`, `status`, `sunrise`, `sunset`, `nextTransition`) plus `enable()`/`disable()`/`set()`. Configure via `scheduled` in the module config. - **useProvidedThemes()** — The auto-imported family catalogue, as a `ref` the template unwraps. Each entry is a family: select by `entry.family`, not `entry.name`, because the name is only the display label. **Transition** - **transition in nuxt.config.ts** — Configure `transition` in the `themvora` config object to enable CSS transitions on theme changes. Duration/easing are set once; Themvora generates the transition styles at runtime. - **runtime.store.set(theme, { suppressTransition: true })** — Per-update escape hatch: `runtime.store.set(theme, { suppressTransition: true })` skips the configured animation. For custom animation orchestration, compose the core diff/plan/runner APIs. **Scrollbar** - **scrollbar: true** — Enables Themvora's custom overlay scrollbar. The SSR bootstrap hides the native scrollbar before first paint, then the overlay engine synchronizes with browser scrolling without replacing native scroll behavior. - **scrollbar option** — Configure the overlay appearance (thickness, radius, colors, auto-hide, …) from the `themvora` config; the overlay stays theme-aware and updates with runtime theme changes.

title: Notes
text: Notes - **Zero-flash:** Included. The module emits the pre-paint bootstrap and server-renders the themed `<html>`. - **Starting mode:** `themvora.initialMode` in `nuxt.config.ts` decides the starting mode, and `themvora.defaultTheme` picks the theme. - **Configuration:** Declared in `nuxt.config.ts` under the `themvora` key. The module reads it and emits the pre-paint bootstrap, so nothing is repeated elsewhere.

title: Remix (@themvora/remix)
text: Remix (@themvora/remix) Resolve the theme in a loader, paint it before first paint, then hydrate a matching runtime. **Tags:** SSR · Loaders · Hydration

title: Feature map
text: Feature map **Server** - **createThemeDocument()** — Pass the registry, fallback theme, `mode` and the optional `transition` / `scrollbar` settings once. Returns `resolveInitial(request)` plus a `Document` component that renders the blocking head script, the matching `<html>` shell and the runtime provider from the same configuration. This is the preferred root setup. - **theming.resolveInitial()** — Reads the `theme-mode` / `theme-family` / `theme-fingerprint` cookies off the request and resolves them against the frozen configuration. Call it in the root loader; request state is never stored on the handle, so concurrent requests stay isolated. - **getInitialThemeState()** — The lower-level resolver behind `resolveInitial()`, imported from `@themvora/remix/server`. Reach for it only when you assemble the document yourself — the factory exists so the loader, script, shell and provider cannot drift apart. - **ThemeHead** — The lower-level head script: emits the blocking bootstrap so the page paints already themed, plus the `prefers-color-scheme` dark fallback for `system` mode. `<theming.Document>` renders it for you; use it directly only in a hand-written `<head>`. - **getThemeShellProps()** — The lower-level `<html>` shell: the attributes and CSS variables the blocking script writes, plus `suppressHydrationWarning` for the resolved mode the server cannot know. `<theming.Document>` spreads it for you — hand-copying seven attributes is what this prevents. - **SSR-first resolution** — Request → root loader → resolve initial state → HTML document → browser hydration. The server resolves the theme, so the first paint already matches the hydrated client. **Client** - **ThemeProvider** — Mounted by `Document` around the route tree with the loader-resolved state, and it mirrors the selection back to cookies on change. Mount the provider once, in `app/root.tsx`; nested routes inherit it through `<Outlet />`. - **createRemixThemePersistence()** — Builds the adapter the provider uses: localStorage plus the `theme-mode`, `theme-family` and `theme-fingerprint` cookies the loader reads on the next request. - **Full hook set + ThemeScope** — Every React hook plus scoped subtrees — re-exported from `@themvora/react`. - **Intentional React dependency** — Remix is a React framework, so `@themvora/remix` depends on `@themvora/core` + `@themvora/react` directly. No other framework or adapter package is pulled in. **Routing** - **Provider lives in the root** — `app/root.tsx` declares the document once; nested routes and layouts inherit the runtime through `<Outlet />`. - **Route-level scopes** — Wrap a route subtree in `ThemeScope` to pin it to a theme without changing the global selection. **Transition** - **transition option** — Pass `transition` to `createThemeDocument()` to animate theme changes — `true`, `false`, or `{ enabled, duration, easing, preset }`. The provider receives the same object, so the document and the runtime cannot disagree. - **runtime.store.set(theme, { suppressTransition: true })** — Per-update escape hatch: `runtime.store.set(theme, { suppressTransition: true })` skips the configured animation. For custom animation orchestration, compose the core diff/plan/runner APIs. **Scrollbar** - **scrollbar option** — The `scrollbar` option in `createThemeDocument()` adds `tv-scrollbar` to `<html>` and emits the pre-paint hiding stylesheet in `<head>`, so the native bar is never painted. Import `@themvora/core/scrollbar.css` yourself — a CSS import is a bundler concern. - **Import the pre-paint styles** — Both halves are required: the class without the stylesheet hides nothing, and the stylesheet without the class has no effect. `Document` renders the class; your global stylesheet supplies the import.

title: Notes
text: Notes - **Zero-flash:** Included: `createThemeDocument()` derives the pre-paint script, the `<html>` shell and the provider from one configuration, so the first byte already carries the resolved theme. The lower-level `ThemeHead` + `getThemeShellProps()` pair does the same thing when you assemble the document by hand. - **Starting mode:** The loader resolves the initial state from the request cookies, so the first paint already matches. `mode` in `createThemeDocument()` is the single value the pre-paint script and the runtime both read — there is no second copy to keep in step. - **Configuration:** Themes and the starting mode are declared once, in `createThemeDocument()`, and the loader, the script, the shell and the runtime all read that object. Remix renders its own document, so there is no bundler plugin to add.

title: React Router (@themvora/remix)
text: React Router (@themvora/remix) One configuration for the root loader, the blocking head script, the document shell and the runtime. **Tags:** SSR · Framework Mode · Hydration **Only if you haven't created the React Router project yet:** `react-router`, `@react-router/dev`, `@react-router/node`, `@react-router/serve`

title: Feature map
text: Feature map **Server** - **createThemeDocument()** — Pass the registry, default theme, mode and scrollbar option once. Returns `resolveInitial(request)` and the `Document` component, so the loader, script, shell and provider cannot disagree. - **theming.resolveInitial()** — Reads `theme-mode` / `theme-family` / `theme-fingerprint` from the request and resolves them against the same frozen configuration. Request state is never stored on the handle. - **SSR-first resolution** — Root loader → static configuration → resolved `initial` state → server-rendered document → hydration. The first byte already carries the correct theme. **Client** - **ThemeProvider** — Mounted by `Document` around the route tree, with the request-resolved state. Selection changes mirror back to the cookies the root loader reads. - **Full hook set + ThemeScope** — Every React hook plus scoped subtrees, re-exported from `@themvora/react` through this package. - **createRemixThemePersistence()** — The adapter behind the provider: localStorage plus the cookie contract the root loader reads. The name is historical; it is framework-neutral. **Routing** - **Root route owns the document** — The root `Layout` still renders `<html>`, `<head>` and `<body>`; `Document` only supplies the theme-owned parts. Ownership stays with React Router. - **Route-level scopes** — Wrap a route subtree in `ThemeScope` to pin it to a theme without changing the global selection. - **Error-boundary fallback** — `Layout` can render while the root loader is unavailable. Passing a missing `initial` falls back to the configuration's static resolution instead of throwing inside the boundary. **Scrollbar** - **scrollbar option** — The `scrollbar` option in `createThemeDocument()` adds `tv-scrollbar` to `<html>` and emits the pre-paint hiding stylesheet in `<head>`. - **Import the pre-paint styles** — Import `@themvora/core/scrollbar.css`; the class and the stylesheet are both required, and `Document` renders the class for you.

title: Notes
text: Notes - **Zero-flash:** The root loader resolves the request cookies and `Document` emits the blocking script in `<head>` before the runtime mounts. The shell renders the same attributes the script writes, so hydration matches. - **Starting mode:** The `mode` in `createThemeDocument()` is the only starting-mode input. The loader, the pre-paint script and the provider all read it from the same object — there is no second constant to keep in sync. - **Configuration:** The configuration lives in `app/root.tsx`: `createThemeDocument({ themes, defaultTheme, mode, scrollbar })`. React Router itself is configured in `app/routes.ts`, `vite.config.ts` and `react-router.config.ts`.

title: Guiding principles
text: Guiding principles The documentation website is built with Themvora itself. Every theme change on this site goes through Themvora's runtime. Every example in the docs runs against the real packages — nothing is mocked or simulated. When a feature lands, the documentation adopts it internally wherever that makes sense. Themvora powers Themvora.
